RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: core_assumptions_conclusion
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem core_assumptions_conclusion {k n₂ : ℕ} {L : LatticeCandidate} (h : RGFCoreAssumptions k n₂ L) : Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Joint sufficiency.** The conjunction of the eight assumptions forces the locked invariants `(k, dim, coord) = (5, 3, 6)`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: two_layer_minimal
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem two_layer_minimal {n₂ : ℕ} (h : EmergenceSupported n₂) : 2 ≤ n₂
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Lower bound — a single layer is insufficient.** A neutral mode and a contracting mode must live in *distinct* two-dimensional blocks, so emergence requires at least two modes `n₂ ≥ 2`. In particular `n₂ = 1` (a single coupled mode / a one-layer iteration) cannot carry both G2 and G3.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: single_mode_no_emergence
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem single_mode_no_emergence : ¬ EmergenceSupported 1
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: The single-mode case (`n₂ = 1`) provably fails to support emergence.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: two_modes_emergence
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem two_modes_emergence : EmergenceSupported 2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Two modes do support emergence.** An explicit two-mode critical spectrum (one neutral mode `ρ = 1`, one contracting mode `ρ = 1/2`) carries both G2 and G3.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: depth_two_caps_frequencies
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem depth_two_caps_frequencies (a b : ℝ) (S : Finset ℝ) (hS : ∀ ω ∈ S, 0 < ω ∧ ω ^ 4 - a * ω ^ 2 + b = 0) : S.card ≤ 2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Upper bound — no third layer.** The depth-2 recurrence makes the characteristic polynomial a biquadratic `ω⁴ − a ω² + b = 0` in the frequency, so the set of positive frequencies has at most two elements: a third independent frequency (a third layer) is excluded.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: layer_count_two_unique
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem layer_count_two_unique : ∃! n₂ : ℕ, EmergenceSupported n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Two layers, uniquely.** Among all mode counts that *support emergence* (lower bound, ≥ 2) and respect the depth-2 frequency cap (upper bound, ≤ 2), the value `n₂ = 2` is the unique survivor. This is the precise sense in which the iteration must be two-layer: not one (fails the lower bound), not three (fails the upper bound).

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: coupling_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem coupling_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ Odd k ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ 0 < L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`coupling` is necessary.** Dropping the dual-mode lower bound `n₂ ≥ 2` admits the single-mode model `k = 3` (here on a `(dim, coord) = (3, 4)` lattice), which satisfies the other seven assumptions but gives `k = 3 ≠ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: depth2_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem depth2_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ Odd k ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ 0 < L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`depth2` is necessary.** Dropping the depth-2 cap `n₂ ≤ 2` admits the over-constrained model `k = 7` (`n₂ = 3`, on a `(3, 8)` BCC-type lattice), satisfying the other seven assumptions but giving `k = 7 ≠ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: oddness_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem oddness_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ 0 < L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`oddk` (L3) is necessary.** Dropping oddness admits the even model `k = 6` (`n₂ = 2`, on a `(3, 7)` lattice), satisfying the other seven assumptions but giving `k = 6 ≠ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: repCount_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem repCount_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ Odd k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ 0 < L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`repCount` is necessary.** Dropping the dihedral representation bridge `n₂ = num2DIrreps k` lets `n₂ = 2` coexist with `k = 3` (on a `(3, 4)` lattice), satisfying the other seven assumptions but giving `k = 3 ≠ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: lock_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem lock_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ Odd k ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ 0 < L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`lock` (the G1/G3 symmetry→direction bridge) is necessary.** Dropping it breaks the link between the mode order and the lattice coordination: the `k = 5` model on the `(3, 8)` BCC-type lattice satisfies the other seven assumptions but has `coord = 8 ≠ 6`, so the locked cubic invariant fails.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: rotation_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem rotation_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ Odd k ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ 0 < L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`rot` (the rotation-vector criterion) is necessary.** Dropping it admits the 2D triangular lattice (`(dim, coord) = (2, 6)`, `forwardCount = 5`) at `k = 5`: it satisfies the other seven assumptions but has `dim = 2 ≠ 3`. This is exactly the dimension-degeneracy the rotation criterion removes.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: dimpos_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem dimpos_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ Odd k ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ L.invSym = true) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`dimpos` is necessary.** Dropping positivity admits the degenerate `dim = 0` model (`(0, 6)` lattice, `forwardCount = 5`) at `k = 5`: it satisfies the other seven assumptions (note `rotGen 0 = 0`) but has `dim = 0 ≠ 3`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: centralSymmetry_necessary
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem centralSymmetry_necessary : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), (2 ≤ n₂ ∧ n₂ ≤ 2 ∧ Odd k ∧ n₂ = num2DIrreps k ∧ forwardCount L = k ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim ∧ 0 < L.dim) ∧ ¬ Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`central` (G1 reversibility / central symmetry) is necessary.** Dropping it admits a non-centrally-symmetric `(3, 5)` lattice at `k = 5`: with no back-step direction to remove, `forwardCount = coord = 5 = k`, so it satisfies the other seven assumptions but has `coord = 5 ≠ 6`, breaking the cubic invariant.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: core_assumptions_satisfiable
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem core_assumptions_satisfiable : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), RGFCoreAssumptions k n₂ L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Satisfiability.** The eight assumptions are jointly satisfiable, witnessed by the 3D simple-cubic lattice at mode order `k = 5`, `n₂ = 2`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: rgf_invariants_unique
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem rgf_invariants_unique {k n₂ : ℕ} {L : LatticeCandidate} (h : RGFCoreAssumptions k n₂ L) : (k, L.dim, L.coord) = (5, 3, 6)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Uniqueness of the locked invariants.** Any model satisfying the eight assumptions has invariants exactly `(k, dim, coord) = (5, 3, 6)`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: cubic_unique_in_class
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem cubic_unique_in_class : ∀ L ∈ candidates, (forwardCount L = 5 ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim) ↔ L = simpleCubic
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Naturalness inside the candidate class.** Among the standard competing lattices (square, triangular, honeycomb, simple-cubic, BCC, FCC, 4D hypercubic), the simple-cubic lattice is the *unique* one passing both geometric criteria (`forwardCount = 5` and `rotGen dim = dim`).

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: coupling
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem coupling (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : 2 ≤ n₂
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`coupling` derived.** The dual-layer contractive dynamics force `2 ≤ n₂`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: depth2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem depth2 (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : n₂ ≤ 2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`depth2` derived.** The depth-2 / real antisymmetric biquadratic spectrum forces `n₂ ≤ 2`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: oddk
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem oddk (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : Odd k
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`oddk` derived.** The real antisymmetric linearization (`k = 2·n₂ + 1`) forces an odd mode order.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: repCount
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem repCount (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : n₂ = num2DIrreps k
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **`repCount` derived (bonus).** The chiral decomposition `k = 2·n₂ + 1` is consistent with the dihedral two-dimensional irrep count `n₂ = num2DIrreps k`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: conclusion
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem conclusion (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : Conclusion k L
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **The primitive derives the locked invariants.** From the single structural primitive, `(k, dim, coord) = (5, 3, 6)` — with no separate `coupling`, `depth2`, `oddk` assumptions.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: invariants_unique
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem invariants_unique (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : (k, L.dim, L.coord) = (5, 3, 6)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Uniqueness of the locked invariants from the primitive.**

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: antisymDualLayerCore_satisfiable
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem antisymDualLayerCore_satisfiable : ∃ (k n₂ : ℕ) (L : LatticeCandidate), Nonempty (AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **Satisfiability.** The primitive is non-vacuous: the 3D simple-cubic lattice at `k = 5`, `n₂ = 2`, with the two positive eigenfrequencies `{1, 2}` (the positive roots of the biquadratic `ω⁴ − 5 ω² + 4 = 0`) realizes it.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.name: antisym_core_upgrades_arithmetic
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.sig: theorem antisym_core_upgrades_arithmetic {k n₂ : ℕ} {L : LatticeCandidate} (C : AntisymDualLayerCore k n₂ L) : (2 ≤ n₂) ∧ (n₂ ≤ 2) ∧ Odd k ∧ (n₂ = num2DIrreps k)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionMini.doc: **The change of basis genuinely reduces the assumption count.** Whenever the primitive holds, the four formerly-free arithmetic inputs `coupling ∧ depth2 ∧ oddk ∧ repCount` are *all* theorems, so only the four geometric/dictionary inputs remain as free hypotheses.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.name: rgf_configuration_unique
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.sig: theorem rgf_configuration_unique : ∃! p : ℕ × ℕ × LatticeCandidate, RGFCoreAssumptions p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.doc: **Configuration uniqueness.** There is one and only one generative configuration `(k, n₂, L)` satisfying the eight RGF selection criteria, namely `(5, 2, simpleCubic)`. None of the eight criteria mentions the answer `(5, 3, 6)`; uniqueness is therefore a property of the *criteria*, not of the conclusion read back into them.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.name: least_layer_count
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.sig: theorem least_layer_count : IsLeast {n₂ : ℕ | EmergenceSupported n₂} 2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.doc: **Least layer count.** Among all mode counts that support emergence (carry a neutral G2 mode and a contracting G3 mode), `n₂ = 2` is the **least**. This is the precise sense in which two layers are the parsimonious minimum: one layer is provably insufficient.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.name: unique_odd_order
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.sig: theorem unique_odd_order : ∃! k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ num2DIrreps k = 2
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.doc: **Unique odd mode order.** `k = 5` is the unique odd mode order whose dihedral two-dimensional irrep count equals the two-mode value `n₂ = 2`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.name: unique_dimension
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.sig: theorem unique_dimension : ∃! d : ℕ, 0 < d ∧ rotGen d = d
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.doc: **Unique dimension.** `d = 3` is the unique positive spatial dimension in which the rotation generators are representable as vectors (`rotGen d = d`, i.e. `d(d−1)/2 = d`).

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.name: rgf_invariants_unique'
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.sig: theorem rgf_invariants_unique' {k n₂ : ℕ} {L : LatticeCandidate} (h : RGFCoreAssumptions k n₂ L) : (k, L.dim, L.coord) = (5, 3, 6)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.doc: **Invariant uniqueness (re-export).** Any model satisfying the eight criteria has invariants exactly `(k, dim, coord) = (5, 3, 6)`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.name: cubic_unique_in_class'
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.sig: theorem cubic_unique_in_class' : ∀ L ∈ candidates, (forwardCount L = 5 ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim) ↔ L = simpleCubic
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/AssumptionUniq.doc: **Candidate-class uniqueness (re-export).** Among the standard competing lattices, the simple-cubic lattice is the unique one passing both geometric criteria.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.name: omega_pow_five
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.doc: The eigenvalue selected by the system, `ω = e^{2πi/5}`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.name: omega_not_real
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.doc: The eigenvalue selected by the system, `ω = e^{2πi/5}`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.name: omega_conj_pair_distinct
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.sig: theorem omega_conj_pair_distinct : omega ^ 4 = (starRingEnd ℂ) omega ∧ (starRingEnd ℂ) omega ≠ omega
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.doc: The eigenvalue selected by the system, `ω = e^{2πi/5}`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.name: rotation_no_real_eigenvector
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.sig: theorem rotation_no_real_eigenvector (μ : ℝ) (v : Fin 2 → ℝ) (hv : v ≠ 0) : (RGF.L2L3Gaps.z5RotMatrix).mulVec v ≠ μ • v
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.doc: **`rotation_no_real_eigenvector`.** The two-dimensional real rotation matrix by angle `2π/5` has no eigenvector over the reals (discriminant `(cosθ−μ)²+sin²θ > 0`). This directly reuses `RGF.L2L3Gaps.z5Rot_no_real_eigenvector`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.name: complex_necessity_master
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.sig: theorem complex_necessity_master : (∀ x : ℝ, x ^ 5 = 1 → x = 1) ∧ (∀ (μ : ℝ) (v : Fin 2 → ℝ), v ≠ 0 → (RGF.L2L3Gaps.z5RotMatrix).mulVec v ≠ μ • v) ∧ (∃ ω : ℂ, ω ^ 5 = 1 ∧ ω.im ≠ 0 ∧ ω ^ 4 = (starRingEnd ℂ) ω ∧ (starRingEnd ℂ) ω ≠ ω)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/ComplexNecessi.doc: **`complex_necessity_master`.** A combined argument for the necessity of a complex base field: 1. over the reals, `x⁵ = 1` has only the trivial root, so there is no nontrivial one-dimensional real representation; 2. the two-dimensional real rotation matrix carrying the `Z₅` phase locking has no eigenvector over the reals; 3. after complexification the system selects a distinct pair of non-real conjugate fifth roots of unity `ω, conj ω` (`ω⁵ = 1`). Together these show that a system carrying the `Z₅`-locked phase cannot be built over the pure real field; a complex base field is necessary.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: toVec_injective
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: A nearest-neighbor direction `(i, b)` on the cubic lattice `ℤ^d`: `i` selects the coordinate axis, `b` selects the positive (`true`) / negative (`false`) orientation. Encoded as the integer vector `±e_i`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: revisitsPrevious_iff_rev
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem revisitsPrevious_iff_rev {d : ℕ} (s t : Fin d × Bool) : revisitsPrevious s t ↔ t = rev s
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: After taking one step along direction `s`, a candidate next direction `t` "returns to the previous lattice point" if and only if its displacement vector is opposite to that of `s`, i.e. `toVec t = - toVec s`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: excludedByG1_eq_singleton
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem excludedByG1_eq_singleton {d : ℕ} (s : Fin d × Bool) : excludedByG1 s = {rev s}
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: The set of candidate directions excluded by the G1-exclusivity rule (directions that return to the previous lattice point).

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: card_excludedByG1
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem card_excludedByG1 {d : ℕ} (s : Fin d × Bool) : (excludedByG1 s).card = 1
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: **`card_excludedByG1`.** Exactly one direction is excluded by G1.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: card_allowedForward
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem card_allowedForward {d : ℕ} (s : Fin d × Bool) : (allowedForward s).card = 2 * d - 1
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: The set of effective forward directions allowed after one step along direction `s`: from the `2d` nearest-neighbor directions, remove the unique return-step direction.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: card_allowedForward_eq_latticeForward
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem card_allowedForward_eq_latticeForward {d : ℕ} (s : Fin d × Bool) : (allowedForward s).card = FeasibilityLattice.latticeForward d
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: **`card_allowedForward_eq_latticeForward`.** The internal count agrees with `FeasibilityLattice.latticeForward d`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: dimension_three_from_G1_and_locking
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem dimension_three_from_G1_and_locking {d k : ℕ} (s : Fin d × Bool) (hbridge : (allowedForward s).card = k) (hk : k = 5) : d = 3
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: **`card_allowedForward_eq_latticeForward`.** The internal count agrees with `FeasibilityLattice.latticeForward d`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..name: g1_dimension_master
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..sig: theorem g1_dimension_master {d : ℕ} (s : Fin d × Bool) : (excludedByG1 s).card = 1 ∧ (allowedForward s).card = 2 * d - 1 ∧ ((allowedForward s).card = 5 → d = 3)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/G1Exclusivity..doc: **`g1_dimension_master`.** Synthesis of the G1 internal chain: exactly one direction is excluded, the number of effective forward directions `= 2d − 1`, and when this is compatible with the direction-star order at mode-locking order `k = 5` it yields `d = 3`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: pentagonLaplacian_sum_zero
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem pentagonLaplacian_sum_zero (v : IRMode) : ∑ x : ZMod 5, pentagonLaplacian v x = 0

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_const
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_const (c : ℝ) : genStep (fun _ => c) = fun _ => c

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_sum
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_sum (v : IRMode) : ∑ x : ZMod 5, genStep v x = ∑ x : ZMod 5, v x

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_linear_add
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_linear_add (u v : IRMode) : genStep (u + v) = genStep u + genStep v

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_linear_smul
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_linear_smul (c : ℝ) (u : IRMode) : genStep (c • u) = c • genStep u

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_sum_iterate
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_sum_iterate (w : IRMode) (n : ℕ) : ∑ x : ZMod 5, (genStep^[n] w) x = ∑ x : ZMod 5, w x
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: The mean is invariant under iteration.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: projKer_genStep
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem projKer_genStep (v : IRMode) : projKer (genStep v) = projKer v
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: The kernel projection is invariant under the generation iteration.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: projKer_iterate
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem projKer_iterate (v : IRMode) (n : ℕ) : projKer (genStep^[n] v) = projKer v
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: The kernel projection is invariant under iteration.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_sub_projKer
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_sub_projKer (v : IRMode) : genStep v - projKer v = genStep (v - projKer v)
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: The generation operator commutes with "subtracting the kernel projection" (L kills constants, so the transverse fluctuations decouple from the kernel).

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: sum_dev_zero
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem sum_dev_zero (v : IRMode) : ∑ x : ZMod 5, (v - projKer v) x = 0
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: A perturbation deviating from the kernel has zero mean.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: genStep_contraction
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem genStep_contraction (w : IRMode) (h : ∑ x : ZMod 5, w x = 0) : nrm2 (genStep w) ≤ (1/2) * nrm2 w
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: A perturbation deviating from the kernel has zero mean.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: nrm2_iterate_decay

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: Iterative decay (squared-norm version): the squared norm of a zero-mean perturbation decays exponentially as `(1/2)^n`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: iterate_dev

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: Iterative decay (squared-norm version): the squared norm of a zero-mean perturbation decays exponentially as `(1/2)^n`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: sqrt_pow_eq
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem sqrt_pow_eq (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (n : ℕ) : Real.sqrt (x ^ n) = (Real.sqrt x) ^ n

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: lock_stability
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem lock_stability (v : IRMode) : ∃ C ρ : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 ≤ ρ ∧ ρ < 1 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, l2norm (genStep^[n] v - projKer v) ≤ C * ρ ^ n
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: **Spectral stability theorem for mode-locking**: any perturbation deviating from the 5 eigenmodes (outside the kernel projection `projKer v`) decays exponentially under the generation iteration `M = genStep` — there exist a constant `C ≥ 0` and a contraction rate `0 ≤ ρ < 1` such that for all `n`, `‖ M^[n] v − projKer v ‖ ≤ C · ρ^n`.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem sigmaOp_involutive (u : IRMode) : sigmaOp (sigmaOp u) = u

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: sigmaOp_eq_pentagonRep

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: smode_eigen
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem smode_eigen (j : ℕ) : pentagonLaplacian (smode j) = (lam j) • smode j

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: cmode_sigma_fixed

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem smode_sigma_anti (j : ℕ) : sigmaOp (smode j) = -smode j

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: block_nondegeneracy
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..sig: theorem block_nondegeneracy (j : ℕ) : pentagonLaplacian (cmode j) = (lam j) • cmode j ∧ pentagonLaplacian (smode j) = (lam j) • smode j ∧ sigmaOp (cmode j) = cmode j ∧ sigmaOp (smode j) = -smode j
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: **Non-degeneracy within a 2-dimensional block (U)**: within the 2-dimensional eigenblock with `λ_j = λ_{5−j}`, the two σ-dual directions (the cosine `cmode j` and the sine `smode j`) share the eigenvalue `λ_j`, but σ sends them to `+` and `−` respectively: the cosine is the unique σ-fixed stable mode, while the sine is sign-flipped by σ. So the two are **not independent σ-fixed stable modes** — this yields locking non-degeneracy independently inside RGF.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..name: lock_attractor

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/LockStability..doc: **Attractor property of mode-locking (G3-type exponential recovery)**: any initial perturbation converges under the generation iteration to the mode-locked core spanned by the 5 eigenmodes (`projKer v`): the norm of the deviating part tends to 0. This is a concrete realization, on the generation dynamics, of `SpectrumReductionConjecture.RGFDynamicalAxioms.g3_holds` (asymptotic attraction), connecting with the dynamical axioms of the spectral-gap theorem.

RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/StabilityUniqu.name: stable_two_layer_locks_uniquely
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/StabilityUniqu.sig: theorem stable_two_layer_locks_uniquely (S : StableTwoLayer) : n₂ 5 = 2 ∧ Odd 5 ∧ StableGen 5 ∧ (∃! k, StableGen k) ∧ (∀ k, StableGen k → k = 5) ∧ Nat.card (DihedralGroup 5) = 10 ∧ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5))
RGF/Generative/Uniqueness/StabilityUniqu.doc: **Uniqueness / master locking theorem.** The existence of a stable two-layer locked structure forces the entire chain of dual-hierarchy locking constants: `n₂ = 2` (L2), the membrane dimension is odd (L3), `k = 5` is the unique stable-generation value, the dihedral group `D₅` has order `10` with exactly two two-dimensional irreducible representations, and the associated permutation symmetry `S₅` is non-solvable.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircleMapReductio.name: spiralPhase_range

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircleMapReductio.doc: At the critical density the coupling strength is exactly 1.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.name: bridge_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.sig: theorem bridge_iff {P Q : α → Prop} (h : DefinitionalBridge P Q) (a : α) : P a ↔ Q a
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.doc: A definitional bridge is, pointwise, the trivial biconditional (`Iff.rfl` when the equality itself is `rfl`). This is the general form of `RGFInvariant.emergence_criterion_is_definitional`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.name: definitional_bridge_no_independent_content
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.sig: theorem definitional_bridge_no_independent_content {P Q : α → Prop} (h : DefinitionalBridge P Q) : (∀ R : α → Prop, (∀ a, P a → R a) = (∀ a, Q a → R a)) ∧ (∀ a, P a ↔ Q a)
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.doc: **The core structural upper bound.** If `P` is a definitional bridge to `Q`, then for *every* conclusion predicate `R`, the statement "`P` forces `R`" is the *identical proposition* to "`Q` forces `R`". Consequently: * taking `R := Q`, "deriving the criterion `Q` from the premise `P`" is literally the same proposition as the trivial "`Q → Q`"; the bridge can never be an *independent* derivation of `Q`; * any necessity/uniqueness theorem proved "via `P`" is, verbatim, the theorem proved "via `Q`" — routing a result through the physical premise adds no deductive content. This delimits (does not close) the open problem: no closure that factors through a definitional bridge can succeed, so an honest closure must first replace the definitional identification by an *independent* definition of the physical premise.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.name: forward_derivation_is_trivial
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.sig: theorem forward_derivation_is_trivial {P Q : α → Prop} (h : DefinitionalBridge P Q) : (∀ a, P a → Q a) = (∀ a, Q a → Q a)
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.doc: Specialisation to `R := Q`: "the premise forces the criterion" is the same proposition as the trivial "the criterion forces itself". The starkest form of the upper bound.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.name: emergence_is_definitional_bridge
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.sig: theorem emergence_is_definitional_bridge : DefinitionalBridge EmergenceCondition (fun sys : RecursiveSystem => ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin sys.k)))
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.doc: The membrane-locking premise is a definitional bridge: `EmergenceCondition` equals, as a predicate, "`S_k` is non-solvable".

RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.name: emergence_bridge_no_independent_content
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.sig: theorem emergence_bridge_no_independent_content : (∀ R : RecursiveSystem → Prop, (∀ sys, EmergenceCondition sys → R sys) = (∀ sys, (¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin sys.k))) → R sys)) ∧ (∀ sys, EmergenceCondition sys ↔ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin sys.k)))
RGF/Generative/Locking/CircularityMetaTh.doc: **Instantiated upper bound.** Because the emergence premise is a definitional bridge, no theorem of the shape "emergence ⟹ `R`" carries content beyond "non-solvable ⟹ `R`"; in particular the "emergence ⟹ non-solvable" bridge is informationally empty. Hence the necessity of the *solvability criterion itself* cannot be established by this route — the residual open problem is genuine, not an artefact of a missing proof.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: commSys_step
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem commSys_step (H : Subgroup G) : (commSys G).step H = commGen H
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **Main bridge (pointwise).** The RGF main generation operator `step = modify ∘ generate` of `commSys` applied to a subgroup `H` is exactly the commutator generator `commGen H = ⁅H, H⁆`. This is where the RGF generation dynamics and the commutator recursion are *identified* — as a theorem, using `Subgroup.commutator_def`, not by fiat.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: commSys_step_eq
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **Main bridge (functional).** As maps on the subgroup lattice, the RGF main generation operator of `commSys` and the commutator generator coincide.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: commSys_step_eq_bilayer
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem commSys_step_eq_bilayer : (commSys G).step = RGF.Bilayer.step (genCommutators (G := G)) modifyClose
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: The RGF `step` of `commSys` is also literally the bilayer `step` `modify ∘ generate` (as defined in `BilayerDuality`), for the same two layers.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: commSys_iterate
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem commSys_iterate (n : ℕ) : (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ = derivedSeries G n
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **The derived series is the RGF orbit.** Iterating the RGF main generation operator `step` of `commSys` from the whole group `⊤` reproduces the derived series. Thus the derived series is *exactly* the trajectory of the RGF generation dynamics.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: commSys_isFixedPoint
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem commSys_isFixedPoint (H : Subgroup G) : (commSys G).IsFixedPoint H ↔ IsCommFixedPoint H
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **RGF fixed point = perfect subgroup.** A subgroup is a fixed point of the RGF main generation operator `commSys.step` iff it is a fixed point of `commGen` (i.e. a perfect subgroup).

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: stableLocking_iff_step
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem stableLocking_iff_step (G : Type*) [Group G] : StableLocking G ↔ ∃ n, (commSys G).step ((commSys G).step^[n] ⊤) = (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ∧ (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ≠ ⊥
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **The `commGen` locking criterion is a statement about the RGF `step` operator.** Stable locking holds iff iterating the RGF main generation operator from `⊤` reaches a *non-trivial* fixed point: some stage `H = step^[n] ⊤` is fixed by `step` and non-trivial.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: rgf_step_locking_iff_not_solvable
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem rgf_step_locking_iff_not_solvable (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : (∃ n, (commSys G).step ((commSys G).step^[n] ⊤) = (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ∧ (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ≠ ⊥) ↔ ¬ IsSolvable G
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **`StableLocking` (RGF-step form) ⟺ non-solvability.** Combining the bridge with `stableLocking_iff_not_solvable`: for a finite group, the RGF main generation operator reaching a non-trivial fixed point is equivalent to non-solvability.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: rgf_step_symmetric_iff_five_le
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem rgf_step_symmetric_iff_five_le (k : ℕ) : (∃ n, (commSys (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))).step ((commSys (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))).step^[n] ⊤) = (commSys (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))).step^[n] ⊤ ∧ (commSys (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))).step^[n] ⊤ ≠ ⊥) ↔ 5 ≤ k
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **Headline (symmetric group), via the RGF `step` operator.** The RGF main generation operator on the subgroup lattice of `S_k`, iterated from `⊤`, reaches a non-trivial fixed point iff `k ≥ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.name: commGen_step_master
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.sig: theorem commGen_step_master (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : ((commSys G).step = commGen) ∧ (∀ n, (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ = derivedSeries G n) ∧ (StableLocking G ↔ ∃ n, (commSys G).step ((commSys G).step^[n] ⊤) = (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ∧ (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ≠ ⊥) ∧ ((∃ n, (commSys G).step ((commSys G).step^[n] ⊤) = (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ∧ (commSys G).step^[n] ⊤ ≠ ⊥) ↔ ¬ IsSolvable G)
RGF/Generative/Locking/CommGenAsStep.lea.doc: **Summary.** In one statement: the RGF main generation operator `step` of `commSys` *is* the commutator generator `commGen`; iterating it from `⊤` *is* the derived series; and the resulting non-trivial-fixed-point (stable-locking) criterion is equivalent to non-solvability and, for `S_k`, to `k ≥ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.name: critical_ratio_eq_one
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.sig: theorem critical_ratio_eq_one (alpha beta L_c : ℝ) (hα : alpha > 0) (hβ : beta > 0) (hL : L_c > 0) (h_critical : L_c ^ 4 = alpha / beta) -- critical-scale condition L_c = (α/β)^{1/4} : criticalWindingMomentumRatio alpha beta L_c 3 = 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.doc: Definition of the critical winding-momentum ratio Γ_c. Corresponding to Definition 3.1 of Paper 13': Γ_c ≡ |m²_wind(L_c) / m²_mom(L_c)| = β·L_c^{d-1} / (α·L_c⁻²) For d = 3 this is β·L_c² / (α·L_c⁻²).

RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.name: critical_scale_balance
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.sig: theorem critical_scale_balance (alpha beta L_c : ℝ) (hα : alpha > 0) (hβ : beta > 0) (hL : L_c > 0) : (alpha * L_c⁻¹ ^ 2 = beta * L_c ^ 2) ↔ L_c ^ 4 = alpha / beta
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.doc: Definition of the critical winding-momentum ratio Γ_c. Corresponding to Definition 3.1 of Paper 13': Γ_c ≡ |m²_wind(L_c) / m²_mom(L_c)| = β·L_c^{d-1} / (α·L_c⁻²) For d = 3 this is β·L_c² / (α·L_c⁻²).

RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.name: critical_ratio_universal
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.sig: theorem critical_ratio_universal (alpha₁ alpha₂ beta₁ beta₂ L₁ L₂ : ℝ) (hα₁ : alpha₁ > 0) (hβ₁ : beta₁ > 0) (hL₁ : L₁ > 0) (hα₂ : alpha₂ > 0) (hβ₂ : beta₂ > 0) (hL₂ : L₂ > 0) (h₁ : L₁ ^ 4 = alpha₁ / beta₁) (h₂ : L₂ ^ 4 = alpha₂ / beta₂) : criticalWindingMomentumRatio alpha₁ beta₁ L₁ 3 = criticalWindingMomentumRatio alpha₂ beta₂ L₂ 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.doc: Definition of the critical winding-momentum ratio Γ_c. Corresponding to Definition 3.1 of Paper 13': Γ_c ≡ |m²_wind(L_c) / m²_mom(L_c)| = β·L_c^{d-1} / (α·L_c⁻²) For d = 3 this is β·L_c² / (α·L_c⁻²).

RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.name: extremal_condition_implies_balance
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.sig: theorem extremal_condition_implies_balance (alpha beta L_c : ℝ) (hα : alpha > 0) (hβ : beta > 0) (hL : L_c > 0) (h_extremal : -2 * alpha * L_c⁻¹ ^ 3 + 2 * beta * L_c = 0) : alpha * L_c⁻¹ ^ 2 = beta * L_c ^ 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/CriticalRatio.lea.doc: The correlation-length function (defined when λ₁ > 0). ξ(L) = 1/√(ξ⁻²(L))

RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.name: dim_three_unique
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.sig: theorem dim_three_unique (d : ℕ) : (d ≤ 3 ∧ Odd d ∧ d ≠ 1) ↔ d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.doc: Arithmetic characterisation of the spatial dimension: constraint I (`d ≤ 3`) together with constraint II (`d` odd and `d ≠ 1`) holds iff `d = 3`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.name: rcd_dim3_iff_rgf_crossProduct
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.sig: theorem rcd_dim3_iff_rgf_crossProduct (d : ℕ) : (d ≤ 3 ∧ Odd d ∧ d ≠ 1) ↔ CP d
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.doc: **Algebraic route.** RCD's three-constraint characterisation of the spatial dimension is *equivalent* to RGF's first-principles cross-product condition `CP d` (`d(d-1) = 2d`, the bivector ↔ vector self-duality).

RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.name: rcd_dim3_iff_rgf_lattice
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.sig: theorem rcd_dim3_iff_rgf_lattice (d : ℕ) : (d ≤ 3 ∧ Odd d ∧ d ≠ 1) ↔ latticeForward d = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.doc: **Combinatorial route.** RCD's three-constraint characterisation is equivalent to the RGF cubic-lattice forward-repulsion count being `5` (i.e. `2d - 1 = 5`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.name: rcd_dim3_iff_rgf_forsPole
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.sig: theorem rcd_dim3_iff_rgf_forsPole (d : ℕ) : (d ≤ 3 ∧ Odd d ∧ d ≠ 1) ↔ forsPoleOrder d 1 = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.doc: **Analytic route.** RCD's three-constraint characterisation is equivalent to the RGF FORS pole order (at recovery order `R = 1`) being `5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.name: rcd_dim3_multipath
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.sig: theorem rcd_dim3_multipath (d : ℕ) : (d ≤ 3 ∧ Odd d ∧ d ≠ 1) ↔ (CP d ∧ latticeForward d = 5 ∧ forsPoleOrder d 1 = 5)
RGF/Generative/Locking/Dimension.lean.doc: **Multi-path robustness (the upgrade).** RCD's spatial-dimension core is simultaneously equivalent to *all three* independent RGF criteria. Thus the RCD value `d = 3` is bracketed by an algebraic, a combinatorial and an analytic machine-verified route at once — none of which references the others.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..name: dimension_locking
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..sig: theorem dimension_locking (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) : gammaCritical d = 1 ↔ d = 3

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..name: dimension_locking_unique
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..sig: theorem dimension_locking_unique : ∃! (d : ℕ), 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ 100 ∧ gammaCritical d = 1

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..name: d3_extremal_gives_Lc4
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..sig: theorem d3_extremal_gives_Lc4 (alpha beta L_c : ℝ) (hα : 0 < alpha) (hβ : 0 < beta) (hL : 0 < L_c) (h_balance : alpha * L_c⁻¹ ^ 2 = beta * L_c ^ 2) : L_c ^ 4 = alpha / beta

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..name: d3_gamma_eq_one
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..sig: theorem d3_gamma_eq_one (alpha beta L_c : ℝ) (hα : 0 < alpha) (hβ : 0 < beta) (hL : 0 < L_c) (h_critical : L_c ^ 4 = alpha / beta) : beta * L_c ^ 2 / (alpha * L_c⁻¹ ^ 2) = 1

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..name: rgf_three_dimensions
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..sig: theorem rgf_three_dimensions : gammaCritical 3 = 1 ∧ gammaCritical 2 ≠ 1 ∧ gammaCritical 4 ≠ 1 ∧ gammaCritical 5 ≠ 1 ∧ gammaCritical 6 ≠ 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionLocking..doc: The three-dimensional emergence theorem of RGF: under the momentum-winding competition mechanism, d = 3 is the unique dimension at which the two modes are perfectly balanced at the critical point. This provides a purely mathematical explanation for "why physical space is three-dimensional".

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.name: latticeForward_eq_forsCount
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.sig: theorem latticeForward_eq_forsCount (d : ℕ) : latticeForward d = forsCount cubicCoord d
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.doc: `latticeForward` is exactly the cubic-family FORS effective-direction count.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.name: latticeForward_eq_five_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.sig: theorem latticeForward_eq_five_iff {d : ℕ} : latticeForward d = 5 ↔ d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.doc: **Lattice criterion.** The forward-repulsion direction count equals `5` iff the spatial dimension is `3`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.name: forsPoleOrder_one_eq_five_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.sig: theorem forsPoleOrder_one_eq_five_iff {d : ℕ} : forsPoleOrder d 1 = 5 ↔ d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.doc: **Pole criterion at recovery order `R = 1`.** The FORS pole order equals `5` iff the spatial dimension is `3`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.name: dimension_three_unique_lattice
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.sig: theorem dimension_three_unique_lattice : ∃! d : ℕ, latticeForward d = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.doc: **Lattice-only uniqueness.** Among all dimensions, exactly one — namely `d = 3` — yields the five-fold forward-repulsion count. (Restatement of the cubic locking in terms of `latticeForward`.)

RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.name: dimension_three_unique
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.sig: theorem dimension_three_unique : ∃! p : ℕ × ℕ, latticeForward p.1 = 5 ∧ forsPoleOrder p.1 p.2 = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/DimensionThreeUni.doc: **Joint uniqueness theorem.** Under the two independent first-principles criteria — the cubic-lattice forward-repulsion direction count `2*d − 1` and the FORS pole order `d + 2*R` — simultaneously requiring *both* to equal `5` has the **unique** solution `(d, R) = (3, 1)`. Thus `d = 3` is locked by the intersection of two independent criteria, not by a single tunable number.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: n₂_eq_pred_div_two_of_odd
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: lemma n₂_eq_pred_div_two_of_odd {k : ℕ} (h : Odd k) : n₂ k = (k - 1) / 2

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: one_lt_n₂_iff_five_le_and_odd
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: lemma one_lt_n₂_iff_five_le_and_odd {k : ℕ} (h : Odd k) : 1 < n₂ k ↔ 5 ≤ k

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: n₂_le_one_of_odd_lt_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: lemma n₂_le_one_of_odd_lt_five {j : ℕ} (hj : Odd j) (hj4 : j ≤ 4) : n₂ j ≤ 1

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: stableGen_iff_eq_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: lemma stableGen_iff_eq_five (k : ℕ) : StableGen k ↔ k = 5

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: rotMatrix_no_real_eigenvector
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: lemma rotMatrix_no_real_eigenvector (θ : ℝ) (hsin : Real.sin θ ≠ 0) : ∀ (v : Fin 2 → ℝ) (lam : ℝ), v ≠ 0 → rotMatrix θ *ᵥ v ≠ lam • v

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: rotMatrix_irreducible
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: lemma rotMatrix_irreducible (θ : ℝ) (hsin : Real.sin θ ≠ 0) : ¬ ∃ (W : Submodule ℝ (Fin 2 → ℝ)), W ≠ ⊤ ∧ W ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∀ (v : Fin 2 → ℝ), v ∈ W → rotMatrix θ *ᵥ v ∈ W

RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.name: definitive_locking
RGF/Generative/Locking/DualHierarchyLock.sig: theorem definitive_locking : (∃! k, StableGen k) ∧ (StableGen 5) ∧ (n₂ 5 = 2) ∧ (∀ k, StableGen k → k = 5) ∧ (Nonempty BiLevel)

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: dual_layer_fixed_point
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem dual_layer_fixed_point {X Y : Type*} [MetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [Nonempty X] [MetricSpace Y] [CompleteSpace Y] [Nonempty Y] {Kf : ℝ≥0} {f : X → X} (hf : ContractingWith Kf f) {Kh : ℝ≥0} {h : X → Y → Y} (hh : ∀ x, ContractingWith Kh (h x)) : ∃! p : X × Y, (f p.1, h p.1 p.2) = p
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: **Dual-layer Banach fixed-point theorem.** Let `f : X → X` be a Banach contraction (outer iteration) and let `h : X → (Y → Y)` be a family of Banach contractions (inner iteration, slaved to the outer state `x`). Then the coupled iteration `Ψ (x, y) = (f x, h x y)` on the product space has a unique joint fixed point. The proof pins the first coordinate by the outer contraction and, at the resulting outer fixed point, pins the second coordinate by the inner contraction.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: affine_half_lipschitz
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem affine_half_lipschitz (c : ℝ) : LipschitzWith (1/2 : ℝ≥0) (affine_half c)

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: affine_half_contracting
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem affine_half_contracting (c : ℝ) : ContractingWith (1/2 : ℝ≥0) (affine_half c)
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: `affine_half c` is a Banach contraction with ratio `1/2`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: affine_half_fixedPoint
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem affine_half_fixedPoint (c : ℝ) : Function.IsFixedPt (affine_half c) (2 * c)
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: `2c` is a fixed point of `affine_half c`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: affine_half_fixedPoint_eq
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem affine_half_fixedPoint_eq (c : ℝ) : (affine_half_contracting c).fixedPoint (affine_half c) = 2 * c
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: The Banach fixed point of `affine_half c` is exactly `2c`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: joint_fixed_point
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem joint_fixed_point (D : DualLayerLockingDynamics) : ∃! p : ℝ × ℝ, (D.fout p.1, D.fin p.1 p.2) = p
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: The coupled double-layer iteration has a unique joint fixed point, by the abstract engine `dual_layer_fixed_point`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: locking_from_dynamics
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem locking_from_dynamics (D : DualLayerLockingDynamics) : n₂ 5 = 2 ∧ Odd 5 ∧ StableGen 5 ∧ (∃! k, StableGen k) ∧ (∀ k, StableGen k → k = 5) ∧ Nat.card (DihedralGroup 5) = 10 ∧ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5))
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: **Locking from dynamics.** Any dual-layer locking dynamics forces the full chain of locking conditions through the derived `StableTwoLayer`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: dynamics_to_locking_master
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem dynamics_to_locking_master (D : DualLayerLockingDynamics) : (∃! p : ℝ × ℝ, (D.fout p.1, D.fin p.1 p.2) = p) ∧ n₂ 5 = 2 ∧ Odd 5 ∧ StableGen 5 ∧ (∃! k, StableGen k) ∧ (∀ k, StableGen k → k = 5) ∧ Nat.card (DihedralGroup 5) = 10 ∧ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5))
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: **Master theorem.** From the contraction dynamics one obtains, in one statement: the unique joint fixed point of the coupled iteration, and the locking conditions `n₂ = 2` (L2), `Odd k` (L3), `k = 5` (unique), and `D₅`-consistency.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: nonempty
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: The dual-layer locking dynamics are non-empty.

RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.name: standard_locks
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.sig: theorem standard_locks : n₂ 5 = 2 ∧ Odd 5 ∧ StableGen 5 ∧ (∃! k, StableGen k) ∧ (∀ k, StableGen k → k = 5) ∧ Nat.card (DihedralGroup 5) = 10 ∧ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5))
RGF/Generative/Locking/DynamicsToLocking.doc: Sanity check: the explicit instance indeed yields the locking conditions.

RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.name: relation_equiv
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.sig: theorem relation_equiv (k d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hk : Odd k) : EmergentDimensionRelation k d ↔ d = (k + 1) / 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.doc: **Equivalent form**: for `d ≥ 1` and `k` odd, `2 d - 1 = k ⟺ d = (k + 1) / 2`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.name: relation_from_lattice
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.sig: theorem relation_from_lattice {d : ℕ} (incoming : LatticeDir d) : EmergentDimensionRelation (allowedNext incoming).card d
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.doc: **Lattice origin of the relation**: the cardinality of the FORS core (the set of admissible propagation directions) is exactly `2 d - 1`, so taking `k` to be that cardinality makes the emergent dimension relation hold automatically. This shows that the left-hand side `2 d - 1` of `2 d - 1 = k` is not written down out of thin air, but is a combinatorial consequence of the lattice rules.

RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.name: relation_of_symmetry
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.sig: theorem relation_of_symmetry (k d : ℕ) [NeZero k] (incoming : LatticeDir d) (Dir : Type) [MulAction (DihedralGroup k) Dir] [IsPretransitive (DihedralGroup k) Dir] (base : Dir) (hstab : Nat.card (stabilizer (DihedralGroup k) base) = 2) (realize : Dir ≃ ↥(allowedNext incoming)) : EmergentDimensionRelation k d
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.doc: Derive the emergent dimension relation `2 d - 1 = k` from the critical symmetry structure: directly invoke the orbit-counting theorem `relation_from_symmetry`, with no numerical bridging hypothesis.

RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.name: emergent_dimension_three
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.sig: theorem emergent_dimension_three {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (incoming : LatticeDir d) (Dir : Type) [MulAction (DihedralGroup 5) Dir] [IsPretransitive (DihedralGroup 5) Dir] (base : Dir) (hstab : Nat.card (stabilizer (DihedralGroup 5) base) = 2) (realize : Dir ≃ ↥(allowedNext incoming)) : d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.doc: **Dimension locking**: under the critical symmetry structure, if the symmetry order `k = 5` then the emergent dimension `d = 3`. This is the formalisation of `2 d - 1 = 5 ⟹ d = 3` (derived by orbit counting, with no bridging hypothesis).

RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.name: emergent_dimension_locked
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.sig: theorem emergent_dimension_locked (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] (hk : StrengthenedLockingMembraneConditions k) {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (incoming : LatticeDir d) (Dir : Type) [MulAction (DihedralGroup k) Dir] [IsPretransitive (DihedralGroup k) Dir] (base : Dir) (hstab : Nat.card (stabilizer (DihedralGroup k) base) = 2) (realize : Dir ≃ ↥(allowedNext incoming)) : (2 * d - 1 = k) ∧ k = 5 ∧ d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.doc: **Complete derivation chain (orbit counting + locking membrane ⟹ three dimensions)** Given: * the three locking-membrane conditions `StrengthenedLockingMembraneConditions k` (whose unique solution is `k = 5`); * the critical symmetry structure (transitive `D_k` action on the type `Dir` of admissible directions, direction stabiliser of order 2, identified with the lattice direction set via `realize`). Then one simultaneously obtains the emergent dimension relation `2 d - 1 = k`, the symmetry order `k = 5`, and the dimension locking `d = 3`. All conclusions are derived; no `axiom`, no `sorry`, no numerical bridging hypothesis.

RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.name: emergent_dimension_locked_witness
RGF/Generative/Locking/EmergentDimension.doc: **Existence witness (non-vacuous)**: on the three-dimensional cubic lattice (`d = 3`) explicitly construct the critical symmetry structure (`Dir = ZMod 5`, the natural transitive `D₅` action, the stabiliser of direction `0` of order 2, `realize` coming from the cardinality 5 of `card_allowedNext`), thereby proving, **with no bridging hypothesis**, simultaneously `2·3 - 1 = 5`, `k = 5`, `d = 3`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.name: totient_5_is_power_of_two
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.sig: theorem totient_5_is_power_of_two : ∃ m : ℕ, Nat.totient 5 = 2 ^ m

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.name: five_minimal_totient_ge_4
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.sig: theorem five_minimal_totient_ge_4 : ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p % 2 = 1 → p < 5 → Nat.totient p < 4

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.name: totient_prime_eq
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.sig: theorem totient_prime_eq (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) : Nat.totient p = p - 1

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.name: totient_7_not_power_of_two
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFold.lean.sig: theorem totient_7_not_power_of_two : ¬ ∃ m : ℕ, m < 10 ∧ Nat.totient 7 = 2 ^ m

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: euler_implies_low_degree
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..sig: theorem euler_implies_low_degree (V E F : ℕ) (hEuler : V + F = E + 2) (hFace : 3 * F ≤ 2 * E) : 2 * E < 6 * V
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: The Euler formula implies the average degree of a planar graph < 6.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: steiner_5_8_24_lambda0
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: Verification of the divisibility condition of the Steiner system S(5,8,24).

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: steiner_6_8_24_fails
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: For t = 6 the divisibility condition of S(6,8,24) fails at i=1: C(23,5) mod C(7,5) ≠ 0.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: five_not_hopf_allowed
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: 5 is not among the allowed dimensions for Hopf invariant 1.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: five_not_hopf_and_prime
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: 5 is not among the Hopf allowed dimensions, and 5 is an odd prime.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: odd_ge3_not_hopf
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..sig: theorem odd_ge3_not_hopf (n : ℕ) (hodd : n % 2 = 1) (hge : n ≥ 3) : n ∉ hopfAllowedDimensions
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: Among the Hopf allowed dimensions {1,2,4,8}, 1 is the only odd one, 4 and 8 are even, and 2 is even. Hence no odd number ≥ 3 is in the allowed set.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: three_and_five_both_excluded
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: 5 is the first odd prime dimension excluded by Adams' theorem. Among the odd primes 3, 5, 7, 11, ..., 3 is also excluded, but 5 is the focus of discussion, because it is the critical point of "local-global balance".

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: euler_totient_2
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: φ(2) = 1, φ(3) = 2 (the Galois group structure of smaller primes is simple).

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..name: all_cases_critical_param_is_5
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..sig: theorem all_cases_critical_param_is_5 : heckeResidueCase.criticalParam = 5 ∧ fiveColorCase.criticalParam = 5 ∧ steinerCase.criticalParam = 5 ∧ hopfInvariantCase.criticalParam = 5 ∧ cyclotomicCase.criticalParam = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveFoldSymmetry..doc: The critical parameter of all five cases is 5.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: solvable_iff_le_four

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: **Core criterion**: S_n is solvable iff n ≤ 4. This is a **structural** theorem (not enumeration), arising from: - the Abel-Ruffini theorem (the quintic has no solution by radicals) - equivalently, A₅ is the smallest non-abelian simple group

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: five_satisfies_fiveLockingCondition

This is the core result of this file: k_c = 5 is not selected by enumeration, but is **uniquely derived** from C1 (emergence → S_k unsolvable) and C2 (convergence → minimality).

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: five_locking_exists_unique

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: **Existence-uniqueness**: there exists a unique value of k satisfying the five-fold locking condition.

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: corollary_S5_minimal_nonsolvable
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.sig: theorem corollary_S5_minimal_nonsolvable : ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5)) ∧ ∀ m, m < 5 → IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: Corollary 1: S₅ is the smallest non-solvable symmetric group

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: corollary_A5_order
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: Corollary 2: A₅ is the smallest non-abelian simple group (order = 60) This explains why the quintic is unsolvable in Galois theory

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: corollary_totient_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: Corollary 3: the fifth cyclotomic field Q(ζ₅) is the smallest non-real cyclotomic extension satisfying φ(p) ≥ 4

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: corollary_steiner_max_t
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: Corollary 4: the Steiner system t = 5 is the largest possible t (S(5,8,24) exists but S(6,k,v) does not) This is the manifestation of five-fold locking in combinatorial design

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: corollary_turan_K6free

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: Corollary 5: the Turán graph T(n,5) is the extremal problem for the complete 5-partite graph r = 5 is the number of parts of a K₆-free graph, corresponding to the structure of S₅

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: corollary_SU5_minimal
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: Corollary 6: SU(5) is the smallest SU(n) group able to accommodate one generation of Standard Model fermions dim SU(5) = 24 = 2 × dim(SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1))

RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.name: complete_deduction_chain
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.sig: theorem complete_deduction_chain : -- (1) emergence condition: S₅ is unsolvable ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 5)) ∧ -- (2) structural criterion: S_n solvable ⟺ n ≤ 4 (∀ n, IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) ↔ n ≤ 4) ∧ -- (3) uniqueness: the k satisfying the locking condition is exactly 5 (∀ sys : RecursiveSystem, FiveLockingCondition sys → sys.k = 5)
RGF/Generative/Locking/FiveLockingUnique.doc: **Complete logical chain**: C1 (recursive generation → emergence) → S_k unsolvable C2 (contraction convergence → minimality) → k minimal S_n unsolvable ⟺ n ≥ 5 (structural theorem) ∴ k_c = 5 (the unique solution) This is a **purely deductive chain**, every step a logical necessity. "5" is not chosen but **derived**.

RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.name: dimension_ladder
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.sig: theorem dimension_ladder : dimSU 5 < dimSO 10 ∧ dimSO 10 < dimE6
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.doc: The strictly increasing generator-count ladder `SU(5) ⊂ SO(10) ⊂ E₆`, i.e. `24 < 45 < 78`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.name: rank_ladder
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.sig: theorem rank_ladder : (5 - 1 : ℕ) = 4 ∧ rankSO_even 5 = 5 ∧ (4 : ℕ) < 5 ∧ (5 : ℕ) < 6
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.doc: The rank ladder `rank SU(5) = 4 < rank SO(10) = 5 < rank E₆ = 6`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.name: spinorDim_ten
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.doc: The chiral spinor of `SO(10)` has dimension `16`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.name: dimSO_locks_ten
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.sig: theorem dimSO_locks_ten (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 100) : dimSO n = 45 ↔ n = 10
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.doc: **Antisymmetric locking.** Within the antisymmetric family `n(n-1)/2`, the value `45` is realised uniquely by `n = 10` (for `n` up to a generous bound).

RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.name: spinorDim_locks_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.sig: theorem spinorDim_locks_five (m : ℕ) (hm : m ≤ 100) : spinorDim m = 16 ↔ m = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.doc: **Spinor locking.** Within the spinor family `2^{m-1}`, the value `16` is realised uniquely by `m = 5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.name: gut_ladder_locked
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.sig: theorem gut_ladder_locked : dimSU 5 = 24 ∧ dimSO 10 = 45 ∧ dimE6 = 78 ∧ spinorDim 5 = 16 ∧ fundE6 = 27 ∧ dimSU 5 < dimSO 10 ∧ dimSO 10 < dimE6 ∧ spinorDim 5 = 10 + 5 + 1 ∧ fundE6 = spinorDim 5 + 10 + 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/HigherGroupLockin.doc: **Full ladder locking.** The triple of generator counts `(24, 45, 78)` together with the spinor/fundamental dimensions `(16, 27)` is realised by the unique ascending chain `SU(5) ⊂ SO(10) ⊂ E₆`, matching the three-generation `16`-plet embedding.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: membrane_criterion_is_definitional
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.sig: theorem membrane_criterion_is_definitional (sys : RecursiveSystem) : EmergenceCondition sys ↔ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin sys.k))
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (B), membrane.** The physical "emergence" premise is, *by definition*, the statement that `S_k` is non-solvable: the proof is `Iff.rfl`. Hence the group-theoretic criterion is not derived from a more primitive generative axiom; it is inserted as the meaning of "emergence". This is the one result that is genuinely *definitionally circular* at its physics→mathematics step.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: recovery_criterion_is_equation
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.sig: theorem recovery_criterion_is_equation (R : ℕ) : emergence_condition R ↔ (alpha_num R = n_eff R)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (B), recovery.** The recovery criterion is *not* a definitional restatement of `R = 1`. It unfolds definitionally to an **equation between two independently defined numeric functions**: the pole-order function `alpha_num R = 3 + 2R` and the effective-direction-count function `n_eff R`. Solving that equation (not unfolding it) gives `R = 1`; the proof of `r_equals_one_unique` requires a genuine case analysis, not `Iff.rfl`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: recovery_target_not_baked_in
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (A), recovery.** The conclusion `R = 1` is not written into the criterion. The two stipulated inputs are ordinary numeric functions (`alpha_num`, `n_eff`); the criterion holds at `R = 1` and fails at the neighbouring values `R = 0, 2`, so `R = 1` is solved for, not stipulated.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: dimension_target_not_baked_in
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (A), dimension.** The forward-direction criterion is the structural form `latticeForward d = 2d − 1`; the target `5` is not baked in — it is the imported locking value `k = 5`. The criterion selects `d = 3` because `2·3 − 1 = 5`, and takes other values at other dimensions (`d = 2 ↦ 3`, `d = 4 ↦ 7`). Thus `d = 3` is solved for, but the criterion inherits whatever grounding the imported number `5` has.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: dimension_joint_unique
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.sig: theorem dimension_joint_unique : ∃! p : ℕ × ℕ, latticeForward p.1 = 5 ∧ forsPoleOrder p.1 p.2 = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (B), dimension.** The two criteria are genuinely *independent* forms: the lattice count `latticeForward d = 2d − 1` does not depend on the recovery order `R`, while the pole order `forsPoleOrder d R = d + 2R` does. Requiring both to equal `5` has the unique solution `(d, R) = (3, 1)` — a real intersection, not a single tunable count.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: emergent_relation_target_not_baked_in
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (A), emergent relation.** The relation `2d − 1 = k` is a genuine constraint, not a tautology: it holds at `(k, d) = (5, 3)` and fails at `(5, 2)` — so `d = 3` is forced by `k = 5`, not written in.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: emergent_relation_is_derived
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.sig: theorem emergent_relation_is_derived (k d : ℕ) [NeZero k] (incoming : LatticeToFORS.LatticeDir d) (Dir : Type) [MulAction (DihedralGroup k) Dir] [MulAction.IsPretransitive (DihedralGroup k) Dir] (base : Dir) (hstab : Nat.card (MulAction.stabilizer (DihedralGroup k) base) = 2) (realize : Dir ≃ ↥(LatticeToFORS.allowedNext incoming)) : RGF.EmergentDimension.EmergentDimensionRelation k d
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (B), emergent relation.** In contrast to the membrane case, the relation `2d − 1 = k` is **not** asserted as a definitional identity: it is a *theorem* proved from a critical symmetry structure via the orbit–stabiliser theorem (`relation_of_symmetry`), with no numerical bridging hypothesis. This is the shape a locking criterion should have to pass audit (B).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: sm26_target_not_baked_in
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (A), 26 parameters.** The number `26` appears in *no* definition: it is the value of the closed-form count `4N + 2(N−1)² + 6` at `N = 3`. At two or four generations the same count gives `16` and `40`, so `26` is a forced consequence of `N = 3`, not a fitted target.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.name: sm26_is_derived
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.sig: theorem sm26_is_derived : rgfPrediction.emergentDim = 3 ∧ (∀ N, RGF.StandardModel26.totalSMParams N = 4 * N + 2 * (N - 1) ^ 2 + 6) ∧ RGF.StandardModel26.totalSMParams rgfPrediction.emergentDim = 26
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingAuditSuite.doc: **Audit (B), 26 parameters.** The count is a forced computation from the two RGF structural inputs — generation number `N = d = 3` and the gauge group `SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1)` from the `5 = 3 + 2` partition — via ordinary textbook parameter counting.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: The spectral gap at a contracting mode is positive.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: single_mode_radial_exclusion
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem single_mode_radial_exclusion {n₂ : ℕ} (h : n₂ = 1) (S : CriticalSpectrum n₂) : ¬ (HasNeutralMode S ∧ HasContractingMode S)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Core spectral lemma: a single two-dimensional block has only one radial coordinate ρ₀, so it cannot be both a neutral mode (ρ₀ = 1) and a contracting mode (ρ₀ < 1). This is the rigorous form of the claim that "argument and modulus are linearly dependent within a single block".

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: RGFDynamicalAxioms.single_mode_exclusion
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem RGFDynamicalAxioms.single_mode_exclusion {n : ℕ} {sys : RGFState.EquivariantSystem n} {s_fix : RGFState n} {k : ℕ} (ax : RGFDynamicalAxioms sys s_fix k) (hn2 : num2DIrreps k = 1) : ¬ (ax.g2_holds ∧ ax.g3_holds)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Proposition 2 (made concrete; the former axiom single_mode_exclusion is now a theorem): when n₂ = 1, G2 ∧ G3 cannot hold simultaneously.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: RGFDynamicalAxioms.solvable_exclusion
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem RGFDynamicalAxioms.solvable_exclusion {n : ℕ} {sys : RGFState.EquivariantSystem n} {s_fix : RGFState n} {k : ℕ} (ax : RGFDynamicalAxioms sys s_fix k) (h : IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))) : ¬ ax.g2_holds
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Proposition 3 (made concrete; the former axiom solvable_exclusion is now a theorem): when Sₖ is solvable, G2 fails.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: num2DIrreps_odd

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Formula for n₂ when k is odd.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: num2DIrreps_even

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: When k is even and n₂ = 2, k = 6.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: n2_pos_of_odd

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Key arithmetic lemma: for odd k ≥ 3, n₂ ≥ 1.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: overconstraint_arithmetic

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: The arithmetic core of over-constraint: n₂ ≥ 3 implies k ≥ 7 (when k is odd).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: overconstraint_implies_zero_spectral_gap
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem overconstraint_implies_zero_spectral_gap {n : ℕ} (sys : RGFState.EquivariantSystem n) (s_fix : RGFState n) [IsCriticalFixedPoint sys s_fix] (k : ℕ) [HasDihedralSymmetry sys s_fix k] (_hn2 : num2DIrreps k ≥ 3) : (linearize sys s_fix).spectralGap = 0
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Proposition 1: when n₂ ≥ 3 the spectral gap is zero (immediate from the definition of linearize).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: overconstraint_no_positive_gap
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem overconstraint_no_positive_gap {n : ℕ} (sys : RGFState.EquivariantSystem n) (s_fix : RGFState n) [IsCriticalFixedPoint sys s_fix] (k : ℕ) [HasDihedralSymmetry sys s_fix k] (_hn2 : num2DIrreps k ≥ 3) : ¬ ((linearize sys s_fix).spectralGap > 0)

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: nonsolvability_necessity

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Proposition 4: when k is even, L3 fails.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: five_satisfies_locking
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem five_satisfies_locking : LockingMembraneConditions 5 where L2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: k = 5 satisfies the Locking-Membrane conditions (L2 ∧ L3).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: locking_unique

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: LockingMembraneConditions.L1
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem LockingMembraneConditions.L1 {k : ℕ} (hk : LockingMembraneConditions k) : ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))

After dropping the L1 field, L1 can still be recovered as a provable consequence: L2 ∧ L3 uniquely lock k = 5, and S₅ is not solvable. This theorem is named `LockingMembraneConditions.L1`, so legacy code can still invoke it via dot notation `h.L1`, preserving backward compatibility.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Synthesis theorem: the k satisfying the Locking-Membrane conditions exists and is unique, k = 5.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: n2_equals_two_from_axioms

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: k_equals_five_from_n2

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: rgf_to_locking_membrane
