RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Complete derivation chain: the conclusions of the four propositions ⇒ k = 5 and L1–L3 hold.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: rgf_critical_emergence
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem rgf_critical_emergence : ∃! (k : ℕ), LockingMembraneConditions k
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Final synthesis theorem: the k satisfying the three Locking-Membrane conditions exists and is unique, k = 5. This is the final closure of the RGF axiom chain — the combination of the four propositions uniquely determines k = 5.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: three_fails_L2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem three_fails_L2 : num2DIrreps 3 ≠ 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: k = 3 fails L2 (n₂ = 1 ≠ 2).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: four_fails_L3
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem four_fails_L3 : ¬ Odd 4
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: k = 4 fails L3 (k = 4 is even).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: seven_fails_L2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem seven_fails_L2 : num2DIrreps 7 ≠ 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: k = 7 fails L2 (n₂ = 3 ≠ 2).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: nine_fails_L2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem nine_fails_L2 : num2DIrreps 9 ≠ 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: k = 9 fails L2 (n₂ = 4 ≠ 2).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: exhaustive_check_small_k
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem exhaustive_check_small_k : ∀ k ∈ ({3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9} : Finset ℕ), LockingMembraneConditions k → k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Exhaustive check for small k: only k = 5 satisfies all three conditions.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: reduction_realizable
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem reduction_realizable : ∃ S : CriticalSpectrum 2, G2_concrete S 5 ∧ G3_concrete S
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Non-triviality (spectral level): there is a two-dimensional critical spectrum (one neutral mode ρ = 1, one contracting mode ρ = 1/2) that satisfies both the concrete G2 (k = 5, S₅ non-solvable) and G3. This shows that Proposition 2 after the spectral reduction is not vacuous.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.name: g2_fails_for_solvable
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.sig: theorem g2_fails_for_solvable {n₂ : ℕ} (S : CriticalSpectrum n₂) (k : ℕ) (h : IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))) : ¬ G2_concrete S k
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembrane.l.doc: Contrast: S₄ is solvable, so no two-dimensional critical spectrum satisfies the concrete G2 (k = 4). This shows that Proposition 3 (solvable_exclusion) after the spectral reduction is not vacuous.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: poleZ_abs
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem poleZ_abs (p : ℕ) (j : ℕ) : ‖poleZ p j‖ = 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: Each pole phase lies on the unit circle.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: Gamma_eigval_abs
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem Gamma_eigval_abs {p : ℕ} {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (j : Fin p) : ‖(ρ : ℂ) * poleZ p j‖ = ρ
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: Every eigenvalue (diagonal entry) of `Γ_p` has modulus `ρ` (for `0 ≤ ρ`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: Gamma_spectralRadius_lt_one
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem Gamma_spectralRadius_lt_one {p : ℕ} {ρ : ℝ} (hρ0 : 0 < ρ) (hρ1 : ρ < 1) (j : Fin p) : ‖(ρ : ℂ) * poleZ p j‖ < 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: **L1** holds for every odd `p ≥ 5`: the modulus of each eigenvalue is `ρ < 1`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: poleZ_injective
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem poleZ_injective (p : ℕ) : Function.Injective (fun j : Fin p => poleZ p j)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: The pole phases `j ↦ exp(i·π·(2j+1)/p)` are pairwise distinct on `Fin p`. For a diagonal matrix this is exactly "every eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity `1`".

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: Gamma_eigvals_distinct
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem Gamma_eigvals_distinct {p : ℕ} {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ρ ≠ 0) : Function.Injective (fun j : Fin p => (ρ : ℂ) * poleZ p j)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: **L2** as stated on the eigenvalues of `Γ_p` (for `ρ ≠ 0`): the diagonal entries are pairwise distinct.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: kappa_lt_one
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem kappa_lt_one {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) : kappa p < 1

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: kappa_strictMono
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem kappa_strictMono {p q : ℕ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) (hpq : p < q) : kappa p < kappa q
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: `p ↦ cos(π/p)` is strictly increasing: for `1 ≤ p < q`, `κ_p < κ_q`. In particular `cos(π/5) < cos(π/7) < cos(π/9) < ⋯`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: kappa_five_le
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem kappa_five_le {p : ℕ} (hodd : Odd p) (hp : 5 ≤ p) : kappa 5 ≤ kappa p
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: Lower bound: `κ₅ ≤ κ_p` for every odd `p ≥ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: argmin_kappa_strict
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem argmin_kappa_strict {p : ℕ} (hp : 5 ≤ p) (hne : p ≠ 5) : kappa 5 < kappa p
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: **argmin**: over `p ≥ 5`, the effective contraction factor `κ_p = cos(π/p)` is *strictly* minimised only at `p = 5` (in particular over the odd `p ≥ 5`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: argmin_kappa
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem argmin_kappa : ∃! p : ℕ, (Odd p ∧ 5 ≤ p) ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, Odd q → 5 ≤ q → kappa p ≤ kappa q
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: **`argmin_{p ∈ {5,7,9,…}} κ_p = 5`**: `p = 5` is the unique minimiser of `κ_p = cos(π/p)` among odd `p ≥ 5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: thermodynamic_dim
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem thermodynamic_dim {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) : 2 * d - 1 = d + 2 ↔ d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: The thermodynamic self-consistency condition `2d − 1 = d + 2` has the unique solution `d = 3` (for `d ≥ 1`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.name: propositionO7
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.sig: theorem propositionO7 : -- L1 : each eigenvalue has modulus `ρ`, so spectral radius `= ρ < 1` (∀ (p : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → ρ < 1 → ∀ j : Fin p, ‖(ρ : ℂ) * poleZ p j‖ < 1) ∧ -- L2 : eigenvalues pairwise distinct for every `p` (with `ρ ≠ 0`) (∀ (p : ℕ) (ρ : ℝ), ρ ≠ 0 → Function.Injective (fun j : Fin p => (ρ : ℂ) * poleZ p j)) ∧ -- selection : `argmin_{odd p ≥ 5} cos(π/p) = 5`, uniquely (∃! p : ℕ, (Odd p ∧ 5 ≤ p) ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, Odd q → 5 ≤ q → kappa p ≤ kappa q) ∧ -- golden value at `p = 5` kappa 5 = (1 + Real.sqrt 5) / 4 ∧ -- thermodynamic dimension (2 * 3 - 1 = 3 + 2)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingMembraneO7.doc: **Proposition O7 (machine-verifiable form).** Bundles the verified content: * **L1** holds for every odd `p ≥ 5` (spectral radius `ρ < 1`); * **L2** holds for every odd `p ≥ 5` (eigenvalues pairwise distinct); * the effective contraction factor `κ_p = cos(π/p)` is strictly increasing, so `p = 5` is its unique minimiser over odd `p ≥ 5` (`argmin κ_p = 5`); * `κ₅ = (1 + √5)/4` with `2·κ₅` the golden ratio; * the thermodynamic constraint `2d − 1 = d + 2` fixes `d = 3`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.name: eq_spiralDual_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.sig: theorem eq_spiralDual_iff (s : ℂ) : s = spiralDual s ↔ s.re = 1 / 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.doc: Key algebraic equivalence: `s = spiralDual s ↔ Re s = 1/2`. (`spiralDual s = 1 - conj s`; the imaginary parts agree automatically, while the real part gives `s.re = 1 - s.re`, i.e. `Re s = 1/2`.)

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.name: locking_nondegenerate_of_RH
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.doc: **Locking non-degeneracy follows from the Riemann Hypothesis**. Given RH (critical-strip version), every `s ∈ ZetaNontrivialZero` has `Re s = 1/2`, and `eq_spiralDual_iff` then gives `s = spiralDual s`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.name: RH_strip_of_locking
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.doc: **Locking non-degeneracy follows from the Riemann Hypothesis**. Given RH (critical-strip version), every `s ∈ ZetaNontrivialZero` has `Re s = 1/2`, and `eq_spiralDual_iff` then gives `s = spiralDual s`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.name: locking_nondegenerate_iff_RH
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.doc: **Equivalence**: the core FORS output (locking non-degeneracy) is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis (critical-strip version).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.name: locking_nondegenerate_for_zeta
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingNonDegener.doc: **The core FORS output theorem (condition (U))**: locking non-degeneracy. As explained in the file header, this statement is **equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis** (critical-strip version), an open problem. We therefore state it in its honest *conditional* form: assuming the Riemann Hypothesis (`RiemannHypothesis_strip`), locking non-degeneracy holds. (Previously this was left as a bare `sorry`; the conditional form removes the `sorry` while remaining mathematically faithful — it is just `locking_nondegenerate_of_RH`, recorded under this name for the FORS output interface. By `locking_nondegenerate_iff_RH` the hypothesis is also necessary.)

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..name: L2_L3_imply_k_eq_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..sig: theorem L2_L3_imply_k_eq_five (hL2 : L2 k) (hL3 : L3 k) : k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..doc: L2 and L3 together uniquely lock k = 5.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..name: S5_not_solvable
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..doc: When k = 5, S₅ is not solvable (an existing Mathlib theorem).

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..name: L2_L3_imply_L1
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..sig: theorem L2_L3_imply_L1 (hL2 : L2 k) (hL3 : L3 k) : L1 k
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..doc: L2 ∧ L3 ⇒ L1: the core theorem of the locking-condition reduction.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..name: locking_reduces_to_two
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..sig: theorem locking_reduces_to_two : (L1 k ∧ L2 k ∧ L3 k) ↔ (L2 k ∧ L3 k)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..doc: The three locking conditions are equivalent to two: L1 ∧ L2 ∧ L3 ↔ L2 ∧ L3.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..name: locking_iff_L2_L3
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..sig: theorem locking_iff_L2_L3 : LockingMembraneConditions k ↔ (L2 k ∧ L3 k)
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..doc: Equivalent form: the locking conditions = L2 ∧ L3.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..name: five_unique_for_L2_L3
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..sig: theorem five_unique_for_L2_L3 (hL2 : L2 k) (hL3 : L3 k) : k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingReduction..doc: k = 5 is the unique natural number satisfying L2 ∧ L3.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.name: locking_membrane_uniqueness
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.sig: theorem locking_membrane_uniqueness (k : ℕ) (hL2 : L2 k) (hL3 : L3 k) : k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.doc: Theorem: any k satisfying L2 and L3 must equal 5.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.name: L1_of_ge_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.sig: theorem L1_of_ge_five {k : ℕ} (hk : 5 ≤ k) : L1 k
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.doc: L1 holds for k ≥ 5: if |Fin k| ≥ 5 then Perm(Fin k) is not solvable.

RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.name: locking_membrane_exists_unique
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.sig: theorem locking_membrane_exists_unique : ∃! k : ℕ, L1 k ∧ L2 k ∧ L3 k
RGF/Generative/Locking/LockingUniqueness.doc: Unique-existence theorem: the only natural number k satisfying L1 ∧ L2 ∧ L3 is exactly 5.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: infrared_five_modes
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.sig: theorem infrared_five_modes (φ0 : Field) (h : IsStableField φ0) : ∃ (modes : Finset Field), Finset.card modes = 5 ∧ (∀ m ∈ modes, ∃ (lam : ℝ), ∀ x t, linearizedOperator φ0 h m x t = lam * m x t)
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: Infrared limit theorem: there are exactly 5 massless principal modes. We construct 5 distinct constant-valued fields indexed by `Fin 5` as the principal modes; under the placeholder linearized operator (identically 0), taking the eigenvalue `lam = 0` satisfies the eigenvalue equation `linearizedOperator φ0 h m = 0 = 0 · m`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: dihedral_five_order
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: Faithful alternative one: the order of D₅ is `2 · 5 = 10`, exactly twice the number of principal modes (5 rotations + 5 reflections), which is the group-theoretic basis of the "five-fold locking".

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: dihedral_five_num_irreps
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: Faithful alternative two: the number of complex irreducible representations (number of conjugacy classes) of D₅ is 4 (trivial, sign, and two 2-dimensional representations), so the 5-dimensional permutation representation decomposes as `1 + 2 + 2 = 5`, corresponding to the 5 infrared principal modes.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: pentagonRep_r
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.sig: theorem pentagonRep_r (i x : ZMod 5) : pentagonRep (DihedralGroup.r i) x = x + i
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: A rotation `r i` acts on the `x`-th mode as `x + i`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: pentagonRep_sr
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.sig: theorem pentagonRep_sr (i x : ZMod 5) : pentagonRep (DihedralGroup.sr i) x = -i - x
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: A reflection `sr i` acts on the `x`-th mode as `-x - i`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: pentagonRep_injective
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: **Faithfulness**: D₅ acts injectively on the 5 principal modes (no nontrivial element acts trivially).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: modes_pentagon_action
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.sig: theorem modes_pentagon_action : ∃ ρ : DihedralGroup 5 →* Equiv.Perm (ZMod 5), Function.Injective ρ
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: Faithful alternative three: the 5 infrared principal modes correspond one-to-one with the 5 pentagon vertices, and D₅ **faithfully** (injectively) permutes these 5 modes via the pentagon rotations/reflections.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: pentagon_action_transitive
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.sig: theorem pentagon_action_transitive (a b : ZMod 5) : ∃ g : DihedralGroup 5, pentagonRep g a = b
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: **Transitivity**: the action of D₅ on the 5 principal modes is transitive (any mode can be sent to any other by a rotation), so the 5 modes form a **single orbit** — corresponding exactly to multiplicity 1 of the trivial representation in the permutation representation.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: dihedral_five_irrep_dims_sq_sum
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: The sum of squares of the dimensions of the irreducible representations of D₅ equals the group order `2·5 = 10`: `1² + 1² + 2² + 2² = 10`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: dihedral_five_total_irreps
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: D₅ has 4 irreducible representations in total: 2 one-dimensional (trivial, sign) + 2 two-dimensional.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.name: pentagon_perm_decomposition
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeDecomposition.doc: **Dimension decomposition of the permutation representation**: the permutation representation spanned by the 5 principal modes decomposes by dimension as trivial(1) ⊕ two-dim(2) ⊕ two-dim(2), i.e. `1 + 2 + 2 = 5`. (This corresponds exactly to 3 of the 4 irreducible representations of D₅, all but the sign representation.)

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: CentralSpectrum.eigPair_conj
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem CentralSpectrum.eigPair_conj (S : CentralSpectrum) : (starRingEnd ℂ) (S.eigPair 0) = S.eigPair 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The two central eigenvalues `ρ₀ e^{±iθ₀}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: CentralSpectrum.eigPair_abs
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem CentralSpectrum.eigPair_abs (S : CentralSpectrum) (i : Fin 2) : ‖S.eigPair i‖ = S.rho0
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The two central eigenvalues `ρ₀ e^{±iθ₀}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: CentralSpectrum.eigPair_not_real
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem CentralSpectrum.eigPair_not_real (S : CentralSpectrum) (i : Fin 2) : (S.eigPair i).im ≠ 0
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The two central eigenvalues `ρ₀ e^{±iθ₀}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: trcgCouplingFactor_nonneg
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem trcgCouplingFactor_nonneg (theta0 : ℝ) (tau : ℕ) : 0 ≤ trcgCouplingFactor theta0 tau
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The TRCG (time-resolved coarse-graining) correction factor applied to the effective coupling: `K^{(τ)} = K · |sin(τθ₀/2) / (τ sin(θ₀/2))|` (eq. 3.3).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: rotateBy_lockedEigenvalue
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem rotateBy_lockedEigenvalue (rho : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (j : ℕ) : rotateBy p (lockedEigenvalue rho p j) = lockedEigenvalue rho p (j + 1)
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The `Z_p` rotation acting on the complex plane: multiplication by `e^{2πi/p}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: lockedEigenvalue_periodic
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem lockedEigenvalue_periodic (rho : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) (j : ℕ) : lockedEigenvalue rho p (j + p) = lockedEigenvalue rho p j
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The `Z_p` rotation acting on the complex plane: multiplication by `e^{2πi/p}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: rotateBy_pow_p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem rotateBy_pow_p (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) (z : ℂ) : (rotateBy p)^[p] z = z
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The `Z_p` rotation acting on the complex plane: multiplication by `e^{2πi/p}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: pgon_rotation_invariant
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem pgon_rotation_invariant (rho : ℝ) (p : ℕ) : rotateBy p '' pgonVertices rho p ⊆ pgonVertices rho p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The `Z_p` rotation acting on the complex plane: multiplication by `e^{2πi/p}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: pgon_conj_invariant
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem pgon_conj_invariant (rho : ℝ) (p : ℕ) : (starRingEnd ℂ) '' pgonVertices rho p ⊆ pgonVertices rho p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The `Z_p` rotation acting on the complex plane: multiplication by `e^{2πi/p}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: arnoldWidth_pos
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem arnoldWidth_pos (K : ℝ) (p : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : 0 < arnoldWidth K p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The width of the order-`p` Arnold tongue at weak coupling `K`: `ΔΩ_p ≈ Kᵖ/π` (eq. 3.8).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: arnoldWidth_5_7_ratio
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem arnoldWidth_5_7_ratio (K : ℝ) (hK : 0 < K) : arnoldWidth K 5 = K⁻¹ ^ 2 * arnoldWidth K 7
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The width of the order-`p` Arnold tongue at weak coupling `K`: `ΔΩ_p ≈ Kᵖ/π` (eq. 3.8).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: arnoldWidth_5_gt_7
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem arnoldWidth_5_gt_7 (K : ℝ) (hK0 : 0 < K) (hK1 : K < 1) : arnoldWidth K 7 < arnoldWidth K 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The width of the order-`p` Arnold tongue at weak coupling `K`: `ΔΩ_p ≈ Kᵖ/π` (eq. 3.8).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: arnoldWidth_strict_anti
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem arnoldWidth_strict_anti (K : ℝ) (hK0 : 0 < K) (hK1 : K < 1) {p q : ℕ} (hpq : p < q) : arnoldWidth K q < arnoldWidth K p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The width of the order-`p` Arnold tongue at weak coupling `K`: `ΔΩ_p ≈ Kᵖ/π` (eq. 3.8).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: uvConvergent_four_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem uvConvergent_four_iff (p : ℕ) : UVConvergent 4 p ↔ 5 ≤ p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: **C1 (UV absolute convergence).** The `d`-dimensional loop integral of the FORS propagator kernel `[1 + (k²/Λ²)^{p/2}]⁻¹` converges absolutely iff `p/2 > d/2`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: five_isCandidate
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem five_isCandidate : IsCandidateOrder 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: **Candidate locking order.** After C1 (`p ≥ 5` in `d = 4`) and C2 (`p` odd, for a non-vanishing bare `θ`-angle) the admissible orders are the odd integers `≥ 5`: `{5, 7, 9, …}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: candidate_ge_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem candidate_ge_five {p : ℕ} (hp : IsCandidateOrder p) : 5 ≤ p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: **Candidate locking order.** After C1 (`p ≥ 5` in `d = 4`) and C2 (`p` odd, for a non-vanishing bare `θ`-angle) the admissible orders are the odd integers `≥ 5`: `{5, 7, 9, …}`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem mode_locking_selects_five (K : ℝ) (hK0 : 0 < K) (hK1 : K < 1) {p : ℕ} (hp : IsCandidateOrder p) (hmax : ∀ q, IsCandidateOrder q → arnoldWidth K q ≤ arnoldWidth K p) : p = 5

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: instantonAction_5_lt_7
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem instantonAction_5_lt_7 : instantonAction 5 < instantonAction 7
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: **Instanton action** `S_inst(p) = π / sin(π/p)` (eq. 4.1).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: locking_order_eq_forsExponent
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem locking_order_eq_forsExponent : (∀ p, IsCandidateOrder p → 5 ≤ p) ∧ IsCandidateOrder forsExponent ∧ forsExponent = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The FORS kernel exponent (the `5` in `1/(1 + w⁵)`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: mode_locking_to_locking_membrane
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem mode_locking_to_locking_membrane (K : ℝ) (hK0 : 0 < K) (hK1 : K < 1) {p : ℕ} (hp : IsCandidateOrder p) (hmax : ∀ q, IsCandidateOrder q → arnoldWidth K q ≤ arnoldWidth K p) : LockingMembraneConditions p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: The FORS kernel exponent (the `5` in `1/(1 + w⁵)`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.name: ModularLockingScenario.locks_to_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.sig: theorem ModularLockingScenario.locks_to_five (M : ModularLockingScenario) : M.p = 5 ∧ LockingMembraneConditions M.p
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeLocking.lean.doc: it sits in the deepest Arnold-tongue basin among candidates.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.name: nontrivial_chars_paired
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.doc: Every nontrivial `Z₅` character is unequal to its conjugate: `k ≠ -k` for `k ∈ {1,2,3,4}` (5 is odd, so `2k ≢ 0 mod 5`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.name: rcd_mode_order_iff_minimalEmergent
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.sig: theorem rcd_mode_order_iff_minimalEmergent (k : ℕ) : MinimalEmergent k ↔ k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.doc: **Group-theoretic criterion.** The RCD mode order is the unique minimal emergent order, i.e. `MinimalEmergent k ↔ k = 5` — the Abel–Ruffini threshold (`S₅` is the smallest non-solvable symmetric group).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.name: rcd_mode_order_two_criteria
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.sig: theorem rcd_mode_order_two_criteria : MinimalEmergent 5 ∧ (Nat.Prime 5 ∧ 2 < Nat.totient 5 ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → p < 5 → Nat.totient p ≤ 2)
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.doc: **Twin independent characterisations.** The mode order `5` is singled out simultaneously by the group-theoretic minimal-emergence criterion *and* by the crystallographic criterion (`5` is the smallest prime rotation order with `totient > 2`, while every smaller prime order has `totient ≤ 2`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.name: rcd_mode_dim_unified
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.sig: theorem rcd_mode_dim_unified : ∃! p : ℕ × ℕ, MinimalEmergent p.1 ∧ CP p.2
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.doc: **Unification of `k = 5` and `d = 3` (the upgrade).** The classically unrelated facts behind RCD's mode order (`5`) and spatial dimension (`3`) are two faces of a single locking principle: `(5, 3)` is the **unique** pair `(k, d)` satisfying minimal emergence `MinimalEmergent k` together with the cross-product condition `CP d`. This is exactly the "same-origin" conclusion that RCD's paper-3 → paper-5 → standard-model spine aims at.

RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.name: rcd_z5_pairing_with_order
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.sig: theorem rcd_z5_pairing_with_order (k : ZMod 5) (hk : k ≠ 0) : k ≠ -k ∧ MinimalEmergent 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/ModeOrder.lean.doc: **Consistency of the RCD `Z₅` character-pairing core with the order lock.** RCD's arithmetic core `nontrivial_chars_paired` (every nontrivial `Z₅` character is unequal to its conjugate) holds together with the RGF minimal-emergence identification of the order as `5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/NoCanonicalInstan.name: no_canonical_instance_on_subgroups
RGF/Generative/Locking/NoCanonicalInstan.sig: theorem no_canonical_instance_on_subgroups (G : Type*) [Group G] [Nontrivial G] : ∃ (L : RGFDualLayer (Subgroup G) (Set G)), L.step ≠ commGen
RGF/Generative/Locking/NoCanonicalInstan.doc: **No canonical instance (faithful form).** For a *non-trivial* group `G` there is a legal `RGFDualLayer (Subgroup G) (Set G)` whose RGF main generation operator `step = modify ∘ generate` is **not** the commutator generator `commGen`. Hence `commSys` is not singled out by the type alone: the choice `step = commGen` is a genuine modelling decision, not something forced. The witness sends every subgroup to the empty entity set and closes every entity set to the whole group `⊤`; its `step` is the constant map `⊤`, which differs from `commGen` already at `⊥` (where `commGen ⊥ = ⁅⊥,⊥⁆ = ⊥ ≠ ⊤`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/NoCanonicalInstan.name: no_canonical_instance_universal_is_false
RGF/Generative/Locking/NoCanonicalInstan.sig: theorem no_canonical_instance_universal_is_false : ¬ (∀ (G : Type) [Group G], ∃ (L : RGFDualLayer (Subgroup G) (Set G)), L.step ≠ commGen)
RGF/Generative/Locking/NoCanonicalInstan.doc: **The literally-universal statement is false.** Quantified over *all* groups (including the trivial one) the existence of a counterexample instance fails: for the trivial group `PUnit` the subgroup lattice is a subsingleton, so every `L.step` necessarily equals `commGen`. This documents why the corrected statement above requires `[Nontrivial G]`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: axes_count
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem axes_count (_R : OrthoStepRule d) : Fintype.card (Fin d) = d

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: axes_linearIndependent
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem axes_linearIndependent (R : OrthoStepRule d) : LinearIndependent ℝ R.e
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Corollary (independence).** The generation axes are linearly independent.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: axes_span
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem axes_span (R : OrthoStepRule d) (hd : 0 < d) : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range R.e) = ⊤
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Corollary (spanning).** The `d` orthonormal generation axes span the whole `d`-dimensional space, hence form a basis.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: signed_axes_injective
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem signed_axes_injective (R : OrthoStepRule d) : Function.Injective (signedAxis R)
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Key geometric lemma.** The `2d` signed axes `{±eᵢ}` are pairwise distinct: the map `signedAxis` is injective. (Orthonormality rules out `eᵢ = eⱼ` for `i ≠ j`, `eᵢ = −eᵢ`, and `eᵢ = −eⱼ`.)

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: coordination_eq_two_mul
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem coordination_eq_two_mul (R : OrthoStepRule d) : (Finset.univ.image (signedAxis R)).card = 2 * d
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Corollary (coordination number).** The neighbour direction set `{±eᵢ}` has exactly `2d` elements: the coordination number is `z = 2d`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: toCandidate_isHypercubic
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem toCandidate_isHypercubic (R : OrthoStepRule d) : IsHypercubic (toCandidate R)

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: toCandidate_invSym
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem toCandidate_invSym (R : OrthoStepRule d) : (toCandidate R).invSym = true
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: The induced candidate is centrally symmetric.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: toCandidate_dim
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem toCandidate_dim (R : OrthoStepRule d) : (toCandidate R).dim = d

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: toCandidate_forward
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem toCandidate_forward (R : OrthoStepRule d) : forwardCount (toCandidate R) = 2 * d - 1
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Corollary (forward count).** Under the orthogonal step rule the effective forward direction count is `2d − 1`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: ortho_locking_forces_three
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem ortho_locking_forces_three (R : OrthoStepRule d) (hd : 0 < d) (hlock : forwardCount (toCandidate R) = 5) : d = 3
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Layer 10.** Under the orthogonal step rule, the locking condition `forwardCount = 5` forces the spatial dimension to be `d = 3` — without presupposing a cubic lattice.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: ortho_locking_forces_cubic
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem ortho_locking_forces_cubic (R : OrthoStepRule d) (hd : 0 < d) (hlock : forwardCount (toCandidate R) = 5) : (toCandidate R).dim = 3 ∧ (toCandidate R).coord = 6
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Layer 10 (cubic invariants).** Under the orthogonal step rule, the locking condition additionally fixes the coordination number at `z = 6`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: ortho_locking_rot_consistent
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem ortho_locking_rot_consistent (R : OrthoStepRule d) (hd : 0 < d) (hlock : forwardCount (toCandidate R) = 5) : rotGen (toCandidate R).dim = (toCandidate R).dim
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Layer 10 (self-consistency with the rotation criterion).** At the locked dimension `d = 3` the intrinsic rotation-vector criterion is automatically satisfied, so the two independent routes agree.

RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.name: triangular_not_orthogonal
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.sig: theorem triangular_not_orthogonal : ¬ ∃ (R : OrthoStepRule triangular.dim), OrthoStepRule.toCandidate R = triangular
RGF/Generative/Locking/OrthogonalStepRul.doc: **Layer 11.** The triangular lattice (`z = 6` at `d = 2`) is *not* realisable by any orthogonal step rule: an orthogonal step rule forces `z = 2·dim`, but the triangular lattice has `z = 6 ≠ 2·2`. This is exactly why it shares the locking count `5` with the simple-cubic lattice yet is excluded once orthogonality is imposed.

RGF/Generative/Locking/Paper4Z5PhaseLock.name: thermodynamic_dim
RGF/Generative/Locking/Paper4Z5PhaseLock.sig: theorem thermodynamic_dim (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) : 2 * d - 1 = d + 2 ↔ d = 3

RGF/Generative/Locking/Paper4Z5PhaseLock.name: poleZ_five_injective
RGF/Generative/Locking/Paper4Z5PhaseLock.sig: theorem poleZ_five_injective : Function.Injective (fun j : Fin 5 => poleZ 5 j)
RGF/Generative/Locking/Paper4Z5PhaseLock.doc: Pole phase `e^{iπ(2j+1)/p}` of the FORS kernel (Paper 4 definition `poleZ`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: fib_eigenvector
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: The Perron eigenvector `(φ, 1)` of the Fibonacci connecting matrix, with eigenvalue the golden ratio `φ`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: emb_add
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem emb_add (p q : ℤ × ℤ) : emb (p + q) = emb p + emb q

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: emb_injective
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: `emb` is injective, so the dimension group `K₀ ≅ ℤ²` has rank `2`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: emb_mul
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem emb_mul (a b c d : ℤ) : emb (a, b) * emb (c, d) = emb (a * c + b * d, a * d + b * c + b * d)
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: The golden-ring multiplication law: the image `ℤ[φ]` is closed under multiplication, `(a+bφ)(c+dφ) = (ac+bd) + (ad+bc+bd)φ`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: caStep_shift
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem caStep_shift (rule : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool) (k : ℤ) (c : Config) : caStep rule (shiftBy k c) = shiftBy k (caStep rule c)
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: The evolution commutes with spatial translation (Curtis–Hedlund locality).

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: shiftBy_shiftBy
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem shiftBy_shiftBy (j k : ℤ) (c : Config) : shiftBy j (shiftBy k c) = shiftBy (j + k) c

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: caStep_iterate_shift
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem caStep_iterate_shift (rule : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool) (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ) (c : Config) : (caStep rule)^[n] (shiftBy k c) = shiftBy k ((caStep rule)^[n] c)
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: Iterated evolution commutes with spatial translation.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: glider_shift
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem glider_shift (rule : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool) (g : Config) (j : ℤ) (h : IsGlider rule g) : IsGlider rule (shiftBy j g)
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: The spatial translate of a glider is again a glider.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.name: static_ether
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.sig: theorem static_ether : caStep rule110 ether = ether
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseKTheory.le.doc: The all-`false` background is a static solution of Rule 110.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: stur_sum
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem stur_sum (α : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, stur α n = ⌊(N : ℝ) * α⌋
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: The mechanical / Sturmian word of slope `α`: the projected-lattice increment `stur α n = ⌊(n+1)α⌋ − ⌊nα⌋`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: stur_sum_periods
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem stur_sum_periods (α : ℝ) {p : ℕ} (hper : ∀ n, stur α (n + p) = stur α n) (k : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (k * p), stur α n = k * ∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, stur α n
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: The mechanical / Sturmian word of slope `α`: the projected-lattice increment `stur α n = ⌊(n+1)α⌋ − ⌊nα⌋`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: stur_aperiodic
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem stur_aperiodic (α : ℝ) (hα : Irrational α) : ¬ ∃ p : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n, stur α (n + p) = stur α n
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: The mechanical / Sturmian word of slope `α`: the projected-lattice increment `stur α n = ⌊(n+1)α⌋ − ⌊nα⌋`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: fibonacci_word_aperiodic
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem fibonacci_word_aperiodic : ¬ ∃ p : ℕ, 0 < p ∧ ∀ n, stur fibSlope (n + p) = stur fibSlope n
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: **Five-fold aperiodic order.** The golden-ratio ("Fibonacci") quasicrystal generated by the local cut-and-project rule is globally aperiodic — the positive counterpart of the crystallographic exclusion of five-fold symmetry from periodic lattices.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: ca_shift_equivariant
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem ca_shift_equivariant (rule : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool) (c : Config) : caStep rule (shift c) = shift (caStep rule c)
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: **Curtis–Hedlund locality / shift-equivariance.** The CA update commutes with the shift: local rules generate translation-invariant global dynamics.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: ca_deterministic
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem ca_deterministic (rule : Bool → Bool → Bool → Bool) (c d : Config) (h : c = d) (t : ℕ) : (caStep rule)^[t] c = (caStep rule)^[t] d
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: **Determinism.** The CA evolution is a genuine function of the initial configuration: equal initial data give equal trajectories.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.name: rule110_example
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.sig: theorem rule110_example : rule110 true false true = true
RGF/Generative/Locking/PenroseQuasicryst.doc: Rule 110 has the expected truth-table value on a representative input.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonComplete..name: psi_eq_goldenConj
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonComplete..doc: Bridging lemma: this module's `psi` coincides with Mathlib's `Real.goldenConj`. For use when old modules unify the golden-conjugate notation, to prevent old theorems from breaking.

RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonComplete..name: golden_pow_succ
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonComplete..sig: theorem golden_pow_succ (n : ℕ) : Real.goldenRatio ^ (n + 1) = (Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℝ) * Real.goldenRatio + (Nat.fib n : ℝ)

RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonComplete..name: psi_pow_succ
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonComplete..sig: theorem psi_pow_succ (n : ℕ) : psi ^ (n + 1) = (Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℝ) * psi + (Nat.fib n : ℝ)

RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.name: four_cos_sum_zero
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.sig: theorem four_cos_sum_zero : cos (π/5) + cos (2*π/5) + cos (3*π/5) + cos (4*π/5) = 0

RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.name: golden_sub_psi_pow
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.sig: theorem golden_sub_psi_pow (n : ℕ) : Real.goldenRatio^(n+1) - psi^(n+1) = (Nat.fib (n+1) : ℝ) * √5

RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.name: pentagon_new_identities
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.sig: theorem pentagon_new_identities : (cos (π/5) + cos (2*π/5) + cos (3*π/5) + cos (4*π/5) = 0) ∧ (Real.goldenRatio⁻¹ = Real.goldenRatio - 1) ∧ (psi = -Real.goldenRatio⁻¹) ∧ (psi = 1 - Real.goldenRatio) ∧ (16 * (cos (π/5)) ^ 4 - 12 * (cos (π/5)) ^ 2 + 1 = 0) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, Real.goldenRatio^(n+1) - psi^(n+1) = (Nat.fib (n+1) : ℝ) * √5)
RGF/Generative/Locking/PentagonNew.lean.doc: All the content of the supplementary identities. Note: the original manuscript wrote this summary theorem as `four_cos_sum_zero ∧ golden_inv_eq ∧ …`, i.e. directly using each theorem's "name (proof term)" as a conjunct. This does not type-check in Lean (`∧` expects a proposition `Prop`, while a theorem name is a proof term of some proposition), so here it is rewritten as an explicit conjunction of each proposition itself, with unchanged meaning; the proof is still provided by the corresponding already-proved theorems one by one.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: n2_eq_two_iff_k_eq_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem n2_eq_two_iff_k_eq_five (k : ℕ) (hk : Odd k) (hk3 : k ≥ 3) : L2_inv k ↔ k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: Locking condition L3 (invariant form): k is odd.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: quintic_locking_from_invariants
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem quintic_locking_from_invariants (k : ℕ) (hL1 : ¬ IsSolvable (Perm (Fin k))) (hL2 : L2_inv k) (hL3 : L3_inv k) : k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: Locking condition L3 (invariant form): k is odd.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: fiber_covers
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem fiber_covers (sys : RGFIterSystem n) (s : RGFState n) (hfp : sys.IsFixedPoint s) : s ∈ invariantFiber sys (toSignature (extractInvariants s))
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: Fibration cover: every fixed point lies in some fiber.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: fibers_disjoint
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem fibers_disjoint (sys : RGFIterSystem n) (α β : InvariantSignature) (hne : α ≠ β) : invariantFiber sys α ∩ invariantFiber sys β = ∅

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: L2_solution_set_is_five_or_six
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem L2_solution_set_is_five_or_six (k : ℕ) : L2_inv k ↔ k = 5 ∨ k = 6
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: **Sensitivity 1 — dropping oddness admits `k = 6`.** The algebraic condition `L2_inv` (`(k-1)/2 = 2`) does **not** have `{5}` as its solution set: without the extra `Odd k` hypothesis, `k = 6` satisfies it too (natural-number division). Hence `L2` alone is under-determined; the oddness assumption `L3` is genuinely load-bearing for the value `5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: six_satisfies_L2
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: `k = 6` explicitly satisfies the algebraic condition `L2`, witnessing the non-uniqueness of Part 5's `L2_solution_set_is_five_or_six`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: n2_target_is_free
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem n2_target_is_free (t : ℕ) : n2_rep (2 * t + 1) = t
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: **Sensitivity 2 — the target `n₂ = 2` is a free parameter.** Retargeting the representation-count condition to `n₂ = t` moves the (odd) solution to `2t + 1`; the choice `t = 2` (giving `5`) is not forced by the condition's form. This makes precise the sense in which the `n₂ = 2` bundle is reverse-engineered: a different but equally "natural" target yields a different `k`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: five_is_forced_by_minimality
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem five_is_forced_by_minimality (sys : RecursiveSystem) (h : FiveLockingCondition sys) : sys.k = 5
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: **The parameter-free necessity.** In contrast to the contingent algebraic bundle, the minimal-non-solvable criterion (`FiveLockingCondition`, i.e. `S_k` unsolvable and `k` least such) has `5` as its *unique* solution, with no adjustable target parameter. This is the robust, non-circular route to `k = 5`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: k_five_circularity_audit
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem k_five_circularity_audit : (∀ k, L2_inv k ↔ k = 5 ∨ k = 6) ∧ (∀ t : ℕ, n2_rep (2 * t + 1) = t) ∧ (∀ sys : RecursiveSystem, FiveLockingCondition sys → sys.k = 5)
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: **Summary: circularity audit for `k = 5`.** A single statement separating the contingent from the necessary: 1. the algebraic `L2` condition alone admits `{5, 6}` (contingent); 2. its target `n₂ = t` is a free parameter (odd solution `2t+1`, so `5` is not forced); 3. the parameter-free minimal-non-solvable criterion forces `k = 5` uniquely. Items 1–2 show the `n₂ = 2` route is premise-contingent; item 3 shows the value `5` is nonetheless a genuine necessity, sourced from the classical minimal-non-solvable group fact rather than from any reverse-engineered algebra.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: emergence_criterion_is_definitional
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem emergence_criterion_is_definitional (sys : RecursiveSystem) : EmergenceCondition sys ↔ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin sys.k))
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: **The physics→group-theory link is definitional, not derived.** The `EmergenceCondition` premise (the C1 side of the minimality route) is *by definition* the statement that `S_k` is non-solvable — the proof is `Iff.rfl`. This is the precise sense in which the solvability criterion is *not* independently justified from a more primitive generative axiom: it is inserted, by definition, as the meaning of "emergence". Consequently theorems of the shape "emergence ⟹ `S_k` non-solvable" carry no independent content, and the necessity of choosing *solvability* (rather than some other parameter-free group invariant) as *the* membrane-locking criterion remains an **open modelling problem** of the framework.

RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.name: k_five_conditional_on_solvability_criterion
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.sig: theorem k_five_conditional_on_solvability_criterion : (∀ sys : RecursiveSystem, FiveLockingCondition sys → sys.k = 5) ∧ (∀ sys : RecursiveSystem, EmergenceCondition sys ↔ ¬ IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin sys.k)))
RGF/Generative/Locking/QuinticLocking.le.doc: **Honest closure statement.** Combining the audit with the definitional observation: the value `5` is genuinely forced *once the solvability criterion is granted* (`five_is_forced_by_minimality`), but the criterion itself is granted by definition (`emergence_criterion_is_definitional`), not deduced from the generative primitives. Hence, at the current state of the formalisation, `k = 5` is a theorem *conditional on the solvability criterion*, and the necessity of that criterion is not yet closed.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: isCriticalBoundary_iff_half
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem isCriticalBoundary_iff_half (x : ℝ) : IsCriticalBoundary x ↔ x = 1 / 2

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: isCriticalBoundary_unique
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem isCriticalBoundary_unique {x y : ℝ} (hx : IsCriticalBoundary x) (hy : IsCriticalBoundary y) : x = y
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: The critical boundary is unique: any two critical boundaries coincide.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: isCriticalBoundary_ne_zero
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem isCriticalBoundary_ne_zero {x : ℝ} (hx : IsCriticalBoundary x) : x ≠ 0
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: The critical boundary is *non-zero* (so `1/2` is genuinely the unique *non-zero* self-dual fixed point, distinguishing it from the trivial value `0`).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: selfDual_scalar_lock
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem selfDual_scalar_lock (x : ℝ) : 2 * x ^ 2 = x ↔ x = 0 ∨ x = 1 / 2
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **The self-dual scalar locking condition `2x² = x`** has solution set `{0, 1/2}`, exactly mirroring the dimension-locking pattern `d(d-1) = 2d ↔ d ∈ {0, 3}` (`RGF.CritiqueResolution.dim_so_eq_dim_iff_zero_or_three`). The unique *non-zero* solution is `1/2`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: isCriticalBoundary_iff_unique_nonzero_lock
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem isCriticalBoundary_iff_unique_nonzero_lock (x : ℝ) : IsCriticalBoundary x ↔ (x ≠ 0 ∧ 2 * x ^ 2 = x)
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **Critical boundary = the unique non-zero solution of the self-dual lock.** `IsCriticalBoundary x` holds iff `x` is the unique non-zero solution of the self-dual locking condition `2x² = x`. This is the precise formal meaning of *"`x` is the unique non-zero fixed point of the self-dual locking condition"*.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: isCriticalBoundary_re_iff_selfDual
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem isCriticalBoundary_re_iff_selfDual (s : ℂ) : IsCriticalBoundary s.re ↔ s = spiralDual s
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: The complex projection: for `s : ℂ`, `Re s` is a critical boundary iff `s` is fixed by the functional-equation reflection `spiralDual s = 1 - conj s`. This is the link that makes the "locking `1/2`" and the "`ζ` `1/2`" two projections of the *same* self-dual involution.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: lock_critical_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem lock_critical_iff (normΓ : ℝ) : CriticalContraction normΓ ↔ IsCriticalBoundary normΓ
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **Locking critical ⇔ critical boundary.** The contraction is critical iff its norm is a critical boundary — the locking `1/2` is a projection of the shared self-dual predicate.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: lock_isCriticalBoundary
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: The locking critical ratio `‖Γ‖ = 1/2` *is* a critical boundary (unconditional).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: RH_critical_iff
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem RH_critical_iff : RiemannHypothesis_strip ↔ ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 → 0 < s.re → s.re < 1 → IsCriticalBoundary s.re
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **RH ⇔ "every nontrivial zero's real part is a critical boundary".** This is the blueprint's RH-side reformulation: RH (strip form) is *exactly* the statement that each nontrivial `ζ`-zero has its real part equal to a critical boundary, expressed via the *same* predicate `IsCriticalBoundary` as the locking side.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: lock_and_RH_share_critical_boundary
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem lock_and_RH_share_critical_boundary : IsCriticalBoundary (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∧ (RiemannHypothesis_strip ↔ ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 → 0 < s.re → s.re < 1 → IsCriticalBoundary s.re)
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **The bridge (strip form).** The locking ratio `‖Γ‖ = 1/2` is a critical boundary, *and* RH (strip form) is exactly the statement that every nontrivial `ζ`-zero's real part is a critical boundary. Both sides speak of the *same* predicate `IsCriticalBoundary`. This is an honest bridge: the left conjunct is unconditional, the right conjunct is an `↔` that does **not** assert RH.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: RCD_lock_bridges_RH
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem RCD_lock_bridges_RH : IsCriticalBoundary (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∧ (RiemannHypothesis ↔ ∀ s : ℂ, riemannZeta s = 0 → 0 < s.re → s.re < 1 → IsCriticalBoundary s.re)
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **The bridge (Mathlib's official `RiemannHypothesis`).** The same bridge, now connecting the locking ratio to Mathlib's full `RiemannHypothesis` via the critical-strip embedding `RGF.RiemannStatus.riemannHypothesis_iff_strip`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.name: critical_contraction_iff_RH_critical_line
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.sig: theorem critical_contraction_iff_RH_critical_line (normΓ : ℝ) : CriticalContraction normΓ ↔ IsCriticalBoundary normΓ
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFCriticalBounda.doc: **The two `1/2`'s are the same object.** Composing the locking projection with the Riemann projection: the contraction is critical (`‖Γ‖` a critical boundary) *iff* its norm equals the unique value that, when it is the real part of a nontrivial `ζ`-zero, makes that zero self-dual. Formally both reduce to the single shared predicate.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: cos_pi_div_five_val
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: cos(π/5) = (1 + √5)/4 (taken from Mathlib, recorded here as a reference).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: alpha_val
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: α = cos(2π/5) = (√5 − 1)/4. Unified deduplication: equivalent to the shared module `RGF.PentagonComplete.cos_two_pi_div_five`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: alpha_root
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: α is a root of the pentagon's quadratic equation 4x² + 2x − 1 = 0.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: cos_four_pi_div_five_val
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: cos(4π/5) = (−1 − √5)/4. Unified deduplication: directly reference the shared module `RGF.PentagonNew.cos_four_pi_div_five`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: cos_four_pi_div_five_root
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: cos(4π/5) is the second root of the same quadratic equation 4x² + 2x − 1 = 0.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: pentagon_roots_sum
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: Vieta relation: sum of the two roots = −1/2.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: pentagon_roots_prod
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: Vieta relation: product of the two roots = −1/4.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: two_cos_pi_div_five_eq_golden
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: 2·cos(π/5) = φ: the ratio diagonal/side of the regular pentagon is exactly the golden ratio.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: golden_eq_one_add_two_alpha
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: φ = 1 + 2α: the golden ratio is linearly determined by the angular-momentum coefficient α.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: golden_sq
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: φ² = φ + 1. Unified deduplication: directly reference the shared module `RGF.PentagonComplete.golden_sq_eq_golden_add_one`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: golden_pow_succ
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.sig: lemma golden_pow_succ (n : ℕ) : goldenRatio ^ (n + 1) = (Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℝ) * goldenRatio + (Nat.fib n : ℝ)
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: Fibonacci power formula of the golden ratio: φ^(n+1) = F(n+1)·φ + F(n). Unified deduplication: directly reference the shared module `RGF.PentagonComplete.golden_pow_succ`.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: zmod5_units_card
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: The order of the multiplicative unit group of ℤ/5 = 4 = φ(5).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: dihedral_five_card
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: The order of the dihedral group D₅ = 10 = 2·5 (the symmetry group of the regular pentagon).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: A5_card
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: The order of A₅ = 60.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: A5_card_eq_factorial_div
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: The order of A₅ = 5!/2.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: num2DIrreps_five
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: At the RGF locking value k = 5, the number of two-dimensional irreps n₂(5) = 2, exactly equal to the number of roots of the pentagon's quadratic 4x²+2x−1.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: pentagon_locking_unification
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.sig: theorem pentagon_locking_unification : num2DIrreps 5 = 2 ∧ Fintype.card (DihedralGroup 5) = 10 ∧ Fintype.card (ZMod 5) = 5 ∧ 4 * alpha ^ 2 + 2 * alpha - 1 = 0 ∧ goldenRatio = 1 + 2 * alpha
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: **Bridging main theorem**: the regular pentagon — golden ratio — ℤ₅ — five-fold symmetry groups converge at the RGF locking value k = 5. (i) n₂(5) = 2, exactly the number of roots of the pentagon's quadratic; (ii) the symmetry group D₅ of the regular pentagon has order 10; (iii) the five-element cyclic field ℤ₅ has cardinality 5; (iv) α = cos(2π/5) satisfies the pentagon's quadratic 4α²+2α−1 = 0; (v) the golden ratio is linearly determined by α: φ = 1 + 2α.

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: sin_mul_sin
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.sig: lemma sin_mul_sin : Real.sin (π / 5) * Real.sin (2 * π / 5) = Real.sqrt 5 / 4

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: tan_mul_tan
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.sig: lemma tan_mul_tan : Real.tan (π / 5) * Real.tan (2 * π / 5) = Real.sqrt 5

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.name: psi_sq
RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: ψ² = ψ + 1 (taken from Mathlib, recorded here as a reference).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: ψ² = ψ + 1 (taken from Mathlib, recorded here as a reference).

RGF/Generative/Locking/RGFPentagonGolden.doc: ψ² = ψ + 1 (taken from Mathlib, recorded here as a reference).
