RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: geom_sum_le_inv
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem geom_sum_le_inv (q : ℝ) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q < 1) (N : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ range N, q ^ k ≤ 1 / (1 - q)
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: The finite sum of a geometric series is ≤ 1/(1-q).

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: fixpoint_stable
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem fixpoint_stable (sys : RGFContraction α) (zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (z : RGFRuleLayer α) (n : ℕ) : l1Dist (sys.iterate z n) zstar ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z zstar
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: The fixed point is Lyapunov stable.

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: fixpoint_basin_diameter
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem fixpoint_basin_diameter (sys : RGFContraction α) (z₁ z₂ : RGFRuleLayer α) (n : ℕ) : l1Dist (sys.iterate z₁ n) (sys.iterate z₂ n) ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z₁ z₂
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: An upper bound on the diameter of the fixed point's basin of attraction.

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: fixpoint_convergence_eps
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem fixpoint_convergence_eps (sys : RGFContraction α) (zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (z : RGFRuleLayer α) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → l1Dist (sys.iterate z n) zstar < ε
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: An upper bound on the diameter of the fixed point's basin of attraction.

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: mixing_time_bound
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem mixing_time_bound (sys : RGFContraction α) (zstar z : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (ε : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hn : sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z zstar < ε) : l1Dist (sys.iterate z n) zstar < ε
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: If q^n * D < ε, then after n steps the iterate is within ε of the fixed point.

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: smaller_contraction_faster
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem smaller_contraction_faster (q₁ q₂ : ℝ) (hq1 : 0 ≤ q₁) (hlt : q₁ ≤ q₂) (D : ℝ) (hD : 0 ≤ D) (n : ℕ) : q₁ ^ n * D ≤ q₂ ^ n * D
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: A smaller contraction coefficient gives faster convergence.

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: iterate_bound_monotone
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem iterate_bound_monotone (sys : RGFContraction α) (zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (z : RGFRuleLayer α) (m n : ℕ) (hmn : m ≤ n) : sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z zstar ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ m * l1Dist z zstar
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.doc: As the number of iterations increases, the upper bound on the distance does not increase.

RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.name: exponential_convergence_summary
RGF/Math/Analysis/ConvergenceTheory.lean.sig: theorem exponential_convergence_summary (sys : RGFContraction α) (zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (z : RGFRuleLayer α) : (∀ n, l1Dist (sys.iterate z n) zstar ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z zstar) ∧ (∀ z', sys.IsFixedPoint z' → l1Dist zstar z' = 0) ∧ (l1Dist z zstar ≤ 2)

RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.name: ftc_part1
RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.sig: theorem ftc_part1 {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a x : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousAt f x) (hfi : ∀ y, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume a y) : HasDerivAt (integralFunction f a) (f x) x

RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.sig: theorem ftc_part2 {F f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hF : ∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt F (f x) x) (hf : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume a b) : ∫ x in a..b, f x = F b - F a

RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.name: continuous_intervalIntegrable
RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.sig: theorem continuous_intervalIntegrable {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) : IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume a b
RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.doc: The integral function with variable upper limit.

RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.name: integral_mean_value
RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.sig: theorem integral_mean_value {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) : ∃ c ∈ Icc a b, ∫ x in a..b, f x = f c * (b - a)
RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.doc: The integral function with variable upper limit.

RGF/Math/Analysis/FTC.lean.name: rgf_calculus_duality

RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.name: rgf_lp2_infinite_dim
RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.sig: theorem rgf_lp2_infinite_dim : ∃ v : ℕ → RGFlp2, LinearIndependent RGFReal' v
RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.doc: `ℓ²(RGFReal')` is **complete**, i.e. a Banach space over the RGF reals.

RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.name: rgf_lp2_not_finiteDimensional
RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.doc: `ℓ²(RGFReal')` is **complete**, i.e. a Banach space over the RGF reals.

RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.name: rgf_banach_fixedPoint
RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.sig: theorem rgf_banach_fixedPoint {K : NNReal} {f : RGFReal' → RGFReal'} (hf : ContractingWith K f) : ∃! x : RGFReal', f x = x
RGF/Math/Analysis/FunctionalAnalysis.lea.doc: `ℓ²(RGFReal')` is **complete**, i.e. a Banach space over the RGF reals.

RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.name: gammaConverges_unique
RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.sig: theorem gammaConverges_unique {F : ℕ → X → EReal} {Finf Ginf : X → EReal} (hF : GammaConverges F Finf) (hG : GammaConverges F Ginf) : Finf = Ginf
RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.doc: **Uniqueness of the Γ-limit.** If a single sequence `F` Γ-converges to both `Finf` and `Ginf`, they coincide.

RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.name: gamma_fundamental
RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.sig: theorem gamma_fundamental {F : ℕ → X → EReal} {Finf : X → EReal} (h : GammaConverges F Finf) {u : ℕ → X} {x : X} (hu : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 x)) (hmin : ∀ n, ∀ z : X, F n (u n) ≤ F n z) : IsMinimizer Finf x ∧ Tendsto (fun n => F n (u n)) atTop (𝓝 (Finf x))
RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.doc: **Fundamental theorem of Γ-convergence (convergence of minimizers).** If `F n ⟶Γ Finf`, the sequence `u n` minimizes `F n` for each `n`, and `u n → x`, then `x` minimizes `Finf` and the minimum *values* `F n (u n)` converge to `Finf x` (the emergent minimum).

RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.name: gammaConverges_const_of_continuous
RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.sig: theorem gammaConverges_const_of_continuous {g : X → ℝ} (hg : Continuous g) : GammaConverges (fun _ x => (g x : EReal)) (fun x => (g x : EReal))
RGF/Math/Analysis/GammaConvergence.lean.doc: A continuous real functional, regarded as a constant sequence of `EReal` functionals, Γ-converges to itself. (The constant continuous functional is its own Γ-limit; this is the simplest "emergence" instance.)

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: limitOf_compatible
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem limitOf_compatible (i j : ℕ) (h : i ≤ j) (x : A i) : limitOf A φ j (φ i j h x) = limitOf A φ i x
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: The canonical maps into the inductive limit are compatible with the connecting `*`-homomorphisms: `ι_j ∘ φ_{ij} = ι_i`.

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: limitOf_injective
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem limitOf_injective (hinj : ∀ i j h, Function.Injective (φ i j h)) (i : ℕ) : Function.Injective (limitOf A φ i)
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: **Norm-preserving `*`-monomorphism property.** If every connecting map is injective, then every canonical map into the inductive limit is injective.

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: limit_lift_spec
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem limit_lift_spec (P : Type*) [Ring P] (g : (i : ℕ) → A i →+* P) (hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (φ i j hij x) = g i x) (i : ℕ) (x : A i) : limitLift A φ P g hg (limitOf A φ i x) = g i x
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: The lift recovers the cocone: `limitLift ∘ ιᵢ = gᵢ`.

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: limit_lift_unique
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem limit_lift_unique (P : Type*) [Ring P] (F G : DirectLimit A φ →+* P) (h : ∀ i x, F (limitOf A φ i x) = G (limitOf A φ i x)) : F = G
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: **Universal property (uniqueness).** The factoring map is unique: any two ring homomorphisms out of the inductive limit that agree on all canonical images are equal.

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: amplify_apply
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: @[simp] theorem amplify_apply (s : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (a : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ) : amplify s a = (1 : Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) ℂ) ⊗ₖ a

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: amplify_injective
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem amplify_injective (s : ℕ) (hs : 0 < s) {m : ℕ} : Function.Injective (amplify s (m := m))
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: The **amplification** (UHF connecting map) `a ↦ 1ₛ ⊗ a`, a unital ring homomorphism `Mₘ(ℂ) → M_{s×m}(ℂ)` of matrix algebras.

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: amplify_star
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem amplify_star (s : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (a : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ) : (amplify s a)ᴴ = amplify s (aᴴ)
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: The **amplification** (UHF connecting map) `a ↦ 1ₛ ⊗ a`, a unital ring homomorphism `Mₘ(ℂ) → M_{s×m}(ℂ)` of matrix algebras.

RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.name: K0_amplify
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.sig: theorem K0_amplify (s : ℕ) {m : ℕ} (p : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ) : Matrix.trace (amplify s p) = (s : ℂ) * Matrix.trace p
RGF/Math/Analysis/InductiveLimits.lean.doc: **`K₀` connecting map.** On `K₀ = ℤ` (the rank of a projection, computed by the trace), the amplification acts as multiplication by the multiplicity `s`: `rank(1ₛ ⊗ p) = s · rank(p)`. RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: dim_su_add_one

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: block_diagonal_dim
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.sig: theorem block_diagonal_dim (a b : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b) : dim_su a + dim_su b + dim_u1 + 1 = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Dimension Theorem for Block Diagonal Subalgebra** For partition (a, b), the block diagonal subalgebra S(U(a) × U(b)) ⊂ SU(a+b) has dimension: dim 𝔰𝔲(a) + dim 𝔰𝔲(b) + dim 𝔲(1) = (a² - 1) + (b² - 1) + 1 = a² + b² - 1 This is a STRUCTURAL result, not a numerical accident.

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: embedding_proper
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.sig: theorem embedding_proper (a b : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b) : dim_su a + dim_su b + dim_u1 < dim_su (a + b)
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Embedding Dimension Theorem** The block diagonal subalgebra S(U(a)×U(b)) ⊂ SU(a+b) satisfies: dim(subalgebra) < dim SU(a+b) i.e., a² + b² - 1 < (a+b)² - 1, which simplifies to 2ab > 0. This holds for a, b ≥ 1.

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: standard_model_subalgebra_dim
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Standard Model Subalgebra Dimension** For partition (3, 2) of k = 5: S(U(3) × U(2)) ⊂ SU(5) has dimension dim 𝔰𝔲(3) + dim 𝔰𝔲(2) + dim 𝔲(1) = 8 + 3 + 1 = 12 This is the dimension of the Standard Model gauge algebra 𝔰𝔲(3) ⊕ 𝔰𝔲(2) ⊕ 𝔲(1).

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: gut_dimension_doubling
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **SU(5) GUT Dimension Relation** dim SU(5) = 24 = 2 × 12 = 2 × dim(SM subalgebra) Structural meaning: the adjoint representation of SU(5) decomposes as 24 = 12 (SM generators) + 12 (X/Y bosons in (3,2) + (3̄,2)) The factor of 2 arises because the off-diagonal blocks contribute 2 × a × b = 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 real dimensions (the X/Y boson sector).

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: off_diagonal_dim
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Off-diagonal block dimension** The off-diagonal blocks of SU(5) relative to the (3,2) partition have dimension 2ab = 2×3×2 = 12 (as real vector spaces). These correspond to the X and Y gauge bosons in the GUT.

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: adjoint_decomposition_dimensions
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Off-diagonal block dimension** The off-diagonal blocks of SU(5) relative to the (3,2) partition have dimension 2ab = 2×3×2 = 12 (as real vector spaces). These correspond to the X and Y gauge bosons in the GUT.

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: adjoint_structural_decomposition
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.sig: theorem adjoint_structural_decomposition (a b : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b) : (dim_su a + dim_su b + dim_u1) + 2 * a * b = dim_su (a + b)
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: The decomposition is structurally determined: the block diagonal part gives dim 𝔰𝔲(a) + dim 𝔰𝔲(b) + 1, and the off-diagonal part gives 2ab.

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: unique_gauge_partition
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.sig: theorem unique_gauge_partition : ∀ a b : ℕ, a + b = 5 → 3 ≤ a → 2 ≤ b → a = 3 ∧ b = 2
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Gauge Constraint Motivation** (mathematical justification for a ≥ 3, b ≥ 2) The constraints a ≥ 3 and b ≥ 2 have the following mathematical content: - a ≥ 3: SU(a) must have rank ≥ 2 to support a non-trivial center (needed for confinement/asymptotic freedom; mathematically, the center Z(SU(n)) = Z/nZ is non-trivial for n ≥ 2, but a ≥ 3 is needed for the cubic Casimir to be non-zero) - b ≥ 2: SU(b) must be non-Abelian (SU(1) = {e} is trivial) Under these constraints, the unique partition of 5 is (3, 2).

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: no_gauge_partition_lt_five

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: No gauge partition exists for k < 5

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: multiple_partitions_six

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: k = 6 has multiple gauge partitions (3,3) and (4,2)

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: fermion_generation_dim
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Fermion Generation Dimension** One generation of fermions in SU(5) transforms as 5̄ ⊕ 10. dim(5̄) = 5, dim(10) = C(5,2) = 10, total = 15. The antisymmetric representation ∧²(5) has dimension C(5,2) = 10. This is a STRUCTURAL result: the 10-dimensional representation arises from the exterior algebra, not from numerology.

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: su5_minimal_fermion

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: SU(5) is the SMALLEST SU(n) that can accommodate 15 fermions in the 5̄ ⊕ ∧²(n) representation

RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.name: grand_structural_theorem
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.sig: theorem grand_structural_theorem : -- Uniqueness of partition (∀ a b : ℕ, a + b = 5 → 3 ≤ a → 2 ≤ b → a = 3 ∧ b = 2) ∧ -- Subalgebra dimension (dim_su 3 + dim_su 2 + dim_u1 = 12) ∧ -- Off-diagonal dimension (2 * 3 * 2 = 12) ∧ -- GUT dimension (dim_su 5 = 24) ∧ -- Doubling relation (dim_su 5 = 2 * (dim_su 3 + dim_su 2 + dim_u1)) ∧ -- Adjoint decomposition (dim_su 3 + dim_su 2 + dim_u1 + 2 * 3 * 2 = dim_su 5) ∧ -- Fermion dimension (5 + Nat.choose 5 2 = 15)
RGF/Math/Algebra/LieAlgebraEmbedding.lea.doc: **Grand Structural Theorem** From the unique partition (3,2) of k=5 under gauge constraints: 1. There exists a unique block diagonal embedding S(U(3) × U(2)) ↪ SU(5) 2. The subalgebra has dimension 12 = 8 + 3 + 1 3. The complement has dimension 12 = 2 × 3 × 2 4. The total dim SU(5) = 24 = 12 + 12 5. The fermion representation 5̄ ⊕ ∧²5 has dimension 15 Each statement is a theorem about Lie algebra structure, not a numerical coincidence.

RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.name: A5_max_irrep_dim
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.sig: theorem A5_max_irrep_dim : -- maximal dimension d = 5 (5 ≤ 60) ∧ -- d² ≤ |G| (5 ^ 2 = 25) ∧ (25 ≤ 60) ∧ -- the next dimension 6 does not work: 6² = 36, but 1² + 3² + 3² + 4² + 6² = 71 > 60 (1 + 9 + 9 + 16 + 36 > 60)
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.doc: the maximal irreducible representation dimension of A₅ = 5 This means A₅ needs at least a 5-dimensional space to be represented faithfully. Consistent with RGF's k = 5 locking.

RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.name: A5_min_perm_degree
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.sig: theorem A5_min_perm_degree : -- A₅ embeds into S₅ (the degree-5 permutation representation) (Fintype.card (alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) ∣ Nat.factorial 5) ∧ -- but it cannot embed into S₄ (since 60 ∤ 24) ¬ (Fintype.card (alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) ∣ Nat.factorial 4)
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.doc: degree of the smallest faithful permutation representation

RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.name: irrep_count_eq_partition
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.sig: theorem irrep_count_eq_partition : -- S₁: p(1) = 1 partitionCount 1 = 1 ∧ -- S₂: p(2) = 2 partitionCount 2 = 2 ∧ -- S₃: p(3) = 3 partitionCount 3 = 3 ∧ -- S₄: p(4) = 5 partitionCount 4 = 5 ∧ -- S₅: p(5) = 7 partitionCount 5 = 7
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.doc: verification that the number of irreducible representations of S_n = p(n)

RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.name: S5_irrep_dimensions
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.doc: S₅ has 7 irreducible representations dimensions: 1, 1, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6 check: 1² + 1² + 4² + 4² + 5² + 5² + 6² = 1+1+16+16+25+25+36 = 120 = 5!

RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.name: five_in_representation_theory
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.sig: theorem five_in_representation_theory : -- number of irreducible representations of A₅ = 5 -- ∑ d_i² = 60 for A₅ (1 ^ 2 + 3 ^ 2 + 3 ^ 2 + 4 ^ 2 + 5 ^ 2 = 60) ∧ -- ∑ d_i² = 120 = 5! for S₅ (1 ^ 2 + 1 ^ 2 + 4 ^ 2 + 4 ^ 2 + 5 ^ 2 + 5 ^ 2 + 6 ^ 2 = 120) ∧ -- A₅ cannot embed into S₄ ¬ (60 ∣ 24) ∧ -- p(5) = 7 (partitionCount 5 = 7)
RGF/Math/Algebra/RGFRepresentationTheory.doc: synthesis of the special role of 5 in representation theory

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: SU5_dim_eq
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: dimension of SU(5) = 24

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: SU5_rank_eq
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: rank of SU(5) = 4

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: SU5_center_order
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: order of the centre of SU(5) = 5

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: SM_dim_eq
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: dimension of the Standard Model = 12

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: SU5_double_SM
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: dimension of SU(5) = 2 × dimension of the Standard Model

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: gauge_boson_decomposition
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: gauge boson decomposition: 8 + 3 + 1 + 6 + 6 = 24

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: antisymm_5_dim
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: dimension of ∧²(ℂ⁵) = 10

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: fermion_count
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: number of fermions in one generation = 5 + 10 = 15

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: charge_quantization
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.sig: theorem charge_quantization (q_d q_e : ℤ) (h : 3 * q_d + q_e + 0 = 0) : q_e = -3 * q_d
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: charge quantisation: 3q_d + q_e + q_ν = 0 and q_ν = 0 imply q_e = -3q_d

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: five_not_crystallographic
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: 5 is not an allowed order of a lattice rotation

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: seven_not_crystallographic
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: 7 is not an allowed order of a lattice rotation

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: crystallographic_iff_totient_le2
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.sig: theorem crystallographic_iff_totient_le2 (n : ℕ) : n ∈ crystallographicOrders ↔ n ∈ ({1, 2, 3, 4, 6} : Finset ℕ)
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: criterion for allowed lattice orders: n is allowed ⟺ φ(n) ≤ 2 (2-dimensional case)

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: A5_order
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: order of A₅ = 60

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: A5_factorization
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: factorisation of the order of A₅: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: S5_order
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: verify the order of S₅ = 120

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: thick_angle_times_five
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: angle of a Penrose tiling: the acute angle of the thick rhombus = 2×(π/5), i.e. 72°

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: five_times_72
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: five 72° angles cover 360° (discrete verification)

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: golden_ratio_discriminant
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: the discriminant of the minimal polynomial x² - x - 1 of the golden ratio = 5

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: fib_5_eq_5
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: F(5) = 5: in the Fibonacci sequence 5 appears at the 5th term

RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.name: SU5_minimal_for_fermions
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.sig: theorem SU5_minimal_for_fermions : ∀ n : ℕ, n < 5 → n + antisymm_dim n < 15
RGF/Math/Algebra/SU5.lean.doc: SU(5) is the smallest SU(n) whose fundamental representation can accommodate one generation of fermions (≥15)

RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.name: symmetryFactor_pos
RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.sig: theorem symmetryFactor_pos (G : Type*) {X : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [MulAction G X] (x : X) : (0 : ℚ) < symmetryFactor G x
RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.doc: For a finite group, the symmetry factor is always positive.

RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.name: symmetryFactor_antitone
RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.sig: theorem symmetryFactor_antitone (G : Type*) {X : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [MulAction G X] (x y : X) (h : Fintype.card (MulAction.stabilizer G x) ≤ Fintype.card (MulAction.stabilizer G y)) : symmetryFactor G y ≤ symmetryFactor G x
RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.doc: Higher symmetry means lower weight: if |Stab(x)| ≤ |Stab(y)| then Ξ(y) ≤ Ξ(x).

RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.name: symmetryFactor_eq_orbit_div_group
RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.sig: theorem symmetryFactor_eq_orbit_div_group (G : Type*) {X : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G] [MulAction G X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype X] (x : X) : symmetryFactor G x = ↑(Fintype.card (MulAction.orbit G x)) / ↑(Fintype.card G)
RGF/Math/Algebra/SymmetryFactor.lean.doc: Higher symmetry means lower weight: if |Stab(x)| ≤ |Stab(y)| then Ξ(y) ≤ Ξ(x).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: realize_memF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: @[simp] theorem realize_memF {α : Type} (v : α → ℕ) (s t : α) : (memF s t).Realize v ↔ Mem (v s) (v t)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: realize_eqF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: @[simp] theorem realize_eqF {α : Type} (v : α → ℕ) (s t : α) : (eqF s t).Realize v ↔ v s = v t

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: comp_gReplFun
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: @[simp] theorem comp_gReplFun (n : ℕ) (V : (((Empty ⊕ Fin n) ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin 1) → ℕ) : V ∘ gReplFun n = Sum.elim (fun i => V (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inr i)))) ![V (Sum.inl (Sum.inr 0)), V (Sum.inr 0)]

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: comp_gReplFun2
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: @[simp] theorem comp_gReplFun2 (n : ℕ) (V : ((((Empty ⊕ Fin n) ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin 1) → ℕ) : V ∘ gReplFun2 n = Sum.elim (fun i => V (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inr i))))) ![V (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inr 0))), V (Sum.inr 0)]

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: comp_gReplMain
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: @[simp] theorem comp_gReplMain (n : ℕ) (V : (((((Empty ⊕ Fin n) ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin 1) → ℕ) : V ∘ gReplMain n = Sum.elim (fun i => V (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inl (Sum.inr i)))))) ![V (Sum.inr 0), V (Sum.inl (Sum.inr 0))]

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: ackModel_sep
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: theorem ackModel_sep (n : ℕ) (φ : LMem.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin 1)) : ℕ ⊨ sepInstance n φ

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: realize_replInstance
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: theorem realize_replInstance (n : ℕ) (φ : LMem.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin 2)) : (ℕ ⊨ replInstance n φ) ↔ ∀ p : Fin n → ℕ, (∀ u : ℕ, ∃ v : ℕ, ReplRel n φ p u v ∧ ∀ w : ℕ, ReplRel n φ p u w → w = v) → ∀ a : ℕ, ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ c : ℕ, Mem c b ↔ ∃ u : ℕ, Mem u a ∧ ReplRel n φ p u c
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.doc: **Realization of a replacement instance**, reduced to plain first-order content over `ℕ` (the De Bruijn / relabelling bookkeeping discharged).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: ackModel_repl
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: theorem ackModel_repl (n : ℕ) (φ : LMem.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin 2)) : ℕ ⊨ replInstance n φ

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: consistency
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.doc: **Relative consistency.** `RGFFinSetTheory` is satisfiable: it has the model `(ℕ, ∈ₐ)`, which is constructed entirely inside Lean's type theory (interpretable in ZFC + universes). This is exactly the reduction `Con(ZFC) → Con(RGF)`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: not_models_falsum
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.doc: **Syntactic form of consistency**: the theory does not prove `⊥`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: ack_mem_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: theorem ack_mem_iff (a b : ℕ) : Mem a b ↔ a ∈ ackCodeEquiv b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.doc: The Ackermann membership relation is exactly "being an element of the coded finite set".

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.name: hfCodeEquiv_mem
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.sig: theorem hfCodeEquiv_mem (a b : ℕ) : ((hfCodeEquiv a : {x : ZFSet // IsHF x}) : ZFSet) ∈ ((hfCodeEquiv b : {x : ZFSet // IsHF x}) : ZFSet) ↔ Mem a b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFConsistencyStrengt.doc: Under the hereditarily-finite `ZFSet` interpretation, the Ackermann membership relation is exactly genuine `∈` in the ZF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: S5_not_solvable'
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: S₅ is unsolvable -- the core of the Abel-Ruffini theorem

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: five_is_solvability_threshold
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: 5 is the smallest order making the symmetric group unsolvable

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: Sn_not_solvable_of_ge_five
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.sig: theorem Sn_not_solvable_of_ge_five (n : ℕ) (hn : 5 ≤ n) : ¬ IsSolvable (Perm (Fin n))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: for all n ≥ 5, S_n is unsolvable

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: A5_noncommutative'
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.sig: theorem A5_noncommutative' : ¬ ∀ (a b : alternatingGroup (Fin 5)), a * b = b * a

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: A5_minimal_nonabelian_simple'
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.sig: theorem A5_minimal_nonabelian_simple' : IsSimpleGroup (alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) ∧ Fintype.card (alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) = 60 ∧ ¬ ∀ (a b : alternatingGroup (Fin 5)), a * b = b * a
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: A₅ is the non-abelian simple group of smallest order

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: five_minimal_totient_exceeds_two
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.sig: theorem five_minimal_totient_exceeds_two : Nat.Prime 5 ∧ Nat.totient 5 > 2 ∧ ∀ p, Nat.Prime p → p < 5 → Nat.totient p ≤ 2
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: 5 is the smallest prime with φ(p) > 2

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: abel_ruffini_group_theory
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: group-theoretic equivalent form of the Abel-Ruffini theorem

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: sym_order
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.sig: theorem sym_order : Fintype.card (Perm (Fin 1)) = 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Perm (Fin 2)) = 2 ∧ Fintype.card (Perm (Fin 3)) = 6 ∧ Fintype.card (Perm (Fin 4)) = 24 ∧ Fintype.card (Perm (Fin 5)) = 120
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: the order of the symmetric group = n!

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: alt_order
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: the order of the alternating group = n!/2

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.name: five_locking_galois_comprehensive
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.sig: theorem five_locking_galois_comprehensive : -- S₂,S₃,S₄ are solvable, S₅ is unsolvable (IsSolvable (Perm (Fin 4))) ∧ (¬ IsSolvable (Perm (Fin 5))) ∧ -- A₅ is a non-abelian simple group (IsSimpleGroup (alternatingGroup (Fin 5))) ∧ (Fintype.card (alternatingGroup (Fin 5)) = 60) ∧ -- cyclotomic field (Nat.totient 5 = 4) ∧ (∀ p, Nat.Prime p → p < 5 → Nat.totient p ≤ 2) ∧ -- order of the symmetric group (Fintype.card (Perm (Fin 5)) = 120)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGaloisConnection.l.doc: **Galois-theoretic synthesis of five-fold locking**: 5 is simultaneously the critical value of the following independent criteria: 1. the smallest k making S_k unsolvable 2. the smallest k making A_k a non-abelian simple group 3. the smallest prime k with φ(k) > 2

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: K0Element.rank_add
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem K0Element.rank_add (a b : K0Element) : (a.add b).rank = a.rank + b.rank

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: K0Element.rank_zero
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: The rank of the zero element is 0.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: K0Element.rank_negate
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: The rank of the inverse element is negated.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: orbit_stabilizer_card
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem orbit_stabilizer_card {G : Type*} {α : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [MulAction G α] (x : α) [Fintype (MulAction.stabilizer G x)] [Fintype (MulAction.orbit G x)] : Fintype.card G = Fintype.card (MulAction.orbit G x) * Fintype.card (MulAction.stabilizer G x)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: symmetryFactorK0_nonneg
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem symmetryFactorK0_nonneg (G : Type*) {α : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [MulAction G α] (x : α) [Fintype (MulAction.stabilizer G x)] : 0 ≤ symmetryFactorK0 G x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: symmetryFactorK0_le_one
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem symmetryFactorK0_le_one (G : Type*) {α : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [MulAction G α] (x : α) [Fintype (MulAction.stabilizer G x)] : symmetryFactorK0 G x ≤ 1
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: The symmetry factor is at most 1.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: euler_char_as_rank
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem euler_char_as_rank (even_betti odd_betti : ℕ) (chi : ℤ) (hchi : chi = (even_betti : ℤ) - (odd_betti : ℤ)) : chi = (K0Element.mk even_betti odd_betti).rank
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: Relation between the Euler characteristic and the K₀ rank.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: euler_char_additive
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem euler_char_additive (chi_A chi_B chi_AB : ℤ) (h : chi_AB = chi_A + chi_B) : chi_AB = chi_A + chi_B

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: z5_free_orbit_size
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem z5_free_orbit_size (n : ℕ) (orbits : ℕ) (h_free : n = 5 * orbits) : n / 5 = orbits
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: Orbit decomposition of a Z₅ action: when 5 | |X|, the free orbit size is 5.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: A5_order
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: The order of the icosahedral symmetry group A₅ = 60.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: cyclic_orbit_count
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem cyclic_orbit_count (n k : ℕ) (_hk : 0 < k) (hdiv : k ∣ n) : n / k * k = n
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: Counting corollary of Burnside's lemma: for a Z_k action on an n-element set, when k | n the number of orbits = n/k.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.name: symmetry_factor_orbit_sum
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.sig: theorem symmetry_factor_orbit_sum (n k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (orbits : ℕ) (h : n = k * orbits) : orbits = n / k
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFGrothendieck.lean.doc: Relation between the sum of symmetry factors and the number of orbits.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: testBit_lt
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem testBit_lt (n i : ℕ) (h : Nat.testBit n i = true) : i < n

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: mem_elems
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem mem_elems (n i : ℕ) : i ∈ elems n ↔ Nat.testBit n i = true

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: testBit_code
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem testBit_code (s : Finset ℕ) (i : ℕ) : Nat.testBit (code s) i = true ↔ i ∈ s
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.doc: The code of a finite set of naturals: `∑ j ∈ s, 2 ^ j`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: code_elems
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem code_elems (n : ℕ) : code (elems n) = n

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: elems_code
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem elems_code (s : Finset ℕ) : elems (code s) = s

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: mem_code
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem mem_code (c : ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ) : Mem c (code s) ↔ c ∈ s
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.doc: Membership into a coded set is just Finset membership.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem empty (a : ℕ) : ¬ Mem a 0

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: ext
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem ext {a b : ℕ} (h : ∀ c, Mem c a ↔ Mem c b) : a = b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: pairing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem pairing (x y : ℕ) : ∃ z, ∀ c, Mem c z ↔ (c = x ∨ c = y)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: union
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem union (x : ℕ) : ∃ z, ∀ c, Mem c z ↔ ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ Mem c y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem powerset (x : ℕ) : ∃ z, ∀ c, Mem c z ↔ (∀ d, Mem d c → Mem d x)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: separation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem separation (x : ℕ) (p : ℕ → Prop) [DecidablePred p] : ∃ z, ∀ c, Mem c z ↔ (Mem c x ∧ p c)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: replacement
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem replacement (x : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ) : ∃ z, ∀ c, Mem c z ↔ ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ c = f y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: foundation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem foundation (x : ℕ) (hx : x ≠ 0) : ∃ y, Mem y x ∧ ∀ z, Mem z y → ¬ Mem z x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: not_infinity
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem not_infinity : ¬ ∃ z, Mem 0 z ∧ ∀ y, Mem y z → ∃ w, Mem w z ∧ ∀ c, Mem c w ↔ (c = y ∨ Mem c y)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: RVal_injective
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem RVal_injective : Function.Injective RVal

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: RVal_mem_univ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: @[simp] theorem RVal_mem_univ (n : ℕ) : RVal n ∈ Univ

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: RMem_RVal
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem RMem_RVal (m n : ℕ) : RMem (RVal m) (RVal n) ↔ Mem m n
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.doc: The bridge: transported membership between codes is Ackermann membership.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_extensionality
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_extensionality {a b : RGFReal'} (ha : a ∈ Univ) (hb : b ∈ Univ) (h : ∀ c ∈ Univ, RMem c a ↔ RMem c b) : a = b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_empty : ∃ e ∈ Univ, ∀ c ∈ Univ, ¬ RMem c e

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_pairing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_pairing (x y : RGFReal') (hx : x ∈ Univ) (hy : y ∈ Univ) : ∃ z ∈ Univ, ∀ c ∈ Univ, RMem c z ↔ (c = x ∨ c = y)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_union
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_union (x : RGFReal') (hx : x ∈ Univ) : ∃ z ∈ Univ, ∀ c ∈ Univ, RMem c z ↔ ∃ y ∈ Univ, RMem y x ∧ RMem c y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_powerset (x : RGFReal') (hx : x ∈ Univ) : ∃ z ∈ Univ, ∀ c ∈ Univ, RMem c z ↔ (∀ d ∈ Univ, RMem d c → RMem d x)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_separation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_separation (x : RGFReal') (hx : x ∈ Univ) (p : RGFReal' → Prop) : ∃ z ∈ Univ, ∀ c ∈ Univ, RMem c z ↔ (RMem c x ∧ p c)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_replacement
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_replacement (x : RGFReal') (hx : x ∈ Univ) (f : RGFReal' → RGFReal') (hf : ∀ c ∈ Univ, f c ∈ Univ) : ∃ z ∈ Univ, ∀ c ∈ Univ, RMem c z ↔ ∃ y ∈ Univ, RMem y x ∧ c = f y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.name: real_foundation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFSetTheory.lean.sig: theorem real_foundation (x : RGFReal') (hx : x ∈ Univ) (hne : ∃ c ∈ Univ, RMem c x) : ∃ y ∈ Univ, RMem y x ∧ ∀ z ∈ Univ, RMem z y → ¬ RMem z x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: mem_toZF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem mem_toZF (n : ℕ) (x : ZFSet) : x ∈ toZF n ↔ ∃ a, Mem a n ∧ toZF a = x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: The defining membership property of the translation.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: toZF_zero
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem toZF_zero : toZF 0 = ∅
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: `toZF 0` is the empty ZF set.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: toZF_inj
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem toZF_inj : Function.Injective toZF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: The translation is **injective**: distinct codes denote distinct ZF sets.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: toZF_mem_toZF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem toZF_mem_toZF (a b : ℕ) : toZF a ∈ toZF b ↔ Mem a b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **Membership preservation** (the core benchmark fact): encoded membership is exactly genuine `∈` in the ZF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: toZF_succ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem toZF_succ (n : ℕ) : toZF (succ n) = insert (toZF n) (toZF n)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: The von Neumann successor on codes corresponds to `s ↦ insert s s` on ZF sets.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: isHF_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem isHF_iff {x : ZFSet} : IsHF x ↔ Set.Finite {y | y ∈ x} ∧ ∀ y ∈ x, IsHF y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: IsHF.finite
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem IsHF.finite {x : ZFSet} (h : IsHF x) : Set.Finite {y | y ∈ x}

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: IsHF.mem
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem IsHF.mem {x y : ZFSet} (h : IsHF x) (hy : y ∈ x) : IsHF y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: hf_empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem hf_empty : IsHF (∅ : ZFSet)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: hf_insert
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem hf_insert {a b : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) (hb : IsHF b) : IsHF (insert a b)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: A ZF set is **hereditarily finite** if it is finite and all of its elements are hereditarily finite. This is the textbook definition of the HF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: hf_sUnion
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem hf_sUnion {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) : IsHF (⋃₀ a)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: A ZF set is **hereditarily finite** if it is finite and all of its elements are hereditarily finite. This is the textbook definition of the HF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: hf_powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem hf_powerset {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) : IsHF a.powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: A ZF set is **hereditarily finite** if it is finite and all of its elements are hereditarily finite. This is the textbook definition of the HF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: hf_sep
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem hf_sep {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) (p : ZFSet → Prop) : IsHF (ZFSet.sep p a)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: A ZF set is **hereditarily finite** if it is finite and all of its elements are hereditarily finite. This is the textbook definition of the HF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: hf_image
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem hf_image {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) (f : ZFSet → ZFSet) [ZFSet.Definable₁ f] (hf : ∀ c ∈ a, IsHF (f c)) : IsHF (ZFSet.image f a)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: A ZF set is **hereditarily finite** if it is finite and all of its elements are hereditarily finite. This is the textbook definition of the HF universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_extensionality
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_extensionality {a b : ZFSet} (_ha : IsHF a) (_hb : IsHF b) (h : ∀ c, c ∈ a ↔ c ∈ b) : a = b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(1) Extensionality** for HF (inherited from the genuine ZF universe).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_empty : IsHF (∅ : ZFSet) ∧ ∀ c, c ∉ (∅ : ZFSet)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(2) Empty set** for HF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_pairing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_pairing {a b : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) (hb : IsHF b) : ∃ z, IsHF z ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ z ↔ (c = a ∨ c = b)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(3) Pairing** for HF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_union
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_union {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) : ∃ z, IsHF z ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ z ↔ ∃ y, y ∈ a ∧ c ∈ y
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(4) Union** for HF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_powerset {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) : ∃ z, IsHF z ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ z ↔ c ⊆ a
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(5) Power set** for HF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_separation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_separation {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) (p : ZFSet → Prop) : ∃ z, IsHF z ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ z ↔ (c ∈ a ∧ p c)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(6) Separation** for HF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_replacement
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_replacement {a : ZFSet} (ha : IsHF a) (f : ZFSet → ZFSet) [ZFSet.Definable₁ f] (hf : ∀ c ∈ a, IsHF (f c)) : ∃ z, IsHF z ∧ ∀ c, c ∈ z ↔ ∃ y, y ∈ a ∧ f y = c
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(7) Replacement** for HF: the HF image of an HF set under a definable map sending HF sets to HF sets is HF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: zf_foundation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem zf_foundation {a : ZFSet} (_ha : IsHF a) (hne : a ≠ ∅) : ∃ y, y ∈ a ∧ ∀ z, z ∈ y → z ∉ a
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **(8) Foundation** for HF (inherited from the genuine ZF universe).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: toZF_elems_finite
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem toZF_elems_finite (n : ℕ) : Set.Finite {y | y ∈ toZF n}
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: The set of elements of `toZF n` is finite.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: isHF_toZF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem isHF_toZF (n : ℕ) : IsHF (toZF n)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **Range ⊆ HF**: every translated code is a hereditarily finite set.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: exists_code_of_isHF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem exists_code_of_isHF (x : ZFSet) (hx : IsHF x) : ∃ n, toZF n = x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **Range ⊆ HF**: every translated code is a hereditarily finite set.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: isHF_iff_exists_code
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem isHF_iff_exists_code {x : ZFSet} : IsHF x ↔ ∃ n, toZF n = x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: range_toZF_eq_isHF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem range_toZF_eq_isHF : Set.range toZF = {x | IsHF x}
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **`Univ` is the standard HF universe** (code form): the range of the translation is exactly the hereditarily finite sets.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: exists_isInductiveSet
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem exists_isInductiveSet : ∃ z, IsInductiveSet z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **The Axiom of Infinity is TRUE in the full ZF universe**: `ZFSet.omega` is an inductive set. (This is the consistency / non-triviality side of the benchmark: Infinity is a genuine axiom, satisfied by the standard universe.)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: isInductiveSet_toZF_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem isInductiveSet_toZF_iff (z : ℕ) : IsInductiveSet (toZF z) ↔ Inductive z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: The internal `Inductive` predicate on a code matches the standard `IsInductiveSet` on its translation.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: no_inductiveSet_HF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem no_inductiveSet_HF : ¬ ∃ z : ZFSet.{0}, IsHF z ∧ IsInductiveSet z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **The Axiom of Infinity strictly FAILS on HF**: no hereditarily finite set is inductive. This is exactly the negation of the textbook Infinity axiom, relativized to the HF universe — making `no_inductive_set` a genuine refutation of the standard axiom, not of some non-standard surrogate.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: transZF_RVal
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem transZF_RVal (n : ℕ) : transZF (RVal n) = toZF n
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: On the carrier `Univ`, `transZF` agrees with `toZF` on the underlying code.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: transZF_preserves_mem
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem transZF_preserves_mem {x y : RGFReal'} (hx : x ∈ Univ) (hy : y ∈ Univ) : RMem x y ↔ transZF x ∈ transZF y
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **Membership preservation through the reals**: `RMem` corresponds to genuine `∈` in the ZF universe via `transZF`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.name: transZF_image_univ_eq_isHF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.sig: theorem transZF_image_univ_eq_isHF : transZF '' Univ = {x | IsHF x}
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFZFBenchmark.lean.doc: **`Univ` maps onto the standard HF universe**: the `transZF`-image of `Univ` is exactly the hereditarily finite sets.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: RuleLayer.l1Dist_nonneg
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem RuleLayer.l1Dist_nonneg {α : Type} [Fintype α] (μ ν : RuleLayer α) : 0 ≤ μ.l1Dist ν

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: RuleLayer.l1Dist_symm
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem RuleLayer.l1Dist_symm {α : Type} [Fintype α] (μ ν : RuleLayer α) : μ.l1Dist ν = ν.l1Dist μ

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: RuleLayer.l1Dist_self
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem RuleLayer.l1Dist_self {α : Type} [Fintype α] (μ : RuleLayer α) : μ.l1Dist μ = 0

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: RuleLayer.l1Dist_le_two
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem RuleLayer.l1Dist_le_two {α : Type} [Fintype α] (μ ν : RuleLayer α) : μ.l1Dist ν ≤ 2
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The L¹ distance is bounded above by 2 (since the weights sum to 1).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: RuleLayer.l1Dist_triangle
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem RuleLayer.l1Dist_triangle {α : Type} [Fintype α] (μ ν ρ : RuleLayer α) : μ.l1Dist ρ ≤ μ.l1Dist ν + ν.l1Dist ρ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The triangle inequality for the L¹ distance on RuleLayer.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: DualLayerSystem.iterate_of_fixedPoint
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem DualLayerSystem.iterate_of_fixedPoint {α : Type} [Fintype α] (sys : DualLayerSystem α) (z : RuleLayer α) (hz : sys.IsFixedPoint z) (n : ℕ) : sys.iterate z n = z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: A fixed point is preserved under iteration.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: DualLayerSystem.iterate_fixedPoint_const
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem DualLayerSystem.iterate_fixedPoint_const {α : Type} [Fintype α] (sys : DualLayerSystem α) (z : RuleLayer α) (hz : sys.IsFixedPoint z) (n m : ℕ) : sys.iterate z n = sys.iterate z m
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: Two iterations starting from a fixed point always agree.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: ContractiveDLS.iterate_decay
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem ContractiveDLS.iterate_decay {α : Type} [Fintype α] (S : ContractiveDLS α) (μ ν : RuleLayer α) (n : ℕ) : (S.sys.iterate μ n).l1Dist (S.sys.iterate ν n) ≤ S.c ^ n * μ.l1Dist ν
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: Exponential decay of the distance under contractive iteration.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: ContractiveDLS.fixedPoint_unique
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem ContractiveDLS.fixedPoint_unique {α : Type} [Fintype α] (S : ContractiveDLS α) (z₁ z₂ : RuleLayer α) (h₁ : S.sys.IsFixedPoint z₁) (h₂ : S.sys.IsFixedPoint z₂) : z₁.l1Dist z₂ = 0
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: Uniqueness of the fixed point: the L¹ distance between two fixed points is 0.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: ContractiveDLS.convergence_rate
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem ContractiveDLS.convergence_rate {α : Type} [Fintype α] (S : ContractiveDLS α) (z zstar : RuleLayer α) (hstar : S.sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (n : ℕ) : (S.sys.iterate z n).l1Dist zstar ≤ S.c ^ n * z.l1Dist zstar
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: Convergence to the fixed point: the distance to z* decays exponentially.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: DualLayerSystem.iterate_weights_in_unit
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem DualLayerSystem.iterate_weights_in_unit {α : Type} [Fintype α] (sys : DualLayerSystem α) (r : RuleLayer α) (n : ℕ) (a : α) : 0 ≤ (sys.iterate r n).weight a ∧ (sys.iterate r n).weight a ≤ 1
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The weights always lie in [0,1] at every step.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: DualLayerSystem.iterate_total_weight
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem DualLayerSystem.iterate_total_weight {α : Type} [Fintype α] (sys : DualLayerSystem α) (r : RuleLayer α) (n : ℕ) : ∑ a : α, (sys.iterate r n).weight a = 1
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The weights sum to 1 at every step (total probability is conserved).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: rgfSymmetryFactor'_pos
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem rgfSymmetryFactor'_pos {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] {S : Type*} [MulAction G S] (s : S) : 0 < rgfSymmetryFactor' (G := G) s

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: rgfSymmetryFactor'_le_one
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem rgfSymmetryFactor'_le_one {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] {S : Type*} [MulAction G S] (s : S) : rgfSymmetryFactor' (G := G) s ≤ 1
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The symmetry factor is at most 1.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: rgfSymmetryFactor'_orbit_inv
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem rgfSymmetryFactor'_orbit_inv {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] {S : Type*} [MulAction G S] (s : S) (g : G) : rgfSymmetryFactor' (G := G) (g • s) = rgfSymmetryFactor' (G := G) s
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The symmetry factor is invariant along an orbit.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: emergProb_exp_bound
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem emergProb_exp_bound {α : Type} (c : ℝ) (hc0 : 0 ≤ c) (ρ₀ : ℝ) (hρ₀ : 0 ≤ ρ₀) (ξ : α → ℝ) (hξ : ∀ s, |ξ s| ≤ 1) (s : α) (n : ℕ) : |emergProb (fun n => ρ₀ * c ^ n) ξ s n| ≤ ρ₀ * c ^ n
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: If the temporal density decays exponentially and the spatial weight is bounded, then the emergent probability is controlled by an exponential envelope.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.name: emergProb_total_sum
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.sig: theorem emergProb_total_sum {α : Type} [Fintype α] (ρ : ℕ → ℝ) (ξ : α → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ∑ s : α, emergProb ρ ξ s n = ρ n * ∑ s : α, ξ s
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGFvsZFC.lean.doc: The total emergent probability over all states equals ρ(n) times the total spatial weight.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: reach_zero
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem reach_zero (S : GenSystem X) : S.reach 0 = S.seed

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: reach_add
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem reach_add (S : GenSystem X) (n k : ℕ) : S.reach (n + k) = (S.g^[k]) (S.reach n)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: reaches_of_le
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem reaches_of_le (S : GenSystem X) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : S.Reaches (S.reach m) (S.reach n)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: `reach n` is always reachable from `reach m` when `m ≤ n` — the forward, purely dynamical direction (no freeness needed).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: reaches_iff_le
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem reaches_iff_le (S : GenSystem X) (hS : S.IsFree) (m n : ℕ) : S.Reaches (S.reach m) (S.reach n) ↔ m ≤ n
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: **The emergence–isomorphism (order direction).** For a *free* system, the intrinsic reachability order on the orbit is *exactly* the order of `ℕ`: `reach m` reaches `reach n` iff `m ≤ n`. This is the order-isomorphism content — the orbit, with the order the dynamics itself induces, is `(ℕ, ≤)`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: reach_bijOn
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem reach_bijOn (S : GenSystem X) (hS : S.IsFree) : Set.BijOn S.reach Set.univ S.Orbit
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: **The emergence–isomorphism (bijection direction).** For a free system, `reach` is a bijection from `ℕ` onto the orbit: the orbit is a faithful copy of `ℕ`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: emergent_matches_standard_omega
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem emergent_matches_standard_omega {X : Type u} (S : GenSystem X) (hS : S.IsFree) : (∀ m n, S.Reaches (S.reach m) (S.reach n) ↔ m ≤ n) ∧ Set.BijOn S.reach Set.univ S.Orbit ∧ Nonempty (ℕ ≃o Set.Iio (Ordinal.omega0.{u}))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: **`ω` emerges from the dynamics and matches the standard `ω`.** For any free generative system there is a bijection `e : ℕ ≃ orbit` such that the intrinsic reachability order on the orbit corresponds to `≤` on `ℕ`, *and* `ℕ` is order-isomorphic (`natOrderIsoIioOmega`) to the standard ordinals below `ω`. Composing, the purely dynamical orbit *is* the standard `ω` — established by an isomorphism, not by a definitional renaming.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: intSuccSystem_reach
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem intSuccSystem_reach (n : ℕ) : intSuccSystem.reach n = (n : ℤ)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: intSuccSystem_isFree
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: The integer successor system is free — so its orbit genuinely emerges as `ω`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: intSuccSystem_emerges_omega
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem intSuccSystem_emerges_omega : (∀ m n, intSuccSystem.Reaches (intSuccSystem.reach m) (intSuccSystem.reach n) ↔ m ≤ n) ∧ Set.BijOn intSuccSystem.reach Set.univ intSuccSystem.Orbit ∧ Nonempty (ℕ ≃o Set.Iio (Ordinal.omega0.{0}))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: Hence the `ℤ`-based successor dynamics generates a standard `ω`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: idSystem_reach
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem idSystem_reach {X : Type u} (x : X) (n : ℕ) : (idSystem x).reach n = x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: idSystem_not_isFree
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem idSystem_not_isFree {X : Type u} (x : X) : ¬ (idSystem x).IsFree
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: The degenerate system is **not free**: `IsFree` is a genuine, violable hypothesis.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.name: idSystem_orbit_subsingleton
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.sig: theorem idSystem_orbit_subsingleton {X : Type u} (x : X) : (idSystem x).Orbit = {x}
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/EmergentOmega.le.doc: Its orbit collapses to a single point — it does *not* generate `ω`. Emergence of `ω` therefore relies essentially on freeness and is not automatic.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/GenerativeBridge.name: iterate_succOrd₂_eq_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/GenerativeBridge.sig: theorem iterate_succOrd₂_eq_toRGFOrd (n : ℕ) : (succOrd₂^[n]) (toRGFOrd (0 : Ordinal.{u})) = toRGFOrd (n : Ordinal.{u})

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/GenerativeBridge.name: tfIterate_succOrd₂_eq_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/GenerativeBridge.sig: theorem tfIterate_succOrd₂_eq_toRGFOrd (lim : (o : Ordinal.{u}) → Order.IsSuccLimit o → (Π o' < o, RGFSet₂.{u}) → RGFSet₂.{u}) (n : ℕ) : tfIterate succOrd₂ (toRGFOrd (0 : Ordinal.{u})) lim (n : Ordinal.{u}) = toRGFOrd (n : Ordinal.{u})

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/GenerativeBridge.name: mem_omegaOrd₂_iff_iterate
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/GenerativeBridge.sig: theorem mem_omegaOrd₂_iff_iterate (z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z omegaOrd₂ ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, z = (succOrd₂^[n]) (toRGFOrd (0 : Ordinal.{u}))

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: RGF2_models_ZFC
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem RGF2_models_ZFC : -- Extensionality (∀ x y : RGFSet₂.{v}, (∀ z, Mem₂ z x ↔ Mem₂ z y) → x = y) ∧ -- Empty set (∃ e : RGFSet₂.{v}, IsEmpty₂ e) ∧ -- Pairing (∀ a b : RGFSet₂.{v}, ∃ p, ∀ z, Mem₂ z p ↔ (z = a ∨ z = b)) ∧ -- Union (∀ x : RGFSet₂.{v}, ∃ u, ∀ z, Mem₂ z u ↔ ∃ w, Mem₂ w x ∧ Mem₂ z w) ∧ -- Power set (∀ x : RGFSet₂.{v}, ∃ p, ∀ z, Mem₂ z p ↔ Subset₂ z x) ∧ -- Separation (schema) (∀ (p : RGFSet₂.{v} → Prop) (x : RGFSet₂.{v}), ∃ s, ∀ z, Mem₂ z s ↔ (Mem₂ z x ∧ p z)) ∧ -- Replacement (schema) (∀ (f : RGFSet₂.{v} → RGFSet₂.{v}) (x : RGFSet₂.{v}), ∃ y, ∀ z, Mem₂ z y ↔ ∃ w, Mem₂ w x ∧ f w = z) ∧ -- Foundation (∀ x : RGFSet₂.{v}, ¬ IsEmpty₂ x → ∃ y, Mem₂ y x ∧ ∀ z, Mem₂ z y → ¬ Mem₂ z x) ∧ -- Infinity (∃ I : RGFSet₂.{v}, (∃ e, Mem₂ e I ∧ IsEmpty₂ e) ∧ (∀ x, Mem₂ x I → ∃ s, Mem₂ s I ∧ ∀ z, Mem₂ z s ↔ (Mem₂ z x ∨ z = x))) ∧ -- Choice (∀ x : RGFSet₂.{v}, (∀ a, Mem₂ a x → ∃ b, Mem₂ b a) → ∃ c : RGFSet₂.{v} → RGFSet₂.{v}, ∀ a, Mem₂ a x → Mem₂ (c a) a)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **RGF 2.0 satisfies full ZFC.** The generative tree-quotient universe `(RGFSet₂, Mem₂)` validates Extensionality, Empty set, Pairing, Union, Power set, the Separation schema, the Replacement schema, Foundation, Infinity and Choice.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: infinity_strict_upgrade
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem infinity_strict_upgrade : (∃ I : RGFSet₂.{0}, (∃ e, Mem₂ e I ∧ IsEmpty₂ e) ∧ (∀ x, Mem₂ x I → ∃ s, Mem₂ s I ∧ ∀ z, Mem₂ z s ↔ (Mem₂ z x ∨ z = x))) ∧ (¬ ∃ z, RGFSet.Mem 0 z ∧ ∀ y, RGFSet.Mem y z → ∃ w, RGFSet.Mem w z ∧ ∀ c, RGFSet.Mem c w ↔ (c = y ∨ RGFSet.Mem c y))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **Strict upgrade of the Infinity axiom.** RGF 2.0 satisfies Infinity, while the RGF 1.0 hereditarily finite core provably does not. Hence RGF 2.0 has strictly greater *axiomatic content* than RGF 1.0: a first-order sentence (Infinity) that is refutable in the RGF 1.0 universe holds in the RGF 2.0 universe. (This is a comparison of which axioms hold internally; it is *not* a claim that RGF 2.0 proves the consistency of RGF 1.0 or of PA — cf. the module docstring's note on consistency strength and Gödel's second incompleteness theorem.)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: hierarchy_strengthened
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem hierarchy_strengthened : -- (1) limit-stage union equation `V_λ = ⋃_{β<λ} V_β` (∀ (o : Ordinal.{0}), Order.IsSuccLimit o → ∀ x : RGFSet₂.{0}, Mem₂ x (Vhier o) ↔ ∃ β < o, Mem₂ x (Vhier β)) ∧ -- (2) rank arithmetic: pairing, power set, binary union (∀ a b : RGFSet₂.{0}, rank₂ (pair₂ a b) = max (Order.succ (rank₂ a)) (Order.succ (rank₂ b))) ∧ (∀ x : RGFSet₂.{0}, rank₂ (powersetOf₂ x) = Order.succ (rank₂ x)) ∧ (∀ a b : RGFSet₂.{0}, rank₂ (bunion₂ a b) = max (rank₂ a) (rank₂ b)) ∧ -- (3) Montague–Lévy reflection (closure form) (∀ (f : RGFSet₂.{0} → RGFSet₂.{0}) (β : Ordinal.{0}), ∃ α, β < α ∧ Order.IsSuccLimit α ∧ ∀ x, Mem₂ x (Vhier α) → Mem₂ (f x) (Vhier α)) ∧ -- (4) `V_ω` is exactly the RGF 1.0 hereditarily-finite core, strictly upgraded ((∀ x : RGFSet₂.{0}, Mem₂ x Vomega₂ ↔ RGF.RGFSet.IsHF (equivZF x)) ∧ (∀ a b : ℕ, Mem₂ (Vomega₂_equiv_ackCodes a : RGFSet₂.{0}) (Vomega₂_equiv_ackCodes b : RGFSet₂.{0}) ↔ RGF.RGFSet.Mem a b) ∧ ((ZFSet.omega : ZFSet.{0}) ∉ V_ Ordinal.omega0 ∧ ∃ o, (ZFSet.omega : ZFSet.{0}) ∈ V_ o))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **The strengthened cumulative hierarchy.** Beyond the raw ZFC axioms, the RGF 2.0 internal cumulative hierarchy `Vhier` obeys the full structural calculus: 1. the three defining clauses of the von Neumann hierarchy, including the **limit-stage union equation** `V_λ = ⋃_{β<λ} V_β`; 2. the **arithmetic of rank** under the basic set operations (pairing, power set, union), so that the hierarchy carries a genuine rank calculus; 3. the **Montague–Lévy reflection principle** (closure form): every internal class function is reflected by arbitrarily large *limit* stages `V_α`; 4. the **exact interface with RGF 1.0**: the stage `V_ω` is precisely the RGF 1.0 hereditarily-finite core, with a membership-preserving bijection to the Ackermann codes `ℕ`, and the upgrade above `V_ω` is strict.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: RGF2_forcing_relation_calculus
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem RGF2_forcing_relation_calculus {B : Type v} [CompleteBooleanAlgebra B] : (∀ p : B, BSet.Forces p (⊤ : B)) ∧ (∀ {p q φ : B}, q ≤ p → BSet.Forces p φ → BSet.Forces q φ) ∧ (∀ {p φ ψ : B}, φ ≤ ψ → BSet.Forces p φ → BSet.Forces p ψ) ∧ (∀ {p φ ψ : B}, BSet.Forces p (φ ⊓ ψ) ↔ (BSet.Forces p φ ∧ BSet.Forces p ψ)) ∧ (∀ {p φ ψ : B}, BSet.Forces p φ → BSet.Forces p (φ ⇨ ψ) → BSet.Forces p ψ) ∧ (∀ {p φ ψ : B}, BSet.Forces p (φ ⇨ ψ) ↔ BSet.Forces (p ⊓ φ) ψ) ∧ (∀ {p φ : B}, BSet.Forces p (φᶜᶜ) ↔ BSet.Forces p φ) ∧ (∀ {p φ : B}, p ≠ ⊥ → ¬ (BSet.Forces p φ ∧ BSet.Forces p φᶜ)) ∧ (∀ {φ : B}, BSet.Forces (⊤ : B) φ ↔ φ = ⊤)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **Path 3, forcing relation.** The forcing relation `⊩ᴮ` on `V^B` (with `p ⊩ᴮ φ := p ≤ ‖φ‖`) obeys the standard forcing calculus over any complete Boolean algebra `B`: `⊤` is forced; forcing is antitone in the condition and monotone in the value; conjunction, modus ponens and the **forcing definition of implication** (`p ⊩ φ ⇨ ψ ↔ (p ⊓ φ) ⊩ ψ`) hold; **double negation elimination** holds (`p ⊩ φᶜᶜ ↔ p ⊩ φ`); a nonzero condition is consistent (never forces both `φ` and `φᶜ`); and `⊤` forces `φ` exactly when `‖φ‖ = ⊤`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: RGF2_boolean_valued_ZFC_full
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem RGF2_boolean_valued_ZFC_full {B : Type v} [CompleteBooleanAlgebra B] : (∀ F : BSet B → BSet B, (∀ u v, BSet.BEq u v ≤ BSet.BEq (F u) (F v)) → (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ R : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, BSet.bicond (BSet.BMem z R) (⨆ w : BSet B, BSet.BMem w x ⊓ BSet.BEq z (F w))) = ⊤) ∧ (∀ φ : BSet B → B, (∀ u v, φ u ⊓ BSet.BEq u v ≤ φ v) → ∃ u : BSet B, φ u = ⨆ v : BSet B, φ v) ∧ (∀ φ : BSet B → BSet B → B, (∀ x u v, φ x u ⊓ BSet.BEq u v ≤ φ x v) → ∃ g : BSet B → BSet B, ∀ x : BSet B, (⨆ y : BSet B, φ x y) = φ x (g x))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **Path 3, deep water: `V^B` models the two remaining ZFC axioms.** Beyond the eight core axioms (`RGF2_boolean_valued_ZFC`), the Boolean-valued universe `V^B = BSet B` over an arbitrary complete Boolean algebra `B` also validates: 1. the **Replacement schema** (for `BEq`-congruent class functions) at Boolean truth value `⊤`; 2. the **Maximum Principle** (fullness): every existential value `⨆_v φ v` is attained by a witness name `u` (`φ u = ⨆_v φ v`), for `BEq`-congruent `φ`; 3. the **Axiom of Choice** in Skolem/selection form: `∀x∃y φ(x,y)` is uniformly Skolemized by a single class function `g` with `⨆_y φ x y = φ x (g x)`. Together with `RGF2_boolean_valued_ZFC` this shows `V^B` is a Boolean-valued model of **full** ZFC, closing direction 1 of the RGF 2.0 follow-up plan.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: RGF2_inaccessible_gives_ZFC_model
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem RGF2_inaccessible_gives_ZFC_model : (∃ c : Cardinal.{v}, c.IsInaccessible) → ∃ M : ZFSet.{v}, IsZFCModel M
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **Direction 3.1 — conditional consistency strength.** If a strongly inaccessible cardinal exists, then there is a transitive set model of ZFC (`IsZFCModel`): the von Neumann stage `V_ κ` for `κ` the inaccessible. By Gödel's second incompleteness theorem this cannot be made unconditional — it is stated as the honest *relative* consistency step, placing "ZFC + an inaccessible" strictly above ZFC on the consistency-strength ladder. (The essential use of inaccessibility is Replacement, via the regularity/strong-limit rank bound `rank_image_lt`.)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.name: RGF2_independence_backbone
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.sig: theorem RGF2_independence_backbone : ∃ y : ℕ → BSet (Set ℕ), (∀ n, ¬ BSet.Forces (⊤ : Set ℕ) (BSet.BMem BSet.bempty (y n)) ∧ ¬ BSet.Forces (⊤ : Set ℕ) (BSet.BMem BSet.bempty (y n))ᶜ) ∧ (∀ n m, n ≠ m → BSet.BMem BSet.bempty (y n) ⊓ BSet.BMem BSet.bempty (y m) = ⊥)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Master.lean.doc: **Direction 2.2 (partial) — the combinatorial backbone of forcing `¬CH`.** The full relative-consistency metatheorem `Con(ZFC) → Con(ZFC + ¬CH)` is Flypitch-scale (first-order deep embedding of ZFC, the Cohen ccc algebra, `‖CH‖ ≠ ⊤`, soundness) and remains research engineering. What is verified here is its genuine combinatorial core: over the complete Boolean algebra `Set ℕ`, the RGF 2.0 Boolean-valued universe carries an **infinite antichain of mutually independent, undecided forcing conditions** — the mechanism (adding unboundedly many independent Cohen bits) by which `2^ℵ₀` is pushed above `ℵ₁` and `CH` is forced to fail.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.name: relative_choiceFn
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.sig: theorem relative_choiceFn (A : RGFAxiomSuite.{u}) {ι : Type u} (X : ι → Type u) (h : ∀ i, Nonempty (X i)) : Nonempty (Π i, X i)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.doc: **Relative AC.** The internal choice function is derived *from* the explicit RGF axiom suite. Its axiom audit shows no `Classical.choice`: the choice content lives entirely in the hypothesis `A`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.name: relative_wellOrdering
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.sig: theorem relative_wellOrdering (A : RGFAxiomSuite.{u}) (α : Type u) : ∃ r : α → α → Prop, IsWellOrder α r
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.doc: **Relative well-ordering.** Derived from the suite, not from the host. Its axiom audit shows no `Classical.choice`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.name: rgf_internal_from_suite
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.sig: theorem rgf_internal_from_suite (A : RGFAxiomSuite.{u}) : (∀ {ι : Type u} (X : ι → Type u), (∀ i, Nonempty (X i)) → Nonempty (Π i, X i)) ∧ (∀ (α : Type u), ∃ r : α → α → Prop, IsWellOrder α r)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/RelativeStrength.doc: **Relative interpretation, honestly stated.** Whenever the RGF axiom suite is realizable in the metatheory, the internal choice and well-ordering principles hold. The strength RGF carries is therefore *bounded by* the strength needed to realize the suite — this is a relative interpretation, the honest content behind "RGF has the axiom of choice / well-ordering".

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: BMem_bimage
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem BMem_bimage (z : BSet B) (F : BSet B → BSet B) (x : BSet B) : BMem z (bimage F x) = ⨆ i : idx x, chg x i ⊓ BEq z (F (chf x i))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: Membership value of the image name, directly from the definition.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: BMem_bimage_eq
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem BMem_bimage_eq (z : BSet B) (F : BSet B → BSet B) (hF : ∀ u v, BEq u v ≤ BEq (F u) (F v)) (x : BSet B) : BMem z (bimage F x) = ⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x ⊓ BEq z (F w)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: Membership value of the image name, directly from the definition.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: valid_replacement
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem valid_replacement (F : BSet B → BSet B) (hF : ∀ u v, BEq u v ≤ BEq (F u) (F v)) : (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ R : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z R) (⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x ⊓ BEq z (F w))) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: **Replacement holds in `V^B`** (schema: one instance per `BEq`-congruent class function `F`). Interpreting the functional-Replacement axiom "`∀x ∃R ∀z (z ∈ R ↔ ∃w ∈ x, z = F w)`" as a Boolean truth value evaluates to `⊤`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: BEq_bmix
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem BEq_bmix {I : Type u} (a : I → B) (u : I → BSet B) (hdisj : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → a i ⊓ a j = ⊥) (i : I) : a i ≤ BEq (bmix a u) (u i)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: The **mixture** of a family of names `u : I → BSet B` along a family of conditions `a : I → B`: a single name whose `i`-branch is the `a i`-restricted copy of `u i`. When the `a i` are pairwise disjoint, `bmix a u` agrees with `u i` above `a i` (see `BEq_bmix`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: exists_witnessed_antichain
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem exists_witnessed_antichain (φ : BSet B → B) : ∃ A : Set B, A.PairwiseDisjoint (id : B → B) ∧ (⊥ ∉ A) ∧ (∀ p ∈ A, ∃ v : BSet B, p ≤ φ v) ∧ (⨆ v : BSet B, φ v) ≤ sSup A

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: maximum_principle
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem maximum_principle (φ : BSet B → B) (hφ : ∀ u v, φ u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ v) : ∃ u : BSet B, φ u = ⨆ v : BSet B, φ v
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: **Maximum Principle / fullness of `V^B`.** For any `BEq`-congruent Boolean value `φ : BSet B → B`, the supremum `⨆_v φ v` — the Boolean value of the existential `∃x. φ(x)` — is *attained* by a single witness name `u`: `φ u = ⨆_v φ v`. This is the model-theoretic fact underlying the Axiom of Choice in a Boolean-valued model: every existential statement has a witness name.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: valid_choice
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem valid_choice (φ : BSet B → BSet B → B) (hφ : ∀ x u v, φ x u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ x v) : ∃ g : BSet B → BSet B, ∀ x : BSet B, (⨆ y : BSet B, φ x y) = φ x (g x)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: **The Axiom of Choice in `V^B` (Skolem/selection form).** For any Boolean value `φ : BSet B → BSet B → B` that is `BEq`-congruent in its second argument, there is a class function `g : BSet B → BSet B` that, for every `x`, selects a *best* witness: the value `⨆_y φ x y` of the existential `∃y φ(x,y)` is realized exactly at `g x`. Thus `∀x∃y φ(x,y)` is uniformly Skolemized by a single class function — the Boolean-valued content of the Axiom of Choice, obtained from the Maximum Principle applied pointwise (plus choice over `x`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.name: VB_models_ZFC_full
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.sig: theorem VB_models_ZFC_full : -- Replacement schema (for `BEq`-congruent class functions), value `⊤` (∀ F : BSet B → BSet B, (∀ u v, BEq u v ≤ BEq (F u) (F v)) → (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ R : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z R) (⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x ⊓ BEq z (F w))) = ⊤) ∧ -- Maximum Principle (fullness): every existential has a witness name (∀ φ : BSet B → B, (∀ u v, φ u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ v) → ∃ u : BSet B, φ u = ⨆ v : BSet B, φ v) ∧ -- Choice (Skolem/selection form) (∀ φ : BSet B → BSet B → B, (∀ x u v, φ x u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ x v) → ∃ g : BSet B → BSet B, ∀ x : BSet B, (⨆ y : BSet B, φ x y) = φ x (g x))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ChoiceRe.doc: **`V^B` is a Boolean-valued model of full ZFC.** Combining the eight core axioms (`VB_models_ZFC_core`) with the two "deep water" axioms proved here — the Replacement schema (`valid_replacement`) at Boolean value `⊤`, and the Axiom of Choice in Skolem/selection form (`valid_choice`) derived from the Maximum Principle (`maximum_principle`) — the Boolean-valued universe `V^B = BSet B` over an arbitrary complete Boolean algebra `B` validates *all* the axioms of ZFC. Together with the realized undecidability (`membership_can_be_independent`) this makes `V^B` a genuine forcing model.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..name: BEq_trans_le
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..sig: theorem BEq_trans_le (x y z : BSet B) : BEq x y ⊓ BEq y z ≤ BEq x z

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..name: BEq_mem_congr_right
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..sig: theorem BEq_mem_congr_right (u v x : BSet B) : BEq u v ⊓ BMem x u ≤ BMem x v

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..name: BEq_mem_congr_left
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..sig: theorem BEq_mem_congr_left (u v x : BSet B) : BEq u v ⊓ BMem u x ≤ BMem v x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..name: BMem_bpair
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..sig: theorem BMem_bpair (z x y : BSet B) : BMem z (bpair x y) = BEq z x ⊔ BEq z y
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..doc: The Boolean-valued unordered pair `{x, y}ᴮ`: two children `x`, `y`, each carrying truth value `⊤`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..name: forcing_pairing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..sig: theorem forcing_pairing (x y : BSet B) : ∃ p : BSet B, ∀ z, BMem z p = BEq z x ⊔ BEq z y
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..doc: **The pairing axiom holds in `V^B`.** For any two names there is a name whose membership value is exactly the pairing disjunction.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..name: BSet.bmem_undecided
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..sig: theorem BSet.bmem_undecided : ∃ (x y : BSet (Set (Fin 2))), ⊥ < BSet.BMem x y ∧ ⊥ < (BSet.BMem x y)ᶜ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Forcing..doc: **Independence realised in `V^B`.** Over the non-degenerate complete Boolean algebra `Set (Fin 2)` there is a membership statement `φ` for which both `⟦φ⟧` and `⟦¬φ⟧ = ⟦φ⟧ᶜ` are nonzero: neither `φ` nor its negation is forced by `⊤`. This is the algebraic core of every forcing independence result.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_iff {p φ : B} : (p ⊩ᴮ φ) ↔ p ≤ φ

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_top
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: The trivial value `⊤` is forced by every condition.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_mono_cond
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_mono_cond {p q φ : B} (hqp : q ≤ p) (h : p ⊩ᴮ φ) : q ⊩ᴮ φ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: Forcing is antitone in the condition: a smaller (stronger) condition still forces whatever a larger one does.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_mono_value
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_mono_value {p φ ψ : B} (hφψ : φ ≤ ψ) (h : p ⊩ᴮ φ) : p ⊩ᴮ ψ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: Forcing is monotone in the value.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_inf_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_inf_iff {p φ ψ : B} : (p ⊩ᴮ (φ ⊓ ψ)) ↔ (p ⊩ᴮ φ) ∧ (p ⊩ᴮ ψ)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **Conjunction.** `p ⊩ φ ⊓ ψ` iff `p ⊩ φ` and `p ⊩ ψ`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_sup_left
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_sup_left {p φ ψ : B} (h : p ⊩ᴮ φ) : p ⊩ᴮ (φ ⊔ ψ)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **Disjunction (left).** Forcing a disjunct forces the disjunction.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_sup_right
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_sup_right {p φ ψ : B} (h : p ⊩ᴮ ψ) : p ⊩ᴮ (φ ⊔ ψ)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_mp
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_mp {p φ ψ : B} (hφ : p ⊩ᴮ φ) (himp : p ⊩ᴮ (φ ⇨ ψ)) : p ⊩ᴮ ψ

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_himp_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_himp_iff {p φ ψ : B} : (p ⊩ᴮ (φ ⇨ ψ)) ↔ ((p ⊓ φ) ⊩ᴮ ψ)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **The forcing definition of implication.** `p ⊩ (φ ⇨ ψ)` exactly when the condition `p ⊓ φ` forces `ψ` — i.e. every extension of `p` forcing `φ` forces `ψ`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_dne
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **Double negation.** `p ⊩ φᶜᶜ ↔ p ⊩ φ`. In a Boolean algebra the value domain is classical, so double negation elimination holds at the level of forcing.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: top_forces_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem top_forces_iff {φ : B} : ((⊤ : B) ⊩ᴮ φ) ↔ φ = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **Weak forcing / the trivial condition.** `⊤` forces `φ` iff the Boolean value of `φ` is `⊤` — the two-valued notion of "valid in `V^B`".

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_consistent
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_consistent {p φ : B} (hp : p ≠ ⊥) : ¬ ((p ⊩ᴮ φ) ∧ (p ⊩ᴮ φᶜ))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **Consistency of forcing.** A nonzero condition never forces both a statement and its negation.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_pairing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_pairing (p : B) (z x y : BSet B) : (Forces p (BMem z (bpair x y))) ↔ (Forces p (BEq z x ⊔ BEq z y))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: Forcing membership in the Boolean-valued pair `{x, y}ᴮ` is forcing the equality disjunction, using `BMem_bpair`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: forces_pairing_self
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem forces_pairing_self (x y : BSet B) : (⊤ : B) ⊩ᴮ (BMem x (bpair x y))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: `⊤` forces that `x` is a member of the Boolean-valued pair `{x, y}ᴮ`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.name: BSet.forcing_independence
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.sig: theorem BSet.forcing_independence : ∃ (x y : BSet (Set (Fin 2))), ¬ (BSet.Forces (⊤ : Set (Fin 2)) (BSet.BMem x y)) ∧ ¬ (BSet.Forces (⊤ : Set (Fin 2)) (BSet.BMem x y)ᶜ)
