RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ForcingR.doc: **Independence, in forcing language.** Over the non-degenerate complete Boolean algebra `Set (Fin 2)` there is a membership statement `⟦x ∈ᴮ y⟧` that the trivial condition `⊤` forces neither positively (`⊤ ⊮ φ`) nor negatively (`⊤ ⊮ φᶜ`). This is the forcing-relation restatement of `BSet.bmem_undecided`, and the algebraic core on which every forcing independence result (CH, AC, …) rests: changing the Boolean algebra `B` can push the truth value of `φ` to `⊤` or to `⊥`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.name: infinite_independent_conditions
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.sig: theorem infinite_independent_conditions : ∃ y : ℕ → BSet (Set ℕ), (∀ n, ⊥ < BMem bempty (y n) ∧ BMem bempty (y n) < ⊤) ∧ (∀ n m, n ≠ m → BMem bempty (y n) ⊓ BMem bempty (y m) = ⊥)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.doc: **Infinite antichain of independent forcing conditions.** Over the complete Boolean algebra `B = Set ℕ`, the names `y n := bsingleton {n}` have membership truth values `‖bempty ∈ y n‖ = {n}`, which are each strictly between `⊥` and `⊤` (undecided) and pairwise disjoint (an infinite antichain of nonzero conditions). This is the combinatorial backbone of adding infinitely many independent Cohen reals — the mechanism forcing `¬CH`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.name: infinite_independent_forcing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.sig: theorem infinite_independent_forcing : ∃ y : ℕ → BSet (Set ℕ), (∀ n, ¬ Forces (⊤ : Set ℕ) (BMem bempty (y n)) ∧ ¬ Forces (⊤ : Set ℕ) (BMem bempty (y n))ᶜ) ∧ (∀ n m, n ≠ m → BMem bempty (y n) ⊓ BMem bempty (y m) = ⊥)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.doc: **The independence family, in forcing language.** Over `B = Set ℕ` there is an infinite family of membership sentences that the trivial condition `⊤` forces neither positively nor negatively, and whose forcing conditions are pairwise incompatible (their meet is `⊥`). This is the forcing-relation restatement of `infinite_independent_conditions`: an infinite supply of independent generic bits.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.name: indepFamily_value
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.sig: theorem indepFamily_value (n : ℕ) : BMem bempty (indepFamily n) = ({n} : Set ℕ)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.name: independent_conditions_injective
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.sig: theorem independent_conditions_injective : Function.Injective (fun n => BMem bempty (indepFamily n))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.doc: **The conditions are genuinely distinct.** The map `n ↦ ‖bempty ∈ y n‖` is injective, so the family is a true antichain of distinct conditions, not merely an `ℕ`-indexed list with possible repeats.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.name: independent_conditions_range_infinite
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.sig: theorem independent_conditions_range_infinite : (Set.range (fun n => BMem bempty (indepFamily n))).Infinite ∧ (∀ n, ⊥ < BMem bempty (indepFamily n) ∧ BMem bempty (indepFamily n) < ⊤) ∧ (∀ n m, n ≠ m → BMem bempty (indepFamily n) ⊓ BMem bempty (indepFamily m) = ⊥)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Independ.doc: **Literal infinite antichain.** Over `B = Set ℕ` the set of membership conditions `{ ‖bempty ∈ y n‖ | n : ℕ }` is genuinely infinite, each condition is strictly between `⊥` and `⊤` (undecided) and any two are disjoint. This upgrades the "infinite antichain" of the ¬CH backbone from an indexed family to a literal `Set.Infinite` statement.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: BEq_def
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem BEq_def (ι f g ι' f' g') : BEq (B := B) ⟨ι, f, g⟩ ⟨ι', f', g'⟩ = (⨅ i, g i ⇨ ⨆ j, g' j ⊓ BEq (f i) (f' j)) ⊓ (⨅ j, g' j ⇨ ⨆ i, g i ⊓ BEq (f i) (f' j))

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: BMem_def
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem BMem_def (x : BSet B) (ι' f' g') : BMem x ⟨ι', f', g'⟩ = ⨆ j, g' j ⊓ BEq x (f' j)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: BEq_refl
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem BEq_refl (x : BSet B) : BEq x x = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.doc: `⟦x =ᴮ x⟧ = ⊤`: Boolean-valued equality is fully true of itself.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: BEq_symm
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem BEq_symm (x y : BSet B) : BEq x y = BEq y x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.doc: `⟦x =ᴮ y⟧ = ⟦y =ᴮ x⟧`: Boolean-valued equality is symmetric.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: BMem_bempty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem BMem_bempty (x : BSet B) : BMem x bempty = ⊥
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.doc: Nothing belongs to the empty name: its membership value is `⊥`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: BMem_bsingleton
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem BMem_bsingleton (b : B) : BMem (bempty : BSet B) (bsingleton b) = b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: sound_mp
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem sound_mp (a b : B) : a ⊓ (a ⇨ b) ≤ b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.doc: **Modus ponens** is sound in the value domain: `a ⊓ (a ⇨ b) ≤ b`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: sound_dne
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.doc: The value domain obeys **classical** (double-negation) logic — this is what distinguishes a Boolean-valued model from a merely intuitionistic (Heyting) one.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.name: RGF.RGF2.membership_can_be_independent
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.sig: theorem RGF.RGF2.membership_can_be_independent : ∃ (b : Set (Fin 2)) (x y : RGF.RGF2.BSet (Set (Fin 2))), ⊥ < b ∧ b < ⊤ ∧ RGF.RGF2.BSet.BMem x y = b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/Model.le.doc: **Model flexibility.** Over a non-degenerate complete Boolean algebra the truth value of a membership statement can be strictly between `⊥` and `⊤`. This is the mechanism by which varying `B` (to a Cohen or random algebra) produces models in which CH or AC fails — the independence phenomena unavailable to two-valued RGF.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: idx_mk
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: @[simp] theorem idx_mk (ι : Type u) (f : ι → BSet B) (g : ι → B) : idx (mk ι f g) = ι

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: chf_mk
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: @[simp] theorem chf_mk (ι : Type u) (f : ι → BSet B) (g : ι → B) : chf (mk ι f g) = f

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: chg_mk
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: @[simp] theorem chg_mk (ι : Type u) (f : ι → BSet B) (g : ι → B) : chg (mk ι f g) = g

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_eq
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_eq (x y : BSet B) : BMem x y = ⨆ j : idx y, chg y j ⊓ BEq x (chf y j)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Membership value expressed through the accessors.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: bicond_eq_top_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem bicond_eq_top_iff {a b : B} : bicond a b = ⊤ ↔ a = b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: bicond_self
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem bicond_self (a : B) : bicond a a = ⊤

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_bsep
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_bsep (φ : BSet B → B) (hφ : ∀ u v, φ u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ v) (z x : BSet B) : BMem z (bsep φ x) = BMem z x ⊓ φ z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Separation characterization.** For a `BEq`-congruent predicate `φ`, `⟦z ∈ bsep φ x⟧ = ⟦z ∈ x⟧ ⊓ φ z`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_bsUnion
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_bsUnion (z x : BSet B) : BMem z (bsUnion x) = ⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x ⊓ BMem z w
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Separation characterization.** For a `BEq`-congruent predicate `φ`, `⟦z ∈ bsep φ x⟧ = ⟦z ∈ x⟧ ⊓ φ z`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_bpsub
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_bpsub (w x : BSet B) (h : idx x → B) : BMem w (bpsub x h) = ⨆ i : idx x, (chg x i ⊓ h i) ⊓ BEq w (chf x i)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Membership value of a sub-name.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_bpsub_le
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_bpsub_le (w x : BSet B) (h : idx x → B) : BMem w (bpsub x h) ≤ BMem w x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Every sub-name is a subset of `x` (value `⊤`): `⟦w ∈ bpsub x h⟧ ≤ ⟦w ∈ x⟧`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BEq_subset_le
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BEq_subset_le (z u x : BSet B) : BEq z u ⊓ BSubset u x ≤ BSubset z x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Every sub-name is a subset of `x` (value `⊤`): `⟦w ∈ bpsub x h⟧ ≤ ⟦w ∈ x⟧`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BSubset_le_BEq_bpsub
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BSubset_le_BEq_bpsub (z x : BSet B) : BSubset z x ≤ BEq z (bpsub x (fun i => BMem (chf x i) z))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Every sub-name is a subset of `x` (value `⊤`): `⟦w ∈ bpsub x h⟧ ≤ ⟦w ∈ x⟧`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_bpowerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_bpowerset (z x : BSet B) : BMem z (bpowerset x) = BSubset z x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Power-set characterization.** `⟦z ∈ 𝒫 x⟧ = ⟦z ⊆ x⟧`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_extensionality
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_extensionality : (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨅ y : BSet B, (⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z x) (BMem z y)) ⇨ BEq x y) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Power-set characterization.** `⟦z ∈ 𝒫 x⟧ = ⟦z ⊆ x⟧`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_empty : (⨆ e : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, (BMem z e)ᶜ) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Empty set** holds in `V^B`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_pairing
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_pairing : (⨅ a : BSet B, ⨅ b : BSet B, ⨆ p : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z p) (BEq z a ⊔ BEq z b)) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Pairing** holds in `V^B`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_union
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_union : (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ u : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z u) (⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x ⊓ BMem z w)) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Union** holds in `V^B`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_powerset : (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ p : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z p) (BSubset z x)) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Power set** holds in `V^B`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_separation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_separation (φ : BSet B → B) (hφ : ∀ u v, φ u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ v) : (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ s : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z s) (BMem z x ⊓ φ z)) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Separation** holds in `V^B` (schema: one instance per `BEq`-congruent predicate `φ`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: foundation_aux
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem foundation_aux (a x : BSet B) : BMem a x ≤ ⨆ y : BSet B, BMem y x ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, BMem z y ⇨ (BMem z x)ᶜ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Separation** holds in `V^B` (schema: one instance per `BEq`-congruent predicate `φ`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_foundation
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_foundation : (⨅ x : BSet B, (⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x) ⇨ ⨆ y : BSet B, BMem y x ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, BMem z y ⇨ (BMem z x)ᶜ) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Foundation / Regularity** holds in `V^B`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: BMem_bsucc
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem BMem_bsucc (z a : BSet B) : BMem z (bsucc a) = BMem z a ⊔ BEq z a
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **Successor characterization.** `⟦z ∈ bsucc a⟧ = ⟦z ∈ a⟧ ⊔ ⟦z =ᴮ a⟧`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: omega_self_mem
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem omega_self_mem (n : ℕ) : BMem ((bsucc)^[n] bempty) (bomega : BSet B) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Each finite von Neumann numeral `bsucc^[n] bempty` is a member of `bomega` with value `⊤`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: valid_infinity
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem valid_infinity : (⨆ I : BSet B, (⨆ e : BSet B, BMem e I ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, (BMem z e)ᶜ) ⊓ (⨅ x : BSet B, BMem x I ⇨ ⨆ s : BSet B, BMem s I ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z s) (BMem z x ⊔ BEq z x))) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: Each finite von Neumann numeral `bsucc^[n] bempty` is a member of `bomega` with value `⊤`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.name: VB_models_ZFC_core
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.sig: theorem VB_models_ZFC_core : -- Extensionality (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨅ y : BSet B, (⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z x) (BMem z y)) ⇨ BEq x y) = ⊤ ∧ -- Empty set (⨆ e : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, (BMem z e)ᶜ) = ⊤ ∧ -- Pairing (⨅ a : BSet B, ⨅ b : BSet B, ⨆ p : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z p) (BEq z a ⊔ BEq z b)) = ⊤ ∧ -- Union (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ u : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z u) (⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x ⊓ BMem z w)) = ⊤ ∧ -- Power set (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ p : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z p) (BSubset z x)) = ⊤ ∧ -- Separation schema (BEq-congruent predicates) (∀ φ : BSet B → B, (∀ u v, φ u ⊓ BEq u v ≤ φ v) → (⨅ x : BSet B, ⨆ s : BSet B, ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z s) (BMem z x ⊓ φ z)) = ⊤) ∧ -- Foundation (⨅ x : BSet B, (⨆ w : BSet B, BMem w x) ⇨ ⨆ y : BSet B, BMem y x ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, BMem z y ⇨ (BMem z x)ᶜ) = ⊤ ∧ -- Infinity (⨆ I : BSet B, (⨆ e : BSet B, BMem e I ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, (BMem z e)ᶜ) ⊓ (⨅ x : BSet B, BMem x I ⇨ ⨆ s : BSet B, BMem s I ⊓ ⨅ z : BSet B, bicond (BMem z s) (BMem z x ⊔ BEq z x))) = ⊤
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Boolean/ValuedZF.doc: **`V^B` is a Boolean-valued model of ZFC (core).** Over an arbitrary complete Boolean algebra `B`, every one of the following ZFC axioms — interpreted as a Boolean truth value with `∀`/`∃` read as `⨅`/`⨆` over the class of names and `↔` as the Boolean biconditional — evaluates to `⊤`: Extensionality, Empty set, Pairing, Union, Power set, the Separation schema (for `BEq`-congruent predicates), Foundation and Infinity. This is Path 3 of the RGF 2.0 reconstruction: the value domain of `∈` is widened from the two-valued `Prop` to `B`, and the axioms remain valid — while `membership_can_be_independent` / `bmem_undecided` show membership truth values can lie strictly between `⊥` and `⊤`, the flexibility forcing rests on.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.name: subset₂_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.sig: theorem subset₂_iff {a b : RGFSet₂.{u}} : Subset₂ a b ↔ equivZF a ⊆ equivZF b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.doc: The internal subset relation corresponds to the standard subset relation.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.name: card₂_empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.doc: The empty internal set has cardinality `0`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.name: card₂_mono
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.sig: theorem card₂_mono {a b : RGFSet₂.{u}} (h : Subset₂ a b) : CardLE₂ a b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.name: card₂_powersetOf
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.sig: theorem card₂_powersetOf (a : RGFSet₂.{u}) : card₂ (powersetOf₂ a) = 2 ^ card₂ a

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.name: cantor₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.sig: theorem cantor₂ (a : RGFSet₂.{u}) : CardLT₂ a (powersetOf₂ a)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.doc: **Cantor's theorem, internally.** Every internal set is strictly dominated in cardinality by its internal power-set.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.name: cardLE₂_antisymm
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.sig: theorem cardLE₂_antisymm {a b : RGFSet₂.{u}} (h1 : CardLE₂ a b) (h2 : CardLE₂ b a) : Equinum₂ a b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalCar.doc: **Schröder–Bernstein direction.** Mutual internal cardinal domination implies internal equinumerosity.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: equivZF_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: @[simp] theorem equivZF_toRGFOrd (o : Ordinal.{u}) : equivZF (toRGFOrd o) = o.toZFSet

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: toRGFOrd_injective
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.doc: The internal von Neumann successor `a ↦ a ∪ {a}`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: isOrdinal₂_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.doc: The internal von Neumann successor `a ↦ a ∪ {a}`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: toRGFOrd_mem_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem toRGFOrd_mem_iff {a b : Ordinal.{u}} : Mem₂ (toRGFOrd a) (toRGFOrd b) ↔ a < b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.doc: The internal von Neumann successor `a ↦ a ∪ {a}`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: toRGFOrd_subset_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem toRGFOrd_subset_iff {a b : Ordinal.{u}} : Subset₂ (toRGFOrd a) (toRGFOrd b) ↔ a ≤ b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.doc: The internal von Neumann successor `a ↦ a ∪ {a}`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: toRGFOrd_zero_isEmpty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.doc: The internal von Neumann successor `a ↦ a ∪ {a}`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: succOrd₂_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem succOrd₂_toRGFOrd (o : Ordinal.{u}) : succOrd₂ (toRGFOrd o) = toRGFOrd (Order.succ o)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.doc: The internal von Neumann successor `a ↦ a ∪ {a}`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: ordAdd₂_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem ordAdd₂_toRGFOrd (a b : Ordinal.{u}) : ordAdd₂ (toRGFOrd a) (toRGFOrd b) = toRGFOrd (a + b)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: ordMul₂_toRGFOrd
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem ordMul₂_toRGFOrd (a b : Ordinal.{u}) : ordMul₂ (toRGFOrd a) (toRGFOrd b) = toRGFOrd (a * b)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: ordAdd₂_assoc
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem ordAdd₂_assoc (a b c : Ordinal.{u}) : ordAdd₂ (ordAdd₂ (toRGFOrd a) (toRGFOrd b)) (toRGFOrd c) = ordAdd₂ (toRGFOrd a) (ordAdd₂ (toRGFOrd b) (toRGFOrd c))

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: ordMul₂_assoc
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem ordMul₂_assoc (a b c : Ordinal.{u}) : ordMul₂ (ordMul₂ (toRGFOrd a) (toRGFOrd b)) (toRGFOrd c) = ordMul₂ (toRGFOrd a) (ordMul₂ (toRGFOrd b) (toRGFOrd c))

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: ordAdd₂_one_omega
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem ordAdd₂_one_omega : ordAdd₂ (toRGFOrd (1 : Ordinal.{u})) omegaOrd₂ = omegaOrd₂

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.name: ordAdd₂_omega_one_ne
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/InternalOrd.sig: theorem ordAdd₂_omega_one_ne : ordAdd₂ omegaOrd₂ (toRGFOrd (1 : Ordinal.{u})) ≠ omegaOrd₂

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.name: mem_mul₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.sig: theorem mem_mul₂ (a b z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (a * b) ↔ ((Mem₂ z a ∧ ¬ Mem₂ z b) ∨ (Mem₂ z b ∧ ¬ Mem₂ z a))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.doc: Membership in a product is the *exclusive or* of the two memberships: `z ∈ a △ b ↔ (z ∈ a ∧ z ∉ b) ∨ (z ∈ b ∧ z ∉ a)`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.name: not_mem_one₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.sig: theorem not_mem_one₂ (z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ¬ Mem₂ z (1 : RGFSet₂.{u})
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.doc: Nothing belongs to the identity, i.e. the internal `1` is empty.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.name: symmDiff_assoc₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.sig: theorem symmDiff_assoc₂ (a b c : RGFSet₂.{u}) : a * b * c = a * (b * c)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.name: symmDiff_comm₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/SymmDiffGro.sig: theorem symmDiff_comm₂ (a b : RGFSet₂.{u}) : a * b = b * a

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: to_of
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem to_of (x : PSet.{u}) : toPSet (ofPSet x) = x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: of_to
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem of_to (x : RGFPreSet.{u}) : ofPSet (toPSet x) = x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: ext₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem ext₂ {x y : RGFSet₂.{u}} (h : ∀ z, Mem₂ z x ↔ Mem₂ z y) : x = y

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: empty₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem empty₂ : ∃ e : RGFSet₂.{u}, IsEmpty₂ e

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: pairing₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem pairing₂ (a b : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ p, ∀ z, Mem₂ z p ↔ (z = a ∨ z = b)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: union₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem union₂ (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ u, ∀ z, Mem₂ z u ↔ ∃ w, Mem₂ w x ∧ Mem₂ z w

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: powerset₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem powerset₂ (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ p, ∀ z, Mem₂ z p ↔ Subset₂ z x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: separation₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem separation₂ (p : RGFSet₂.{u} → Prop) (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ s, ∀ z, Mem₂ z s ↔ (Mem₂ z x ∧ p z)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.doc: **Separation** (full first-order schema, one instance per predicate `p`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: replacement₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem replacement₂ (f : RGFSet₂.{u} → RGFSet₂.{u}) (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ y, ∀ z, Mem₂ z y ↔ ∃ w, Mem₂ w x ∧ f w = z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.doc: **Replacement** (full first-order schema, one instance per class function `f`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: foundation₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem foundation₂ (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) (hx : ¬ IsEmpty₂ x) : ∃ y, Mem₂ y x ∧ ∀ z, Mem₂ z y → ¬ Mem₂ z x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: infinity₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem infinity₂ : ∃ I : RGFSet₂.{u}, (∃ e, Mem₂ e I ∧ IsEmpty₂ e) ∧ (∀ x, Mem₂ x I → ∃ s, Mem₂ s I ∧ ∀ z, Mem₂ z s ↔ (Mem₂ z x ∨ z = x))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.doc: **Infinity** — the defect that genuinely *fails* for the RGF 1.0 arithmetic codes now holds unconditionally: there is an inductive set (empty element, closed under von Neumann successor `x ↦ x ∪ {x}`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.name: choice₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.sig: theorem choice₂ (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) (h : ∀ a, Mem₂ a x → ∃ b, Mem₂ b a) : ∃ c : RGFSet₂.{u} → RGFSet₂.{u}, ∀ a, Mem₂ a x → Mem₂ (c a) a
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Core/WType.lean.doc: **Choice.** Any RGF 2.0 set of non-empty sets admits a choice function.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: mem_Vhier_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem mem_Vhier_iff (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) (o : Ordinal.{u}) : Mem₂ x (Vhier o) ↔ rank₂ x < o
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: Membership in a hierarchy stage is governed by rank.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_zero
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_zero : IsEmpty₂ (Vhier.{u} 0)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_succ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_succ (o : Ordinal.{u}) (z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (Vhier (Order.succ o)) ↔ Subset₂ z (Vhier o)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: `V (α+1)` is exactly the power set of `V α`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_mono
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_mono {a b : Ordinal.{u}} (h : a ≤ b) : Subset₂ (Vhier a) (Vhier b)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: The hierarchy is monotone in the ordinal stage.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_transitive
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_transitive (o : Ordinal.{u}) (x y : RGFSet₂.{u}) (hx : Mem₂ x (Vhier o)) (hy : Mem₂ y x) : Mem₂ y (Vhier o)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: Every stage is transitive: members of members are members.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_exhaustion
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_exhaustion (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ o, Mem₂ x (Vhier o)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Exhaustion.** Every RGF 2.0 set appears at some stage of the hierarchy.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_reflection
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_reflection (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : ∃ o, Mem₂ x (Vhier o) ∧ ∀ y, Mem₂ y x → Mem₂ y (Vhier o)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Reflection.** Every set, together with all of its members, is captured by a single set stage `V o` of the hierarchy.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: Vhier_limit
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem Vhier_limit (o : Ordinal.{u}) (ho : Order.IsSuccLimit o) (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ x (Vhier o) ↔ ∃ β < o, Mem₂ x (Vhier β)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **The limit-stage union equation** `V_λ = ⋃_{β<λ} V_β`, in its membership form: at a limit stage a set appears iff it already appears at some earlier stage. This is the third defining clause of the cumulative hierarchy (`V 0 = ∅`, `V (α+1) = 𝒫(V α)`, `V λ = ⋃_{β<λ} V β`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: mem_pair₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: @[simp] theorem mem_pair₂ (a b z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (pair₂ a b) ↔ z = a ∨ z = b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: mem_singleton₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: @[simp] theorem mem_singleton₂ (a z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (singleton₂ a) ↔ z = a

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: mem_bunion₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: @[simp] theorem mem_bunion₂ (a b z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (bunion₂ a b) ↔ Mem₂ z a ∨ Mem₂ z b

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: mem_sUnion₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: @[simp] theorem mem_sUnion₂ (x z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (sUnion₂ x) ↔ ∃ w, Mem₂ w x ∧ Mem₂ z w

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: mem_powersetOf₂
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: @[simp] theorem mem_powersetOf₂ (x z : RGFSet₂.{u}) : Mem₂ z (powersetOf₂ x) ↔ Subset₂ z x

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_pair
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_pair (a b : RGFSet₂.{u}) : rank₂ (pair₂ a b) = max (Order.succ (rank₂ a)) (Order.succ (rank₂ b))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Rank of a pair.** `rank({a,b}) = max (rank a + 1) (rank b + 1)`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_singleton
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_singleton (a : RGFSet₂.{u}) : rank₂ (singleton₂ a) = Order.succ (rank₂ a)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_insert
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_insert (a x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : rank₂ (insert₂ a x) = max (Order.succ (rank₂ a)) (rank₂ x)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Rank of an insert.** `rank(insert a x) = max (rank a + 1) (rank x)`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_bunion
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_bunion (a b : RGFSet₂.{u}) : rank₂ (bunion₂ a b) = max (rank₂ a) (rank₂ b)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Rank of a binary union.** `rank(a ∪ b) = max (rank a) (rank b)`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_powerset
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_powerset (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : rank₂ (powersetOf₂ x) = Order.succ (rank₂ x)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Rank of a power set.** `rank(𝒫 x) = rank x + 1`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_empty
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_empty : rank₂ (empty₂'.{u}) = 0

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.name: rank₂_sUnion_le
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.sig: theorem rank₂_sUnion_le (x : RGFSet₂.{u}) : rank₂ (sUnion₂ x) ≤ rank₂ x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Cumula.doc: **Rank of a big union.** `rank(⋃ x) ≤ rank x`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: isHF_vonNeumann_nat
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: Each finite von Neumann stage `V_ n` is a hereditarily finite set.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: isHF_of_rank_lt_omega
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem isHF_of_rank_lt_omega {x : ZFSet.{0}} (hx : x.rank < Ordinal.omega0) : RGF.RGFSet.IsHF x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: **Forward:** a set of finite rank is hereditarily finite.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: rank_lt_omega_of_isHF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem rank_lt_omega_of_isHF {x : ZFSet.{0}} (hx : RGF.RGFSet.IsHF x) : x.rank < Ordinal.omega0
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: **Forward:** a set of finite rank is hereditarily finite.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: isHF_iff_rank_lt_omega
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem isHF_iff_rank_lt_omega {x : ZFSet.{0}} : RGF.RGFSet.IsHF x ↔ x.rank < Ordinal.omega0

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: mem_Vomega_iff_isHF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem mem_Vomega_iff_isHF (x : ZFSet.{0}) : x ∈ V_ Ordinal.omega0 ↔ RGF.RGFSet.IsHF x
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: **`V_ω` = HF (stage form).** The ω-th von Neumann stage consists of exactly the hereditarily finite sets.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: mem_Vomega₂_iff
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem mem_Vomega₂_iff (x : RGFSet₂.{0}) : Mem₂ x Vomega₂ ↔ RGF.RGFSet.IsHF (equivZF x)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: A RGF 2.0 set lies in `V_ω` iff it is (under the canonical `RGFSet₂ ≃ ZFSet`) hereditarily finite.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: Vomega₂_equiv_mem
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem Vomega₂_equiv_mem (a b : ℕ) : Mem₂ (Vomega₂_equiv_ackCodes a : RGFSet₂.{0}) (Vomega₂_equiv_ackCodes b : RGFSet₂.{0}) ↔ RGF.RGFSet.Mem a b
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: Under the docking bijection, RGF 2.0 membership inside `V_ω` coincides *exactly* with RGF 1.0 Ackermann membership `∈ₐ`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: omega_not_isHF
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: The set `ω` is not hereditarily finite.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: omega_new_object
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem omega_new_object : (ZFSet.omega : ZFSet.{0}) ∉ V_ Ordinal.omega0 ∧ ∃ o, (ZFSet.omega : ZFSet.{0}) ∈ V_ o
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: `ω` is a genuinely new object: it is absent from `V_ω` yet appears at some higher stage of the hierarchy.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.name: Vomega_is_RGF1_core
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.sig: theorem Vomega_is_RGF1_core : (∀ x : RGFSet₂.{0}, Mem₂ x Vomega₂ ↔ RGF.RGFSet.IsHF (equivZF x)) ∧ (∀ a b : ℕ, Mem₂ (Vomega₂_equiv_ackCodes a : RGFSet₂.{0}) (Vomega₂_equiv_ackCodes b : RGFSet₂.{0}) ↔ RGF.RGFSet.Mem a b) ∧ ((ZFSet.omega : ZFSet.{0}) ∉ V_ Ordinal.omega0 ∧ ∃ o, (ZFSet.omega : ZFSet.{0}) ∈ V_ o)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Heredi.doc: **Capstone.** `V_ω` is *exactly* the RGF 1.0 hereditarily-finite core, and the RGF 2.0 upgrade over it is strict. Concretely: 1. `V_ω` consists exactly of the hereditarily finite sets; 2. there is a membership-preserving bijection between the RGF 1.0 Ackermann codes `ℕ` and the members of `V_ω`; 3. `ω` itself is a genuinely new object — absent from `V_ω`, present higher up.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.name: preBeth_lt_of_lt_ord
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.sig: theorem preBeth_lt_of_lt_ord (hc : c.IsInaccessible) {o : Ordinal} (ho : o < c.ord) : preBeth o < c
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.doc: For a strongly inaccessible `c`, the pre-beth function stays below `c` on all ordinals `< c.ord`. Proved by transfinite induction: `preBeth 0 = 0 < c`, the successor step uses the strong-limit property (`2 ^ κ' < c` for `κ' < c`), and the limit step uses regularity (a supremum of `< c` many cardinals `< c` is `< c`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.name: card_lt_of_rank_lt
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.sig: theorem card_lt_of_rank_lt (hc : c.IsInaccessible) {x : ZFSet.{u}} (hx : x.rank < c.ord) : x.card < c
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.doc: A set of rank `< c.ord` has cardinality `< c` (uses the strong-limit bound via `preBeth`).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.name: rank_image_lt
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.sig: theorem rank_image_lt (hc : c.IsInaccessible) {x : ZFSet.{u}} (f : ZFSet.{u} → ZFSet.{u}) [Definable₁ f] (hx : x.rank < c.ord) (hf : ∀ y ∈ x, (f y).rank < c.ord) : (image f x).rank < c.ord
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.doc: **The Replacement rank bound (heart of the argument).** If `x` has rank `< c.ord` and a class function `f` sends each member of `x` into `V_ c.ord`, then the image `image f x` also has rank `< c.ord`. This is where regularity of `c` is essential: the image is indexed by the `< c` elements of `x`, so its rank supremum stays below `c.ord`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.name: rank_omega_lt
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.doc: **The Replacement rank bound (heart of the argument).** If `x` has rank `< c.ord` and a class function `f` sends each member of `x` into `V_ c.ord`, then the image `image f x` also has rank `< c.ord`. This is where regularity of `c` is essential: the image is indexed by the `< c` elements of `x`, so its rank supremum stays below `c.ord`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.name: inaccessible_imp_ZFCmodel
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.sig: theorem inaccessible_imp_ZFCmodel (h : ∃ c : Cardinal.{u}, c.IsInaccessible) : ∃ M : ZFSet.{u}, IsZFCModel M
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Inacce.doc: **Direction 3.1 — conditional consistency of ZFC.** If there is a strongly inaccessible cardinal, then there is a transitive set that is a model of ZFC (in the semantic sense of `IsZFCModel`). By the soundness theorem this witnesses `Con(ZFC)`: the existence of an inaccessible cardinal is a strictly stronger theory than ZFC. The model is the von Neumann stage `V_ c.ord`. Its closure properties follow from the rank calculus: `c.ord` is a limit ordinal (as `c` is an infinite cardinal), so `V_ c.ord` is closed under Pairing, Union, Power set and Separation; it contains `ω`; and it is closed under Replacement by `rank_image_lt` (the step that genuinely uses inaccessibility).

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.name: vonNeumann_reflection
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.sig: theorem vonNeumann_reflection (F : ZFSet.{u} → ZFSet.{u}) (β : Ordinal.{u}) : ∃ α, β < α ∧ Order.IsSuccLimit α ∧ ∀ x ∈ V_ α, F x ∈ V_ α

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.name: Vhier_reflection_strong
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.sig: theorem Vhier_reflection_strong (f : RGFSet₂.{u} → RGFSet₂.{u}) (β : Ordinal.{u}) : ∃ α, β < α ∧ Order.IsSuccLimit α ∧ ∀ x, Mem₂ x (Vhier α) → Mem₂ (f x) (Vhier α)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.doc: **Montague–Lévy reflection for the RGF 2.0 hierarchy.** For any internal class function `f : RGFSet₂ → RGFSet₂` and any ordinal `β`, there is a limit ordinal `α > β` such that the RGF 2.0 stage `Vhier α` is closed under `f`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.name: Vhier_reflection_pair
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.sig: theorem Vhier_reflection_pair (f g : RGFSet₂.{u} → RGFSet₂.{u}) (β : Ordinal.{u}) : ∃ α, β < α ∧ Order.IsSuccLimit α ∧ (∀ x, Mem₂ x (Vhier α) → Mem₂ (f x) (Vhier α)) ∧ (∀ x, Mem₂ x (Vhier α) → Mem₂ (g x) (Vhier α))
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Reflec.doc: **Two-function (finite-family) reflection.** For any two internal class functions and any ordinal `β`, there is a limit stage `Vhier α`, `α > β`, closed under both — the shape one uses to reflect a formula with several Skolem functions.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfRec_zero
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: @[simp] theorem tfRec_zero {α : Sort*} (z : α) s lim : tfRec z s lim 0 = z

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfRec_succ
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem tfRec_succ {α : Sort*} (z : α) s lim (o : Ordinal.{u}) : tfRec z s lim (Order.succ o) = s o (tfRec z s lim o)

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfRec_limit
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem tfRec_limit {α : Sort*} (z : α) s lim (o : Ordinal.{u}) (ho : Order.IsSuccLimit o) : tfRec z s lim o = lim o ho (fun o' _ => tfRec z s lim o')

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfIterate_natCast
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem tfIterate_natCast {α : Type*} (s : α → α) (z : α) lim (n : ℕ) : tfIterate s z lim (n : Ordinal.{u}) = s^[n] z
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **The RGF 1.0 discrete flow is the finite restriction of the RGF 2.0 transfinite flow.** On the finite ordinals, transfinite iteration coincides with ordinary `Nat.iterate`.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: hartogs
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem hartogs (α : Type u) : ∃ o : Ordinal.{u}, Cardinal.mk α < o.card
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **Hartogs.** For any type there is an ordinal of strictly larger cardinality — the internally generated "next size".

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: hartogs_no_inj
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem hartogs_no_inj (α : Type u) : ∃ o : Ordinal.{u}, ¬ Nonempty (o.ToType ↪ α)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **Hartogs (no-injection form).** For any type there is an ordinal whose underlying type does not inject into it.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: wellOrdering
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem wellOrdering (α : Type u) : ∃ r : α → α → Prop, IsWellOrder α r
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **Well-ordering theorem.** Every type carries a well-order — so transfinite recursion applies to every set of the generative universe.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: choiceFn
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem choiceFn {ι : Type u} (X : ι → Type u) (h : ∀ i, Nonempty (X i)) : Nonempty (Π i, X i)
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **Axiom of Choice** as a non-trivial tool: every family of non-empty types admits a choice function, even over an infinite / transfinite index.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfIterate_omega_eq_lim
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem tfIterate_omega_eq_lim {α : Sort*} (s : α → α) (z : α) (lim : (o : Ordinal.{u}) → Order.IsSuccLimit o → (Π o' < o, α) → α) : tfIterate s z lim Ordinal.omega0.{u} = lim Ordinal.omega0.{u} isSuccLimit_omega0 (fun o' _ => tfIterate s z lim o')
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **The limit stage is queried.** At the first limit ordinal `ω`, transfinite iteration is by definition the value the limit-aggregation rule `lim` computes from the family of all earlier stages. Unlike the finite/`ω`-fragment bridge theorems, this equation *cannot* be stated without `lim`: the limit rule is on the nose.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfIterate_omega_limDependent
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem tfIterate_omega_limDependent : ∃ (lim₁ lim₂ : (o : Ordinal.{u}) → Order.IsSuccLimit o → (Π o' < o, ℕ) → ℕ), tfIterate (id : ℕ → ℕ) 0 lim₁ Ordinal.omega0.{u} ≠ tfIterate (id : ℕ → ℕ) 0 lim₂ Ordinal.omega0.{u}
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **Negative test: the value at `ω` depends on the limit rule.** Take the constant step `s = id` on `ℕ` with seed `z = 0`. The rule that always returns `0` and the rule that always returns `1` produce different values of the transfinite flow at `ω` (`0 ≠ 1`). Hence the limit rule genuinely carries the result at limit stages — the "transfinite" part is not a free parameter that the theorems ignore.

RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.name: tfIterate_omega_agg
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.sig: theorem tfIterate_omega_agg : tfIterate (id : ℕ → ℕ) 5 (fun _ h prev => prev 0 (Ordinal.bot_eq_zero ▸ h.bot_lt)) Ordinal.omega0.{u} = 5
RGF/Math/SetTheory/RGF2/Hierarchy/Transf.doc: **Positive aggregation instance.** With the step `s = id` and seed `z = 5` on `ℕ`, using the limit rule that reads off the stage at `0` (`prev 0 …`), the value at `ω` is exactly `5` — but obtained *through* `lim`, i.e. via the genuine limit computation, not the finite reduction. This shows a real aggregation flowing across the limit stage.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: dynEquiv_fixEquiv_refl
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.sig: theorem dynEquiv_fixEquiv_refl (X : GenSys) : dynEquiv_fixEquiv (Iso.refl X) = Equiv.refl (FixSet X)
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: **Dynamical univalence transcription.** An isomorphism of generative systems (a dynamical equivalence, i.e. an equivalence commuting with the dynamics) induces an equivalence of their fixed-point (attractor) types. This is the dynamical form of "equivalent systems are transportable": the attractor type is a univalent invariant of the system up to dynamical equivalence.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: dynEquiv_fixEquiv_trans
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.sig: theorem dynEquiv_fixEquiv_trans {X Y Z : GenSys} (e : X ≅ Y) (f : Y ≅ Z) : dynEquiv_fixEquiv (e ≪≫ f) = (dynEquiv_fixEquiv e).trans (dynEquiv_fixEquiv f)
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: **Dynamical univalence transcription.** An isomorphism of generative systems (a dynamical equivalence, i.e. an equivalence commuting with the dynamics) induces an equivalence of their fixed-point (attractor) types. This is the dynamical form of "equivalent systems are transportable": the attractor type is a univalent invariant of the system up to dynamical equivalence.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: membraneLocked_perm_subsingleton
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.sig: theorem membraneLocked_perm_subsingleton (X : GenSys) (h : IsContractible (FixSet X)) : Subsingleton (Equiv.Perm (FixSet X))
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: The projection of a self-equivalence (automorphism) of a system onto a permutation of its attractor type.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: membraneLocked_autToPerm_trivial
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.sig: theorem membraneLocked_autToPerm_trivial (X : GenSys) (h : IsContractible (FixSet X)) (e : Aut X) : autToPerm X e = 1
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: The projection of a self-equivalence (automorphism) of a system onto a permutation of its attractor type.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: autZ5_card
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: The projection of a self-equivalence (automorphism) of a system onto a permutation of its attractor type.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: symm5_card
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: The projection of a self-equivalence (automorphism) of a system onto a permutation of its attractor type.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.name: autZ5_ne_symm5
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTT.lean.doc: The projection of a self-equivalence (automorphism) of a system onto a permutation of its attractor type.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: flow_locked_simplyConnected
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem flow_locked_simplyConnected (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [ContractibleSpace X] : SimplyConnectedSpace X
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: A locked flow with contractible phase space is simply connected: all trajectory loops contract.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: flow_locked_pi1_trivial
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem flow_locked_pi1_trivial (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [ContractibleSpace X] (x : X) : Subsingleton (Path.Homotopic.Quotient x x)
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: A locked flow with contractible phase space has trivial fundamental group at every base point (every loop is homotopic to the constant loop).

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: rot_iterate
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem rot_iterate (n : ℕ) (k : ℕ) (x : ZMod n) : (rotStep n)^[k] x = x + (k : ZMod n)
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: **Monodromy of the limit cycle.** Iterating the generator `k` times adds `k`.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: rot_step_ne_id
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem rot_step_ne_id (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : rotStep n ≠ id
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: The generator is not the identity when `n ≥ 2` (non-trivial winding).

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: rot_period
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: The generator has period exactly `n`: `stepⁿ = id`.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: rotStep_no_fixed
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem rotStep_no_fixed (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (x : ZMod n) : rotStep n x ≠ x
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: The generator of the rotation system has no fixed point for `n ≥ 2`.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: rot_not_locked
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem rot_not_locked (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ¬ IsMembraneLocked (rotationSys n)
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: The rotation system has no fixed point for `n ≥ 2`, hence is **not** membrane-locked.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: limitCycle_nontrivial_winding
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem limitCycle_nontrivial_winding (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : rotStep n ≠ id ∧ (rotStep n)^[n] = id
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: **Non-trivial winding of the limit cycle.** The generator is not the identity yet has period `n` (`π₁ ≅ ℤ/n ≠ 0`).

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: order_iff_contractible
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem order_iff_contractible (X : GenSys) : IsMembraneLocked X ↔ IsContractible (FixSet X)
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: **Order ⇔ contractibility.** Membrane locking is equivalent to contractibility of the attractor (fixed-point) type.

RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.name: chaos_not_contractible
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.sig: theorem chaos_not_contractible (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ¬ IsContractible (FixSet (rotationSys n))
RGF/Math/Category/DynamicalHoTTFlows.lea.doc: **Chaos ⇒ non-contractible attractor.** The limit-cycle attractor type is not contractible (non-trivial fundamental group).

RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.name: permToEnd_one
RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.sig: theorem permToEnd_one (X : RGFObject) : permToEndomorphism X 1 = 𝟙 X

RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.name: permToEnd_mul
RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.sig: theorem permToEnd_mul (X : RGFObject) (σ τ : Perm (Fin X.n)) : permToEndomorphism X σ ≫ permToEndomorphism X τ = permToEndomorphism X (τ * σ)
RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.doc: permToEndomorphism preserves multiplication (reversing order: σ ∘ τ ↦ τ * σ).

RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.name: rgfObject_is_equivariant
RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.doc: The equivariance condition of an RGF object holds automatically (since EquivariantSystem already includes it).

RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.name: conjugate_id
RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.sig: theorem conjugate_id {X Y : RGFObject} (φ : InvertibleRGFMorphism X Y) : conjugateByMorphism φ (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 Y

RGF/Math/Category/Equivariant_Functor.le.name: conjugate_comp

RGF/Math/Category/FixedPoint_Subcategory.name: id_comp

RGF/Math/Category/FixedPoint_Subcategory.name: comp_id
RGF/Math/Category/FixedPoint_Subcategory.sig: theorem comp_id {G H : GraphObject} (f : GraphMorphism G H) : comp f (id H) = f

RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.name: forget_map_id
RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.doc: The forgetful functor preserves the identity morphism.

RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.name: forget_map_comp
RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.sig: theorem forget_map_comp {X Y Z : RGFObject} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : RGF_forget.map (f ≫ g) = g.f ∘ f.f

RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.name: freeRGF_vertexCount
RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.doc: The vertex count of the free construction.

RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.name: freeRGF_step_id
RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.sig: theorem freeRGF_step_id (n : ℕ) (s : RGFState n) : (freeRGF n).sys.step s = s
RGF/Math/Category/ForgetfulFunctor.lean.doc: The free construction uses trivial dynamics.

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.name: GenHom.id_f
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.sig: @[simp] theorem GenHom.id_f (X : GenSys) : (𝟙 X : GenHom X X).f = _root_.id

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.name: GenHom.comp_f
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.sig: @[simp] theorem GenHom.comp_f {X Y Z : GenSys} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : (f ≫ g).f = g.f ∘ f.f

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.name: fix_universal
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.sig: theorem fix_universal (X : GenSys) {Z : Type u} (g : Z → X.carrier) (hg : ∀ z, X.step (g z) = g z) : ∃! g' : Z → FixSet X, (fun z => (g' z).1) = g
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.doc: **The fixed-point set is the equalizer of `step` and `id`.** Any map from an arbitrary type `Z` that lands in the locked states factors uniquely through the inclusion `FixSet X ↪ X.carrier`. This is the limit universal property.

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.name: membraneLocked_iff_fix_contractible
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.sig: theorem membraneLocked_iff_fix_contractible (X : GenSys) : IsMembraneLocked X ↔ IsContractible (FixSet X)
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.doc: **Membrane locking is contractibility of the fixed-point type.**

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.name: IsContractible.of_equiv
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.sig: theorem IsContractible.of_equiv {S T : Type u} (e : S ≃ T) (h : IsContractible S) : IsContractible T

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.name: membraneLocked_iff_globalElements_contractible
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.sig: theorem membraneLocked_iff_globalElements_contractible (X : GenSys) : IsMembraneLocked X ↔ IsContractible (trivialSys ⟶ X)
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeDynamicalCat.doc: **Membrane locking is contractibility of the type of global elements.** A system is membrane-locked iff the type of morphisms from the terminal object (its global elements) is contractible.

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.name: rapid_iff_modulus_id
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.sig: theorem rapid_iff_modulus_id (a : GenReal) : Rapid a ↔ IsModulus a id

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.name: isCau_of_tendsto
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.sig: theorem isCau_of_tendsto (g : ℕ → ℚ) (L : ℝ) (h : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ((g n : ℚ) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds L)) : IsCauSeq abs g

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.name: value_dist_le
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.sig: theorem value_dist_le (a : GenReal) (h : Rapid a) (n : ℕ) : |(a.approx n : ℝ) - value a| ≤ 1 / (n + 1)
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.doc: The value of a rapid process is within `1/(n+1)` of every term.

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.name: exists_rapid_value
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.sig: theorem exists_rapid_value (x : ℝ) : ∃ a : GenReal, Rapid a ∧ value a = x
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.doc: Every real number is the value of a rapid generative process.

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.name: rapid_distinguishes_equal_value
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.sig: theorem rapid_distinguishes_equal_value : ∃ a b : GenReal, value a = value b ∧ Rapid a ∧ ¬ Rapid b
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.doc: There exist two processes with the *same value* (here `0`), one rapid and one not: rapidity is genuine generative data not visible through `value`.

RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.name: rapid_pointwise_rigid
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.sig: theorem rapid_pointwise_rigid (a b : GenReal) (ha : Rapid a) (hb : Rapid b) (hval : value a = value b) (n : ℕ) : |(a.approx n : ℝ) - (b.approx n : ℝ)| ≤ 3 / (n + 1)
RGF/Math/Category/GenerativeRefinement.l.doc: Two rapid processes for the same value are pinned within `3/(n+1)` at every index.

RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.name: id_comp
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.sig: theorem id_comp {X Y : RGFObject} (f : RGFMorphism X Y) : comp (id X) f = f

RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.name: comp_id
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.sig: theorem comp_id {X Y : RGFObject} (f : RGFMorphism X Y) : comp f (id Y) = f

RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.name: comp_assoc
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.sig: theorem comp_assoc {W X Y Z : RGFObject} (f : RGFMorphism W X) (g : RGFMorphism X Y) (h : RGFMorphism Y Z) : comp (comp f g) h = comp f (comp g h)

RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.name: id_f
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.sig: theorem id_f (X : RGFObject) : (𝟙 X : RGFMorphism X X).f = _root_.id
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.doc: The identity morphism is the identity function.

RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.name: comp_f
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.sig: theorem comp_f {X Y Z : RGFObject} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : (f ≫ g).f = g.f ∘ f.f
RGF/Math/Category/RGF_Category.lean.doc: The composite morphism is function composition.

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: l1Dist_nonneg
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem l1Dist_nonneg (μ ν : RGFRuleLayer α) : 0 ≤ l1Dist μ ν

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: l1Dist_symm
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem l1Dist_symm (μ ν : RGFRuleLayer α) : l1Dist μ ν = l1Dist ν μ

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: l1Dist_triangle
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem l1Dist_triangle (μ ν ρ : RGFRuleLayer α) : l1Dist μ ρ ≤ l1Dist μ ν + l1Dist ν ρ

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: l1Dist_eq_zero_of_eq
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem l1Dist_eq_zero_of_eq (μ ν : RGFRuleLayer α) (h : μ.weight = ν.weight) : l1Dist μ ν = 0

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: l1Dist_le_two
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem l1Dist_le_two (μ ν : RGFRuleLayer α) : l1Dist μ ν ≤ 2

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: RGFContraction.iterate_distance_bound
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem RGFContraction.iterate_distance_bound (sys : RGFContraction α) (μ ν : RGFRuleLayer α) (n : ℕ) : l1Dist (sys.iterate μ n) (sys.iterate ν n) ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist μ ν

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: RGFContraction.fixedPoint_unique_l1
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem RGFContraction.fixedPoint_unique_l1 (sys : RGFContraction α) (z₁ z₂ : RGFRuleLayer α) (h₁ : sys.IsFixedPoint z₁) (h₂ : sys.IsFixedPoint z₂) : l1Dist z₁ z₂ = 0

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: RGFContraction.iterate_fixedPoint
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem RGFContraction.iterate_fixedPoint (sys : RGFContraction α) (zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) : ∀ n, sys.iterate zstar n = zstar
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.doc: The fixed point is invariant under iteration.

RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.name: RGFContraction.convergence_rate
RGF/Math/Real/BanachContraction.lean.sig: theorem RGFContraction.convergence_rate (sys : RGFContraction α) (z zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (n : ℕ) : l1Dist (sys.iterate z n) zstar ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z zstar

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: cauchyEquiv_refl
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem cauchyEquiv_refl (a : CauchyRatSeq) : CauchyEquiv a a

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: cauchyEquiv_symm
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem cauchyEquiv_symm {a b : CauchyRatSeq} (h : CauchyEquiv a b) : CauchyEquiv b a

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: cauchyEquiv_trans
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem cauchyEquiv_trans {a b c : CauchyRatSeq} (hab : CauchyEquiv a b) (hbc : CauchyEquiv b c) : CauchyEquiv a c

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: sum_isCauchy
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem sum_isCauchy (a b : CauchyRatSeq) : IsCauchyRat (fun n => a.seq n + b.seq n)

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: add_respects_equiv
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem add_respects_equiv {a₁ a₂ b₁ b₂ : CauchyRatSeq} (ha : CauchyEquiv a₁ a₂) (hb : CauchyEquiv b₁ b₂) : CauchyEquiv (addSeq a₁ b₁) (addSeq a₂ b₂)

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: cauchy_bounded
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem cauchy_bounded (a : CauchyRatSeq) : ∃ M : ℚ, 0 < M ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, |a.seq n| < M
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.doc: A Cauchy real = an equivalence class of Cauchy sequences.

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: cauchy_eventually_close
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem cauchy_eventually_close (a : CauchyRatSeq) (ε : ℚ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m n : ℕ, N ≤ m → N ≤ n → |a.seq m - a.seq n| < ε
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.doc: The Cauchy condition implies asymptotic locking.

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: const_is_fixpoint
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem const_is_fixpoint (q : ℚ) : CauchyEquiv (ofRat q) (ofRat q)
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.doc: A constant sequence is equivalent to itself (an RGF fixed point).

RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.name: converge_same_implies_equiv
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.sig: theorem converge_same_implies_equiv (a b : CauchyRatSeq) (q : ℚ) (ha : ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → |a.seq n - q| < ε) (hb : ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → |b.seq n - q| < ε) : CauchyEquiv a b
RGF/Math/Real/CauchySequence.lean.doc: Two sequences converging to the same rational are equivalent.

RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.name: rgf_real_contraction_unique
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.sig: theorem rgf_real_contraction_unique (f : ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (hc1 : c < 1) (hcontr : ∀ x y, |f x - f y| ≤ c * |x - y|) {x y : ℝ} (hx : f x = x) (hy : f y = y) : x = y
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.doc: **General real contraction principle.** Any self-map `f : ℝ → ℝ` that is a `c`-Lipschitz contraction (`c < 1`) has at most one fixed point. This is the one-line abstraction that subsumes RCD's scalar `Paper0.contraction_unique_fixed`.

RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.name: rcd_contraction_unique_fixed_via_general
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.sig: theorem rcd_contraction_unique_fixed_via_general (α x : ℝ) (hα : |α| < 1) (hx : α * x = x) : x = 0
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.doc: **RCD scalar core as an instance (the bridge).** RCD's `Paper0.contraction_unique_fixed` (`|α| < 1`, `α·x = x ⟹ x = 0`) is recovered from the general real contraction principle applied to the linear map `t ↦ α·t`, whose obvious fixed point is `0`.

RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.name: rcd_p5_fixed_point_unique
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.sig: theorem rcd_p5_fixed_point_unique {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (sys : RGFContraction α) (z₁ z₂ : RGFRuleLayer α) (h₁ : sys.IsFixedPoint z₁) (h₂ : sys.IsFixedPoint z₂) : l1Dist z₁ z₂ = 0
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.doc: **Upgraded P5 uniqueness.** The unique-stationary-state claim that RCD only establishes in the scalar case holds for an arbitrary `L¹` contraction on the rule layer: any two fixed points coincide (`l1Dist = 0`).

RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.name: rcd_p5_geometric_convergence
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.sig: theorem rcd_p5_geometric_convergence {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (sys : RGFContraction α) (z zstar : RGFRuleLayer α) (hstar : sys.IsFixedPoint zstar) (n : ℕ) : l1Dist (sys.iterate z n) zstar ≤ sys.contractCoeff ^ n * l1Dist z zstar
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.doc: **Upgraded P5 quantitative convergence.** Iterating an arbitrary `L¹` contraction converges to its fixed point geometrically (exponential decay of the `L¹` distance), upgrading RCD's scalar geometric-series picture.

RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.name: rcd_stationary_variance_general
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.sig: theorem rcd_stationary_variance_general (r : ℝ) (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr1 : r < 1) : (∑' k : ℕ, r ^ k) = 1 / (1 - r)
RGF/Math/Real/Contraction.lean.doc: **Stationary variance (shared geometric-series core).** Both RCD scalar stationary-variance lemmas (`Paper0.stationary_variance` and `Paper2.mode_stationary_variance`) are the single identity `Σ (r)ᵏ = 1/(1-r)` for `0 ≤ r < 1`; we record the general statement that underlies both.

RGF/Math/Real/DedekindCut.lean.name: DedekindCut.ext
RGF/Math/Real/DedekindCut.lean.sig: theorem DedekindCut.ext {α β : DedekindCut} (h : α.carrier = β.carrier) : α = β

RGF/Math/Real/DedekindCut.lean.sig: theorem le_antisymm' {α β : DedekindCut} (h₁ : α ≤ β) (h₂ : β ≤ α) : α = β

RGF/Math/Real/DedekindCut.lean.sig: theorem add_comm' (α β : DedekindCut) : α + β = β + α

RGF/Math/Real/DedekindCut.lean.name: le_total'

RGF/Math/Real/GenReal.lean.sig: theorem GenReal.equiv_trans {a b c : GenReal} (hab : a.Equiv b) (hbc : b.Equiv c) : a.Equiv c

RGF/Math/Real/GenReal.lean.sig: theorem GenReal.bounded (a : GenReal) : ∃ M : ℚ, 0 < M ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, |a.approx n| < M

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.name: ringEquivReal_apply
RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: @[simp] theorem ringEquivReal_apply (a : RGFReal') : ringEquivReal a = toReal a

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.name: complete
RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: theorem complete (s : ℕ → RGFReal') (h : IsCauchySeqReal s) : ∃ L : RGFReal', ∀ k : RGFNat, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ i : ℕ, N ≤ i → |toReal (s i - L)| ≤ 1 / ((k.toNat : ℚ) + 1)

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.name: add_assoc'
RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: theorem add_assoc' (a b c : RGFReal') : a + b + c = a + (b + c)

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.name: mul_assoc'
RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: theorem mul_assoc' (a b c : RGFReal') : a * b * c = a * (b * c)

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.name: mul_comm'
RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: theorem mul_comm' (a b : RGFReal') : a * b = b * a

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: theorem left_distrib' (a b c : RGFReal') : a * (b + c) = a * b + a * c

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: @[simp] theorem toReal_inv (a : RGFReal') : toReal (inv a) = (toReal a)⁻¹

RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.name: mul_inv_cancel'
RGF/Math/Real/RGFField.lean.sig: theorem mul_inv_cancel' (a : RGFReal') (ha : a ≠ 0) : a * inv a = 1

RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.sig: theorem testBit_self (n : ℕ) : Nat.testBit n n = false
RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.doc: The `n`-th binary digit of `n` is always `0` (since `n < 2 ^ n`).

RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.name: mem_succ

RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.name: self_mem_succ
RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.sig: theorem self_mem_succ (n : ℕ) : Mem n (succ n)
RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.doc: `n` is a member of its own successor.

RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.name: rgf_bounded_infinity

RGF/Math/Real/RGFInfinity.lean.doc: **Resolution of Infinity for the RGF reals.** (i) No real coding an HF set is inductive: the Infinity axiom, read as a statement about a single set, fails internally (`no_inductive_set`). (ii) Yet the generation process realizes the von Neumann naturals `RNat` as an *actual infinite* family of RGF reals, inductive as a class: `RNat 0` is empty and `RNat (k+1)` is the successor of `RNat k`. Together these say precisely that the RGF reals model ZF − Infinity (the internal HF universe) together with the bounded / potential infinity principle supplied by the generation process.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: forwardCount_odd

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.doc: Theorem 2.1 (the forward direction count is odd): for all `d ≥ 1`, `forwardCount d` is always odd.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: order_lock

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.doc: Theorem 2.2 (order lock): `SelfConsistent d ∧ d ≠ 0 ⟹ forwardCount d = 5`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: depth_lock

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.doc: Theorem 2.3 (depth lock): the recursion depth `L = n₂(forwardCount d) = 2`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: coord_lock
RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.sig: theorem coord_lock {d : ℕ} (h : SelfConsistent d) (h0 : d ≠ 0) : coord d = 6
RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.doc: Theorem 3.1 (coordination number): `SelfConsistent d ∧ d ≠ 0 ⟹ coord d = 6`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: master_lock
RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.sig: theorem master_lock {d : ℕ} (h : SelfConsistent d) (h0 : d ≠ 0) : (num2DIrreps (forwardCount d), forwardCount d, d, coord d) = (2, 5, 3, 6)

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: axiomG_is_selfConsistent

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.doc: Theorem 4.2 (self-consistency implies Axiom M): from `SelfConsistent`, the order `5` is the minimal emergent order.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: intertwine
RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.sig: theorem intertwine {R E : Type*} (generate : R → E) (modify : E → R) (n : ℕ) : generate ∘ (step generate modify)^[n] = (costep generate modify)^[n] ∘ generate
RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.doc: Theorem 5.1 (semiconjugacy / intertwining law): `generate ∘ stepⁿ = costepⁿ ∘ generate`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: locking_order_odd

RGF/Physics/Emergence/CompleteDerivation.name: locking_num2DIrreps

RGF/Physics/Emergence/ComplexityEmergenc.name: solvable_is_shallow

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem forsEnergyGen_three (s : ℝ) : forsEnergyGen 3 s = forsEnergy s

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: forsEnergy_nonneg
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem forsEnergy_nonneg (s : ℝ) : 0 ≤ forsEnergy s

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: forsEnergy_eq_zero_iff
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem forsEnergy_eq_zero_iff (s : ℝ) : forsEnergy s = 0 ↔ s = 2

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: omega_scaling

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: kinetic_integral
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem kinetic_integral : (∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1, omega t) = 2 / 7

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem omega_continuous : Continuous omega

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: omega_monotoneOn

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.doc: The discrete kinetic Riemann sum `K_n = (1/n) ∑_{j=1}^{n} ω(j/n)`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: Kdiscr_sub_bounds
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem Kdiscr_sub_bounds (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : 0 ≤ Kdiscr n - 2 / 7 ∧ Kdiscr n - 2 / 7 ≤ 1 / n
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.doc: The discrete kinetic Riemann sum `K_n = (1/n) ∑_{j=1}^{n} ω(j/n)`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: Kdiscr_tendsto
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem Kdiscr_tendsto : Tendsto Kdiscr atTop (nhds (2 / 7))
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.doc: The discrete kinetic Riemann sum `K_n = (1/n) ∑_{j=1}^{n} ω(j/n)`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.name: fors_energy_first_principles
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.sig: theorem fors_energy_first_principles : -- Step 0: five-pole structure (∀ j : Fin 5, (forsPole j) ^ 5 = -1) ∧ -- Step 1: the packing radius tends to zero (Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => fillRad 3 ε) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0)) ∧ -- Step 2: discrete energy converges + the vacuum state is the unique minimum (∀ a : ℝ, 0 ≤ a → Tendsto (fun n => Ediscr a n) atTop (nhds (Econt a))) ∧ Econt 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → 0 < Econt a) ∧ -- Step 3: joint dimension locking (∀ d R : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → 1 ≤ R → 2 * d - 1 = 5 → d + 2 * R = 5 → d = 3 ∧ R = 1 ∧ d - R = 2) ∧ -- Step 5: the kernel determines the energy (forsEnergy 2 = 0 ∧ (∀ s : ℝ, 0 ≤ forsEnergy s) ∧ (∀ s : ℝ, forsEnergy s = 0 ↔ s = 2)) ∧ -- Step 6: kinetic integral ((∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1, omega t) = 2 / 7)
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FORSEnergyFirstPri.doc: The discrete kinetic Riemann sum `K_n = (1/n) ∑_{j=1}^{n} ω(j/n)`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: solvable_of_le_four
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.sig: theorem solvable_of_le_four {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ 4) : IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin k))
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: Theorem 1 (solvability bound, lower half): for `k ≤ 4`, `S_k` is solvable. Together with `S_5` unsolvable this is the group-theoretic root of Abel–Ruffini.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: emergentOrder_iff_five_le
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.sig: theorem emergentOrder_iff_five_le {k : ℕ} : EmergentOrder k ↔ 5 ≤ k
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: `EmergentOrder k ↔ 5 ≤ k`: emergence (non-solvability of `S_k`) holds exactly from order `5` onwards.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: minimalEmergent_iff_five
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.sig: theorem minimalEmergent_iff_five {k : ℕ} : MinimalEmergent k ↔ k = 5
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: Theorem 2 (the minimal genuine emergent order is 5): the unique minimal emergent order is `5`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: axiom_M
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: Axiom M as a *theorem*: there exists a unique minimal emergent order.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: cp_iff_three
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.sig: theorem cp_iff_three {d : ℕ} : CP d ↔ d = 3
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: Theorem 5 (the spatial dimension is locked to 3): the cross-product / "rotation = vector" equation `d(d-1)/2 = d` has the unique nontrivial solution `d = 3`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: first_principle_forces_k_five_d_three
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.sig: theorem first_principle_forces_k_five_d_three {k d : ℕ} (hk : MinimalEmergent k) (hd : CP d) : k = 5 ∧ d = 3 ∧ 2 * d = 6 ∧ (k - 1) / 2 = 2
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: **Core theorem (`first_principle_forces_k_five_d_three`).** From the two first principles — `MinimalEmergent k` (Axiom M) and `CP d` (Axiom G) — the entire locked tuple is forced: * mode order `k = 5`, * spatial dimension `d = 3`, * coordination number `z = 2 d = 6` (simple-cubic nearest neighbours), * recursion depth `L = (k-1)/2 = 2` (number of 2D rotation planes). No target numeral is assumed anywhere: each appears only as a *conclusion*.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.name: meta_resolution
RGF/Physics/Emergence/FirstPrinciples.le.doc: **Honest meta-resolution (`meta_resolution`).** The bare emergence predicate does *not* single out a unique value: e.g. both `5` and `7` are emergent (`S_5` and `S_7` are unsolvable) and `5 ≠ 7`. Uniqueness of `5` arises *only* via the minimality extremal principle (Axiom M / `minimalEmergent_iff_five`). Thus the foundation contracts to an extremal principle but cannot disappear entirely — this is stated transparently rather than hidden.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.name: bulk_instability
RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.sig: theorem bulk_instability (φ : Field) (h : IsStableField φ) (hbulk : ∀ (x : SpacePoint) (t : Time), φ x t > 0) : False
RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.doc: **3-dimensional bulk instability theorem**: a bulk field occupying the whole space and nonzero everywhere cannot be a stable solution. Proof: the bulk field's support is the whole space, of dimension 3, so its energy is `(3−2)² = 1 > 0`; but a stable solution must have energy at the global minimum 0 (`stable_field_energy_eq_zero`), a contradiction.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.name: line_annihilation
RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.sig: theorem line_annihilation (φ : Field) (h : IsStableField φ) (hline : suppDim φ ≤ 1) : False
RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.doc: **1-dimensional line annihilation theorem**: a line-like field with support dimension ≤ 1 cannot be a stable solution. Proof: a stable solution has support dimension exactly 2 (`stable_field_suppDim_eq_two`), contradicting dimension ≤ 1. Note: the original statement wrote the line phase as an indicator function `φ x t = if x = f t then 1 else 0`, but that form does not constrain the dimension of the image of `f`. The faithful "line phase" condition is exactly "support dimension ≤ 1" (concentrated on a 1-dimensional or lower subset), which is the hypothesis `hline` below.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.name: membrane_unique_stable
RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.sig: theorem membrane_unique_stable : ∃ (φ : Field), IsStableField φ ∧ (∃ (M : Set SpacePoint), (∀ x ∈ M, ∀ t, φ x t ≠ 0) ∧ suppDim φ = 2)
RGF/Physics/Emergence/GeometricReduction.doc: **2-dimensional membrane unique-stable-phase theorem**: there exists a stable solution whose support dimension is exactly 2, and which is nonzero everywhere on a 2-dimensional subset `M` (the plane `{x | x₂ = 0}`). Take the locked membrane field `membraneField` constructed in `Setup.lean`: it takes the value `1/2` on the plane `{x₂ = 0}`, its support is exactly that 2-dimensional plane (`suppDim = 2`), and its energy is the global minimum 0, hence it is stable.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer0_fixed_point_unique
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer0_fixed_point_unique {R E : Type} (sys : ContractingDualLayer R E) (r₁ r₂ : R) (h₁ : sys.toAbstractDualLayer.FixedPoint r₁) (h₂ : sys.toAbstractDualLayer.FixedPoint r₂) : r₁ = r₂
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 0.** Restatement: in a contracting dual-layer system the stable structure (fixed point of `step = modify ∘ generate`) is unique.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer1_charpoly_form
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer1_charpoly_form (M : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) (hM : Mᵀ = -M) : ∃ a b : ℝ, M.charpoly = Polynomial.X ^ 5 + Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ 3 + Polynomial.C b * Polynomial.X
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 1 (version D upper bound).** The antisymmetric `5×5` linearised generator has characteristic polynomial of the depth-2 form `X⁵ + a X³ + b X` (the even-degree coefficients vanish), so its positive eigenfrequencies solve a biquadratic and therefore number at most two.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer1_n2_upper
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer1_n2_upper (a b : ℝ) (S : Finset ℝ) (hS : ∀ ω ∈ S, 0 < ω ∧ ω ^ 4 - a * ω ^ 2 + b = 0) : S.card ≤ 2
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 1, clean arithmetic core.** Any finite set of positive frequencies obeying a biquadratic relation `ω⁴ − a ω² + b = 0` has at most two elements.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer2_chiral_axis
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer2_chiral_axis {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hM : Mᵀ = -M) (hn : Odd n) : M.det = 0
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 2 (L3).** An odd-dimensional real antisymmetric generator has a zero eigenvalue (`det = 0`), i.e. a stable real chiral axis exists precisely because the dimension is odd.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer4_frequency_count_two
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer4_frequency_count_two (n₂ : ℕ) (hlow : 2 ≤ n₂) (hup : n₂ ≤ 2) : n₂ = 2
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layers 3–4 (L2).** The genuine dual-layer lower bound `n₂ ≥ 2` and the depth-2 upper bound `n₂ ≤ 2` squeeze the frequency count to exactly two.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer5_k_eq_five
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer5_k_eq_five (k : ℕ) (hodd : Odd k) (hn2 : num2DIrreps k = 2) : k = 5
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 5.** Combining `L2` (`n₂ = 2`) with `L3` (`k` odd) and the dihedral two-dimensional irrep count `n₂(k) = (k−1)/2` forces `k = 5`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer5_unique
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer5_unique : ∃! k : ℕ, LockingMembraneConditions k
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 5, uniqueness.** `k = 5` is the unique solution of the locking-membrane conditions (`n₂ = 2` and odd).

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer8_rot_iff
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer8_rot_iff (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : rotGen d = d ↔ d = 3
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 8.** The intrinsic rotation-vector criterion: for any positive dimension, `rotGen d = d` iff `d = 3`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer7_gap
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer7_gap : ∃ L₁ L₂ : LatticeCandidate, forwardCount L₁ = 5 ∧ forwardCount L₂ = 5 ∧ L₁.dim ≠ L₂.dim
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 7.** Honest exposure of the gap: the locking count `= 5` alone does not fix the dimension (a 2D and a 3D candidate both give 5 forward channels).

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer9_dim_three
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer9_dim_three (L : LatticeCandidate) (hdim : 0 < L.dim) (hlock : forwardCount L = 5) (hrot : rotGen L.dim = L.dim) : L.dim = 3
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 9.** The double-criterion intersection: for any candidate lattice, `forwardCount = 5` together with `rotGen dim = dim` forces `dim = 3`.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer10_unique_cubic
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer10_unique_cubic : ∀ L ∈ candidates, (forwardCount L = 5 ∧ rotGen L.dim = L.dim) ↔ L = simpleCubic
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 10.** Among the standard competing lattices the simple-cubic lattice is the unique one passing both criteria.

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer9_ortho_axes
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.sig: theorem layer9_ortho_axes {d : ℕ} (R : OrthoStepRule d) (hd : 0 < d) : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range R.e) = ⊤ ∧ (Finset.univ.image (OrthoStepRule.signedAxis R)).card = 2 * d
RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.doc: **Layer 9 (orthogonal step rule).** The `d` orthonormal generation axes span the whole space, and the signed neighbour directions `{±eᵢ}` number exactly `2d` — i.e. the coordination number is `z = 2d`, derived (not assumed).

RGF/Physics/Emergence/IntegratedDerivati.name: layer10_ortho_dim_three
